activities.name: Hike to Mount Le Conte on Alum Cave Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Hike 10 miles (16.1 km) roundtrip on Alum Cave Trail as it climbs steadily through dense forest to Alum Cave Bluffs and on to the summit of Mount LeConte. This popular but strenuous hike includes stairs, bridges, and some steep and rocky sections of trail.

activities.name: Enjoy a 360-Degree View at Little Baldy Dome
activities.basis: estimated from duration (2-3 Hours)
activities.description: Hike on a lesser-known trail in Sequoia National Park. The Little Baldy trail takes you through a mixed-conifer forest to the top of a granite dome. Once there, you can take in a 360-degree panoramic view.

activities.name: Mascall Formation Overlook
activities.basis: estimated from duration (5-15 Minutes)
activities.description: This 430 ft (131 m) roundtrip trail leads to a scenic view of the Mascall Formation, Picture Gorge, and John Day Valley.

activities.name: Ebey's Reserve - Fort Casey & Admiralty Head Lighthouse
activities.description: A visit to Fort Casey State Park offers the visitor a glimpse into early military life as well as spectacular views of Mount Rainier and the Olympic Mountains. Camping is also available year-round. Admiralty Lighthouse is a favorite stop when visiting the park and Ebey's Reserve.

activities.name: Become a Yosemite Junior Ranger
activities.description: Kids can become a Yosemite Junior Ranger by taking a self-guided handbook with them as they travel around the park and complete the activities that are the best fit for them. The Yosemite Junior Ranger handbook is available for free at visitor centers. When you are done, share your booklet with a park ranger at any…

activities.name: Bike the Tour Road
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-3 Hours)
activities.description: While Saratoga National Historical Park is primarily known for its history, we’re also a very popular spot for cycling; no matter your level of expertise!

activities.name: Charlestown Navy Yard: Tour USS CASSIN YOUNG (DD 793)
activities.description: Explore above and below the main deck of USS CASSIN YOUNG (DD 793), a Fletcher-class Destroyer that served in the Second World War and throughout the 1950s.

activities.name: Cane River Creole Junior Ranger
activities.description: The Cane River Creole Junior Ranger program includes different levels of activities for children of all ages. Complete 6 activities, as you learn about the history of Oakland and Magnolia Plantations, to earn a Cane River Creole Junior Ranger badge.

activities.name: Multi-Park Loop
activities.place: APPA, CAJO, CHOH, GWMP, NAMA, POHE, ROCR, STSP, THIS, WARO, WWII
activities.description: Park your car and stretch your legs! Visit four different National Parks in Washington, DC and begin logging miles on seven different National Historic or National Scenic trails!

activities.name: Hike Giant Slide Loop
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: A challenging hike up a rugged ravine to excellent views atop Mount Desert Island's second highest peak, Sargent Mountain, and other summits.

activities.name: Hike Trails at the Base of Capulin Volcano
activities.basis: estimated from duration (10-180 Minutes)
activities.description: The trails at the base of Capulin Volcano are less traveled and quieter than the ones on the top and offer a different view of the volcanic geology here.

activities.name: The General Sherman Tree
activities.description: The General Sherman Tree is a must-see while visiting the Giant Forest. It is the largest tree in the world by volume.

activities.name: Visit Grand Portage State Park
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-4 Hours)
activities.description: Grand Portage State Park is the location of the highest waterfall in Minnesota. The waterfalls and rapids along this section of the Pigeon River caused the significance of the Grand Portage Trail bypass for canoe traffic. The wheelchair appropriate mile-long (round trip) trail is available year round.

activities.name: Explore the Visitor Center Museum
activities.description: The park museum is found within the Visitor Center and contains exhibits focused on scales of time: Geological, Ecological, Human, and with special exhibits on the Night Sky and Air Quality.

activities.name: Moderate: Paddle from Ten Mile River to Lackawaxen
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Paddle this stretch of river with a mix of calm waters and rapids from Ten Mile River Access to Lackawaxen River Access. This stretch is approximately 6.5 river miles and takes on average 2.5 hours to paddle.

activities.name: Antelope House Ranger-Led Hike
activities.description: The Antelope House Hike is a unique opportunity for visitors to experience the backcountry of Wupatki with a ranger and see excellent examples of Ancestral Puebloan structures and scenic views within Wupatki National Monument's Eligible Wilderness.

activities.name: Enjoy the View of the Mountains
activities.basis: estimated from duration (10-60 Minutes)
activities.description: Dwight and Mamie Eisenhower loved their Gettysburg farm. The location was perfect to them--on a historic battlefield, in the midst of a rural landscape, with gorgeous views of the surrounding countryside and mountains in the distance. The views you can see as you walk the farm grounds today are virtually unchanged…

activities.name: Birding Along the Anhinga Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The Anhinga Trail is a popular place to start your exploration at Everglades National Park, providing a ready sample of wetland wildlife including alligators, turtles, fish, plants, and birds, all along a short, three-quarter mile paved and boardwalk trail.

activities.name: Monumental Men Exhibit
activities.description: The Monumental Men exhibit corresponds with the statue "Benito Juarez: Child to Man" located on the esplanade in front of the Cultural Center.

activities.name: Sheep Rock Overlook Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (10-30 Minutes)
activities.description: Starting at the front gate of the historic Cant home, this 0.5 mi (0.8 km) trail ends at an overlook with a view of the river valley with Sheep Rock high above.

activities.name: Take a Selfie at Fort Point
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: Take in the views of the Golden Gate Bridge and San Francisco Bay from below at Fort Point.

activities.name: Hike the Lost Mine Trail
activities.description: The Lost Mine Trail climbs to the side of Lost Mine Peak, offering spectacular views of Juniper Canyon and the Northeast Rim of the Chisos.

activities.name: Bainbridge Island Japanese American Exclusion Memorial
activities.basis: estimated from duration (60-120 Minutes)
activities.description: The Bainbridge Island Japanese American Exclusion Memorial is an outdoor exhibit commemorating the internment of Japanese Americans from Bainbridge Island in the state of Washington. It is a unit of the Minidoka National Historic Site in Idaho.

activities.name: Hike the Sky–Woodward Valley–Fire Lane Loop
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Descend from forested Inverness ridge through coastal scrub to the coast. However, it's a steep return through the forest back to the trailhead. Most of this hike is within the Phillip Burton Wilderness and much of this area was burned in the Woodward Fire, which was ignited by lightning strikes in August of 2020…

activities.name: Reflect at the Martin Luther King, Jr. Memorial
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-90 Minutes)
activities.description: Visit the Martin Luther King, Jr. Memorial to take in the Tidal Basin and contemplate quotes from King's lifelong perseverance for freedom and equality.

activities.name: Hiking the Nature Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-50 Minutes)
activities.description: Enjoy a walk along the nature trail at George Washington Birthplace National Monument and experience different habitats that are home to different plants and animals.

activities.name: Turk Mountain
activities.basis: estimated from duration (2-3 Hours)
activities.description: MILE 94.1 | A hike to the 2,981’ summit of Turk Mountain, located in the Shenandoah Wilderness, that provides a wonderful view to the west.

activities.name: Bay Venture Outfitters, North East, MD
activities.basis: estimated from duration (60-240 Minutes)
activities.description: Bay Venture Outfitters in North East, Maryland offers kayak and paddleboard access to the North East River and nearby wetlands. Visitors explore upper Chesapeake Bay tributaries through guided and self-guided tours that emphasize watershed conservation, wildlife observation, and regional history.

activities.name: Hike the Longleaf Pine Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: 1 mile roundtrip | Stroll through a longleaf pine forest near the visitor center on Big Thicket's newest trail.

activities.name: Appalachian Trail - Tanners Ridge Road
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: MILE 52.8 | A fairly level hike that takes you through a former homestead on the famous Appalachian Trail.

activities.name: Watch the Park Film: Forging Greatness; Lincoln in Indiana
activities.description: A 14-minute interpretive film tells of the boyhood of Abraham Lincoln, who grew up to become the 16th President of the United States.

activities.name: Hike to Chimney Tops Overlook
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Hike 3.5 miles (5.6 km) roundtrip on this popular but challenging trail to enjoy views of surrounding mountains and the Chimney Tops pinnacles. This trail is steep and rocky at times, and includes bridges, stairs, and some lingering signs of 2016 wildfires.

activities.name: Go Birding
activities.description: The estuary, shores and forests of Sitka NHP are excellent places to watch birds that are migrating through in the spring and fall. We also boast a fabulous array of birds that are hardy enough to stay all year around.

activities.name: General Grant National Memorial Park Film
activities.description: Watch the 22-minute park film that highlights Grant's life and accomplishments.

activities.name: Flag Change Programs
activities.description: Join the park for its morning or evening flag change programs!

activities.name: Hike the 7 Creeks Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (200-440 Minutes)
activities.description: Hike the seven mile, Seven Creeks partnership trail crossing through habitats and national, state, and city parks.

activities.name: Explore the Dunes
activities.duration: Unlimited - you can explore for a few minutes or a few hours!
activities.description: Explore the tallest dunes in North America! The centerpiece of Great Sand Dunes National Park and Preserve is the 30-square-mile (78-square-km) dunefield, featuring the tallest dunes in North America. Because there are no trails, you can venture out anywhere you'd like to discover unusual insects, plants, wildlife…

activities.name: Guided Tour of the Vassall-Craigie-Longfellow House
activities.description: Join a ranger in exploring the layers of history and significance in the Vassall-Craigie-Longfellow House.

activities.name: Hike the Buffalo River Trail - Boxley to Pruitt
activities.basis: estimated from duration (Hikers may choose to spend a few hours or a few days on the Buffalo River Trail. At 37 miles long, this is a popular thru-hiking trail is typically done in 3 to 5 days. Day hikers may access the trail from several locations for shorter out-and-back or point-to-point hikes.)
activities.duration: Hikers may choose to spend a few hours or a few days on the Buffalo River Trail. At 37 miles long, this is a popular thru-hiking trail is typically done in 3 to 5 days. Day hikers may access the trail from several locations for shorter out-and-back or point-to-point hikes.
activities.description: The Buffalo River Trail (BRT) winds along the bluffs and ridgelines on the south side of the river, traversing the Ponca Wilderness past scenic overlooks, old home sites, and cascading creeks. This portion of the BRT is 37 miles long and is a popular thru-hiking destination for backpackers. Day hikers can access the…

activities.name: Become a Junior Ranger at Sunset Crater Volcano
activities.description: Explore Sunset Crater Volcano and learn about geology, wildlife, starry skies and how you can help us protect national parks.

activities.name: See Endangered Pupfish Along the Visitor Center Nature Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Next to the Kris Eggle Visitor Center is a 1/10th of a mile paved nature trail that loops by a small pond and showcases native Sonoran Desert plant life. The trail begins by the back door of the visitor center and loops back around to the parking lot.

activities.name: An Overview: West Mountain Trails
activities.basis: estimated from duration (40-240 Minutes)
activities.description: The West Mountain trails are less traveled, providing greater opportunities for wildlife sightings. You can get to these trails via Whittington Park and the Canyon Trailhead. See the West Mountain trail map for more information.

activities.name: Hike the Old Military Road Trail
activities.description: The Old Military Road Trail (also known and more often signed as “The American Camp Trail”) is a 1 mile trail that takes visitors from the American Camp Visitor Center to the Frazer Homestead Preserve.

activities.name: Walking the South Pasture Loop
activities.basis: estimated from duration (90-150 Minutes)
activities.description: Walking the South Pasture Loop Trail offers visitors the chance to enjoy a quieter side of the park.

activities.name: Visit Mulberry Bend Overlook
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Great view of the river and sandbars from the overlooks. A paved trail takes visitors from the parking lot to several interpretive wayside exhibits that define the natural and cultural history of the river. Continue your journey by exploring a bur oak forest on the Nature Trail. Average visit time: 30 minutes. Nature…

activities.name: Halemaʻumaʻu Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: Hike down to the floor of Kaluapele (Kīlauea caldera), with possible longer connections to Byron Ledge, Kīlauea Iki, and Nāhuku.

activities.name: Decipher the Code in Poe's Head
activities.description: You'll need to employ your skills of observation carefully to find the combination and unravel the hidden message in the exhibit area.

activities.name: Ghost Towns
activities.description: Ghost towns were once thriving communities that have dwindled over the decades, often created by the search for gold, copper and other valuable minerals. Some vanished entirely after the boom or were absorbed into newer settlements, but many of these towns still stand today, allowing us a nostalgic glimpse into the…

activities.name: Wildlife Watching at Ocmulgee Mounds
activities.description: Ocmulgee Mounds offers a plethora of wildlife to watch as visitors explore the park.

activities.name: Kayak from Port Alsworth to Tommy Island
activities.basis: estimated from duration (2-7 Hours)
activities.description: Get acquainted with the beauty and vastness of Lake Clark firsthand. Spend a day on the water watching birds and jumping fish while paddling out to Tommy Island

activities.name: Fort Windham Rocks
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1 Hour)
activities.description: Compton Gap Parking Area (mile 10.4) | A short hike along the Appalachian Trail that leads to an interesting geologic feature.

activities.name: An Overview: Hot Springs and North Mountain Trails
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The Hot Springs and North Mountain trails are popular since they are easy to reach and provide scenic views. You can get to these trails via Stephen’s Balustrade (grand staircase) behind the Fordyce Bathhouse, Hot Springs Mountain Drive, and the Gulpha Gorge Campground. See the Hot Springs and North Mountain trail map…

activities.name: Watch the Park Film at the Birthplace
activities.description: View the 15 minute orientation film, Abraham Lincoln: The Kentucky Years shown in the Birthplace Unit Visitor Center.

activities.name: Hike Juniper Canyon Trail Loop
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: West Side Trails, Strenuous Hikes, Loop Hike

activities.name: Cross-Country Skiing in Valles Caldera
activities.description: Winter is a spectacular time to visit Valles Caldera National Preserve. The park has miles of groomed trails for the adventurous skier.

activities.name: Ocmulgee River Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-60 Minutes)
activities.description: A trail that winds through a wooded area to the Ocmulgee River.

activities.name: Paddle Kyles Landing to Erbie
activities.basis: estimated from duration (3-4 Hours)
activities.description: Downstream from the hustle and bustle of Kyles Landing, one can find solitude among this comparatively quiet, 5.7-mile stretch of river snaking through the Ponca Wilderness. Paddlers will cruise through adrenaline-inducing shoals, tranquil pools, and haystack waves on this section with fascinating sandstone formations…

activities.name: Short Hike to Makahiku Falls
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1 Hour)
activities.description: Golden light. Verdant forests. White waters. View Makahiku Falls from the Pīpīwai Trail in the Kīpahulu District of Haleakalā National Park.

activities.name: Fish the Headwaters of San Antonio Creek
activities.description: San Antonio Creek is famous throughout New Mexico for wild brown trout and beautiful scenery. Reserve your backcountry vehicle pass and drive to Valle Toledo to fish this stream's headwaters!

activities.name: Bike to Big Spring Brook Hut
activities.description: Take this 12 mile out-and-back route starting at Haskell Gate to Big Spring Brook Hut.

activities.name: Flight 93 National Memorial Junior Ranger
activities.description: This program is designed for children ages 6-12 making a visit to Flight 93 National Memorial. Children can explore the memorial and learn about Flight 93 through 11 activities of varying difficulty. The program also provides a narrative to help explain the Flight 93 story to younger audiences. The Junior Ranger…

activities.name: Explore Biological Diversity in the Park
activities.description: The park is comprised of over 15,000 acres of dunes, oak savannas, swamps, bogs, marshes, prairies, rivers, and forests. It contains 15 miles of Lake Michigan shoreline spanning the distance from Gary to Michigan City. Lake Michigan is part of the largest complex of freshwater lakes in the world. The national park's…

activities.name: Kayak the Beardslees
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: If you’re visiting Glacier Bay on a budget, one of the more accessible wilderness areas of the park is the Beardslee Islands. Kayak through these peaceful, wild waters and look for wildlife along the shoreline for a true Glacier Bay adventure.

activities.name: Rattlesnake Springs Picnic Area
activities.description: Have a relaxing picnic among tall cottonwood trees and watch for a variety of birds.

activities.name: Longmire Historic District Walking Tour
activities.basis: estimated from duration (60 Minutes)
activities.description: At Mount Rainier, designers selected massive logs and glacial boulders as the building materials best suited for integrating new structures with their natural settings. This style of architecture, known as "National Park Service Rustic", can be seen throughout the Longmire District on this walking tour.

activities.name: Hike Anderson Bay Loop
activities.basis: estimated from duration (90-150 Minutes)
activities.description: This trail takes you through the forest past rocky clearings and beaver ponds to spectacular views of Rainy Lake form the shoreline and Anderson Bay from the top of the cliffs.

activities.name: Become a Ninety Six National Historic Site BARK Ranger
activities.description: Help your pet become a BARK Ranger by practicing the BARK Ranger rules and learning about the park.

activities.name: Fossil Butte Visitor Center Exhibits
activities.description: Stop by the visitor center to see the fossils of the animals that lived in Fossil Lake 52 million years ago.

activities.name: Geologic Time Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (10-35 Minutes)
activities.description: Travel in time between the past and present on this 0.5 mi (0.8 km) path connecting the Trail of Fossils and the picnic area. No collecting is permitted.

activities.name: Become a Salem Maritime Junior Ranger
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The Salem Maritime National Historic Site Junior Ranger program is an activity based program offering visitors the opportunity to join the National Park Service "family" as Junior Rangers.

activities.name: Picnic at Cottonwood Cove
activities.description: Cottonwood Cove picnic area features 14 picnic tables, 10 grills, restrooms, and drinking water.

activities.name: Bicycle Port Tobacco to Smallwood State Park
activities.description: Port Tobacco Historic District and Smallwood State Park provide a contrast in landscape diversity, and travel between them is a fine bicycle ride. This route is part of the Adventure Cycling Association Tidewater Potomac Heritage Bicycling Route.

activities.name: McKittrick Canyon Nature Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-60 Minutes)
activities.description: This fascinating, short trail passes an intermittent seep that lies hidden in junipers, then wanders up a southwest slope along an arroyo. Here, plants and animals tolerate true desert conditions. At the top of the trail you can look down at the mouth of McKittrick Canyon and read about Permian Reef geology.

activities.name: Hike the San Antonio Mountain Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The San Antonio Mountain Trail is a strenuous, 11-mile round-trip hike that climbs to the summit of San Antonio Mountain. It takes 5-6 hours to complete. Pets are not permitted.

activities.name: Earn Your Junior Ranger Badge at Eugene O'Neill NHS
activities.description: Opportunities for kids to earn their Junior Ranger badge.

activities.name: Ocean Explorations
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Imagine how the ancient Hawaiian people who lived here and used the ocean and its abundant resources. This is was a beautiful but difficult place to live hundreds of years ago. While you are here take a tidal pool walk (but be careful the rocks can be slippery!), or watch a beautiful sunset along the seashore. Fishing…

activities.name: Overnight on McKittrick Ridge
activities.description: The journey to the top of McKittrick Ridge is "the toughest hike in Texas." This arduous hike is best enjoyed as an overnight hike allowing for rest, recovery, and fabulous night skies at the McKittrick Ridge Wilderness Campground. An overnight Wilderness Use Permit is required for camping.

activities.name: Pullman Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The Pullman Trail is the only trail in the park that allows bicycles. This moderate trail passes an archeological site and connects with the city's Northwoods Trails.

activities.name: Hike the Bolinas Ridge Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-11 Hours)
activities.description: Admire redwood forests and expansive views of the Olema Valley on this dog-friendly, multi-use trail. This up-to-11-mile-long trail begins at either at the Bolinas Ridge Trailhead along Sir Francis Drake Boulevard or at the trail's southern end at the Fairfax-Bolinas Road's junction with the West Ridgecrest Rd. Allow…

activities.name: Crescent Meadow Road Winter Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The most popular of the Giant Forest’s ski trails, Crescent Meadow Road begins at the west end of the Giant Forest Museum Plaza. The entire route is an unplowed road with gentle to moderate grades and lots of giant sequoias.

activities.name: Tunnel Log
activities.description: Since 1935, people have been driving through Tunnel Log. You too can join in on the novelty of driving through a fallen Sequoia.

activities.name: Visit Lomaki and Box Canyon Pueblos
activities.basis: estimated from duration (10-30 Minutes)
activities.description: Lomaki, Beautiful House in the Hopi language, is located at the end of this trail. It had nine rooms constructed from local limestone and sandstone in the last decade of the 1100s.

activities.name: Hike the Wilkinson Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-3 Hours)
activities.description: Saratoga National Historical Park preserves the sites associated with the 1777 Battles of Saratoga. Follow the footsteps of those before you as you hike along hallowed ground.

activities.name: Hike the Fossil Discovery Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: 2.5 mile (4 km) round trip, out and back trail. Easy to moderate difficulty. The Fossil Discovery Trail gives visitors an opportunity to explore a variety of rock layers and see unexcavated fossils as they are often found by paleontologists. The most famous of these rock layers is the Morrison Formation, which…

activities.name: Start at the Henry A. Wallace Visitor Center
activities.description: Begin your visit at the Henry A. Wallace Visitor & Education Center to speak with park rangers about how to get the most out of the Roosevelt experience.

activities.name: Spring Ephemeral Hike
activities.basis: estimated from duration (45-120 Minutes)
activities.description: Enjoy a 1.5-mile hike through the northern floodplain of Rock Creek Park and look for spring ephemerals.

activities.name: Take a walk through time to the bank of the Potomac River
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-3 Hours)
activities.description: Take a two-mile walk from the parking area to access the shoreline of the Potomac River to relax along the river, search for shark teeth, or enjoy a picnic at the overlook.

activities.name: Hike the Minisink Battleground Park Trail System
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Walk this moderately easy, moss-covered loop trail system to catch glimpses of both nature and history. Minisink Battleground Park is the site of the only Revolutionary War battle fought in the Upper Delaware River Valley. Please note Minisink Battleground Park is closed December 1 - April 30. The park is owned and…

activities.name: Virtual 360 Fort Scott Tour
activities.description: Take a tour of Fort Scott through a series of 360 degree panoramic views of the buildings, furnished rooms and exhibit areas.

activities.name: Fort Tours on Georges Island
activities.description: Join a ranger for a tour of Fort Warren on Georges Island!

activities.name: Tour the Eisenhower Home
activities.description: Extensively remodeled in the 1950s to suit the Eisenhowers and reflect their tastes, today the Eisenhower farmhouse is almost frozen in time, just as it when they left it to the American people. During your visit, take a tour inside the home to reflect on the moments and memories that it witnessed, from the historic…

activities.name: Strike a Pose at the Armory
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The Blue Dome and Rampart Colt have long graced the skyline of Hartford and have stood as a symbol of the famed industrialist Samuel Colt. There are many locations within Hartford where the Dome can be seen, but seeing it from the perspective of a worker heading to work, fills one with a sense of awe at the…

activities.name: Hike the Oberholtzer Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (45-80 Minutes)
activities.description: Wander through deciduous and conifer forest as the trail twists around the edge of a cattail filled wetland and past rocks deposited by ancient glaciers. Look for signs of wildlife as you hike to two different overlooks with marsh and lake views.

activities.name: Start at the Booker T. Washington Visitor Center
activities.description: Begin your visit at the Booker T. Washington Visitor Center. Pick up a park brochure and have your park passport stamped. Information desk staff are available to help you plan your visit. Kids can ask for a Junior Ranger activity book. Explore exhibits about Booker T. Washington's early life, from his birth into…

activities.name: Old North Church: Audio Tour
activities.basis: estimated from duration (0-35 Minutes)
activities.description: Discover Old North’s secrets and stories with a brand-new audio tour! Available in English or Spanish, the tour weaves together the story of Paul Revere’s famous lantern signal with recent research into the lives of Old North’s free and enslaved Indigenous and Black congregants.

activities.name: Bike the IAT - Wassataquoik Stream Loop
activities.description: Bike the 11 miles IAT-Wassataquoik Stream Loop at the southern section of Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument.

activities.name: Big Sink Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: Big Sink Trail has three loops that all connect at the picnic area. The parking for it is across the street on 31 E from the park entrance.

activities.name: Hike Warner Point Trail - South Rim
activities.description: Warner Point Trail provides views of various mountain ranges, the Black Canyon, and the Gunnison River. Nature trail guides are available at High Point Overlook or the South Rim Visitor Center.

activities.name: Slaughter Canyon Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (7 Hours)
activities.description: This 5.3 mile (8.6 km) hike travels up Slaughter Canyon with mountains towering above.

activities.name: Walk Main Street in Yorktown
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-120 Minutes)
activities.description: Historic Yorktown is available year round. The Nelson House is open as staffing permits. There are informational waysides along Main Street.

activities.name: Earn Your Russell Cave B.A.R.K Ranger Badge
activities.description: Bring your pet along with you and earn your own B.A.R.K. Ranger tag.

activities.name: Drive-In Camping at Pictured Rocks
activities.description: Pictured Rocks has three drive-in campgrounds open May 15 through Oct. 15. Two are along Lake Superior and the third is on a beautiful inland lake.

activities.name: Waysides at Schoodic Woods Ranger Station
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: There are two waysides featured on a wall at the Schoodic Woods Ranger Station. "Exploring Schoodic," offers an aerial view of a peninsula with a rugged coastline. The land-mass is partially surrounded by deep blue water. "Summit to Sea," captures the essence of the Schoodic Peninsula in a variety of images -- its…

activities.name: Take a Self-guided Tour
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-60 Minutes)
activities.description: The grounds of the historic site are open 24 hours a day. Pick up a map at the Visitor Center or download the NPS App to your phone. Then visit the Birthplace Cottage, Blacksmith Shop, Schoolhouse, Friends Meetinghouse, Statue of Isis, Gravesite, and other historic features of the park.

activities.name: Hiking the Ancestral Sites Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (40-90 Minutes)
activities.description: This trail gives you a glimpse into the past as you pass by the ancestral sites of the Pecos Pueblo and the mission church. You will also enjoy beautiful vistas of the Sangre de Cristo Mountains and Glorieta Mesa as you venture around the trail.

activities.name: Wildlife Viewing - South Unit
activities.description: Explore the South Unit of Theodore Roosevelt National Park and see the wide variety of wildlife that lives there.

activities.name: Funeral Loop Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (15-30 Minutes)
activities.description: A 1/4th mile loop through woods near the Funeral Mound parking lot.

activities.name: Garnet Canyon
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Travel to the heart of the Teton Range on a strenuous hike into Garnet Canyon.

activities.name: Swim Sand Beach
activities.description: Acadia’s only sandy ocean beach, at the beginning of the Park Loop Road’s coastal section, is one of the park’s most heavily-visited areas. Visitors come to swim in the frigid water, bask and play on the sand, seek intertidal creatures, or view a feature widely publicized as a “must-see.”

activities.name: Moose-Wilson Road in Winter
activities.description: The Moose-Wilson Road is a corridor road connecting the towns of Moose and Wilson. In the winter the road is closed from the south at the Granite Trailhead and from the north at the Death Canyon Junction, providing 3 miles (4.8 km) of walking, skiing, and snowshoeing. As you ski or snowshoe on the road you will wind…

activities.name: Take Me Fishing
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Learn to fish with us this summer! Join park staff Sunday afternoons in June, July, and August for some FREE family fun. Catch some fish, learn about the river, and earn a Junior Angler badge. All fishing material and bait are provided. Activities available from 11:00 AM - 4:00 PM.

activities.name: Story in Stone Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The mostly level Story in Stone Trail loops through dramatic pillars of blue-green claystone rocks that make up the Turtle Cove formation of John Day Fossil Beds. Before the trail intersection, the walkway is paved for 900 ft (275 m). Please stay on trail, no collecting permitted, and keep your pets leashed.

activities.name: Boating, Paddling, and Windsurfing
activities.description: Explore Padre Island National Seashore on the water.

activities.name: Hike Oasis of Mara
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: An easy half mile walk to a desert oasis.

activities.name: Head of the Meadow Bike Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-60 Minutes)
activities.description: Get ready to explore! Enjoy a calm bike ride along berry bushes and trees.

activities.name: Hike Pine City Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: A moderate four mile out and back hike.

activities.name: Spend the Night in a Rustic Cabin
activities.description: Experience the simplicity and beauty of a public use cabin. Enjoy world class fishing and kayaking right outside the front door of a beautiful cabin in remote Alaska.

activities.name: Trail to Natural Bridge
activities.basis: estimated from duration (3-4 Hours)
activities.description: This trail is a great opportunity to avoid the crowds in March and to see wildlife. It crosses through a stunning variety of ecosystems before ending at a bridge overlook. The small water-carved bridge is located across the canyon. This hike is about the journey, not the bridge. Return the same way.

activities.name: Green River Road on the OVNHT
activities.basis: estimated from duration (45-60 Minutes)
activities.description: Exploring the Green River Road (Hiking, Equestrian)

activities.name: Explore the Park's Visitor Center
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Start your visit to Little Rock Central High School NHS at the park visitor center - featuring a detailed exhibit with interviews, news footage, and audio/video recordings of those directly involved plus a new park interpretive film, accessible restrooms and a Jefferson National Parks Association (JNPA) bookstore.

activities.name: Round Spring Guided Cave Tour
activities.description: Discover the amazing world beneath your feet! Round Spring Cave is considered the most spectacular cave within Ozark National Scenic Riverways. Large, varied formations fill over a mile of the passage, which has been well-preserved over the years. There is no better way to learn about Ozark caves than through a tour!

activities.name: Historic 1935 Lady Patty Sailing Charter
activities.description: St. Michaels Sailing Charters offers authentic sailing experiences aboard the Historic 1935 Lady Patty Sailing Charter, a restored 1935 wooden ketch departing from St. Michaels, Maryland. Visitors explore the Miles River and Chesapeake Bay while learning about maritime heritage, local history, wildlife, and the…

activities.name: Half Day Activities
activities.description: Suggestions for what to do if you have a half day to explore Grand Portage. Plan to bring a picnic lunch and enjoy a view of the bay. These activities take place indoors at the Heritage Center and Depot, as well as outdoors on the grounds.

activities.name: Honeysuckle Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (20-45 Minutes)
activities.description: Honeysuckle Trail connects Peak Trail with Hot Springs Mountain Trail.

activities.name: Mountain Goats
activities.description: The mountain goat is one of the park's most inconic creatures. It is the only living member of its genus and is more closely related to caprines (the chamois of Europe and the gorals and serows of Asia) than to domesticated goats.

activities.name: Wildlife Viewing - North Unit
activities.description: Explore the North Unit of Theodore Roosevelt National Park and see the wide variety of wildlife that lives there.

activities.name: Report for Duty
activities.description: Designed for visitors 5-12 (but open to all!) the Junior Ranger program is designed to help young visitors learn more about the people, places and events related to St. Louis history and westward expansion in the 1800s.

activities.name: Hike to Chasteen Creek Cascade
activities.description: Hike 3.6 miles (5.8 km) roundtrip through hardwood forest following the path of mountain streams to a peaceful cascade. This trail is wide, well-graded, and regularly used by both hikers and horse riders.

activities.name: Hike the City of Rocks Loop
activities.basis: estimated from duration (4-6 Hours)
activities.description: This remote loop hike is a ranger favorite. The combination of pine trees, rock formations, and epic views offer a surprise at every turn of the trail.

activities.name: Park Store
activities.description: Looking for the perfect souvenir from your visit to Grant-Kohrs Ranch? We’ve got it and more at the park store! The park store offers a wide range of educational products, apparel, books, toys and games, handmade items, and other Grant-Kohrs Ranch souvenirs for all ages and interests. These products complement the…

activities.name: Move Along the Mississippi River
activities.description: Move along the historic St. Louis Riverfront Trail

activities.name: Look for Red-Legged Frogs in Mori Point
activities.description: Watch for California's red-legged frogs in the restored pond habitat at Mori Point.

activities.name: Go Roller Skating
activities.description: Visit the National Park Service's only roller skating pavilion!

activities.name: Upper Dogwood Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Upper Dogwood trail has short rises and long stretches of flat trail. It can be combined with the Lower Dogwood Trail or the Goat Rock Trail to create a longer hike.

activities.name: Follow Trenches on the 19th Corps Trails
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-120 Minutes)
activities.description: Woodland trails follow a line of trenches built by the US 19th Corps in the fall of 1864. They connect the 128th New York Monument with Belle Grove Plantation. Remnants of trenches and earthworks are still visible along the trails. The trails are on lands managed by Cedar Creek Battlefield Foundation (CCBF) and Belle…

activities.name: Picnic at South Arizona Telepone Cove
activities.description: South Arizona Telephone Cove picnic area features 6 picnic tables. This location does not have grills, restrooms, or drinking water.

activities.name: Visit Forks of the Road
activities.description: From 1833 to 1863, Forks of the Road was the second largest slave market in the Deep South. Tens of thousands of enslaved men, women and children were transported from Virginia, Maryland, Kentucky, and the Carolinas to the market at Natchez. The slave market operated from 1833 until the arrival of Federal troops on…

activities.name: Wander Through Georgetown Waterfront Park
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-3 Hours)
activities.description: Georgetown Waterfront Park stretches along the banks of the Potomac River

activities.name: See the Park Film
activities.description: "A Song of Seasons" plays in the Visitor Center theater every half hour when the Visitor Center is open.

activities.name: Stay in a Public Use Cabin
activities.description: Consider staying in one of the park's three public use cabins. These cabins provide a great opportunity to stay overnight in Kenai Fjords. You can experience the solitude and enjoyment of your park, no matter the season, while still enjoying a roof over your head.

activities.name: Hiking the Potkopinu Section of the Natchez Trace National Scenic Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-6 Hours)
activities.description: Potkopinu (Pot-cop-i-new), the southernmost section of the Natchez Trace National Scenic Trail, is only three miles long, but it is the longest stretch of "sunken" historic Trace remaining. Named for the Natchez word meaning "little valley." Thus trail cuts deep into the rich, fine-grained soil. It doesn't take much…

activities.name: Picnic Where the President Picnicked
activities.description: Picnic where the President picnicked! Herbert Hoover celebrated his 80th birthday in 1954 at a picnic shelter built by Boy Scouts in his honor. Herbert Hoover National Historic Site has two picnic shelters.

activities.name: Castillo San Cristobal - Plaza Norzagaray
activities.description: This event site is located in front of the old Spanish ramp entrance to Castillo San Cristobal. This location can accommodate over 100 participants. With the amazing water view it is perfect for all kinds of events. Water and electricity are not available.

activities.name: Horseback Riding in Rock Creek Park
activities.description: For the horseback rider, 13 miles of dirt and gravel bridle paths crisscross the park.

activities.name: Overlook Trail at Knob Creek
activities.basis: estimated from duration (2-3 Hours)
activities.description: 3-mile round trip hiking trail at Knob Creek Boyhood home site.

activities.name: Visit the USS Arizona Memorial
activities.description: A white monolithic structure sits in Pearl Harbor spanning the width of the sunken USS Arizona battleship.

activities.name: Stamp Your Passport To Your National Parks
activities.description: Get four different cancellation stamps by visiting NPS and partner sites at Cedar Creek & Belle Grove NHP.

activities.name: Hike the Holly Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (4 Hours)
activities.description: The Holly Trail (8 miles, roundtrip) offers the chance to explore away from roads and busier trails and stretch your legs with a longer hike. Gain new perspective as you traverse a canyon floor, squeeze through slot canyons, and take the long way around. At the end, your reward is reaching the towering remains and…

activities.name: Orienteering
activities.description: If you would like to practice your orienteering skills, the park maintains courses that are available for public use.

activities.name: Labor Day Weekend at Slater Mill
activities.description: Join us for a celebration of Labor Day weekend at Old Slater Mill. Free musical performances, tours, talks, and activities. The weekend's highlights include: 8/29: Walkabout/Workshop at 6:30 PM 8/30: River Bend East Songwriters Festival Kickoff at 6:30 PM 8/31: River Bend East Songwriters Festival 12-4 PM; Specialty…

activities.name: Pack a Picnic
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: All picnic tables are accessible and located along concrete routes. Some of these picnic tables are shaded. There are accessible parking spots near the picnic area.

activities.name: Visit The Point at Harpers Ferry
activities.description: Visit where the Potomac and Shenandoah rivers meet! From this location, known as The Point, you look upon three states - Maryland, Virginia, and West Virginia - as well as the confluence of two rivers: the Potomac and the Shenandoah. We invite you to visit in any season to gaze upon the magnificent sight of this water…

activities.name: Fish the East Fork in Hidden Valley
activities.description: Hike the Jemez River Trail to Hidden Valley, where the Rio Grande chub, Rio Grande sucker, and longnose dace are the dominant fish species.

activities.name: Hike the Cruiser Lake Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: This rugged trail crosses over the peninsula, up rocky cliffs and down into remote wetland areas. See parts of the park many people do not visit. Start your hike either at Anderson Bay on the Rainy Lake side or Lost Bay on the Kabetogama side. Reserve a backcounrty campsite to turn this into a multi-day trip. Hiking…

activities.name: Ring the Bell: A Symbolic Marker of Freedom
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Booker T. Washington and his family were among the four million enslaved individuals emancipated throughout the South in 1865, following the arrival of Union troops at the Burroughs Plantation in Hale’s Ford, Franklin County. Although historical records do not confirm whether Union troops or formerly enslaved…

activities.name: Hike Bubbles Nubble Loop
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: This hike traverses the summits of North Bubble, South Bubble, and Connors Nubble and crosses varying terrain of forest paths, steep granite sections, and a level carriage road. Visitors can enjoy views of Eagle Lake, Jordan Pond, Pemetic and Sargent Mountains, and the Cranberry Isles.

activities.name: Hike Balconies Cliffs Trail to Balconies Cave Trail Loop
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: West Side Trails, Moderate Hikes, Loop Hike, Cave Hike

activities.name: Mammoth Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: A short, paved trail takes you from the Welcome Center to the Dig Shelter where you can see the fossilized remains of Ice Age animals.

activities.name: Ebey's Reserve - Historic Coupeville
activities.description: Pay a visit to one of the oldest towns in Washington State - located in the Central Whidbey Island Historic District and part of Ebey's Landing National Historical Reserve. Shopping, dining are all just steps away from the convenient parking on Alexander Street - a block from downtown.

activities.name: Hike the Beech Woods Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: 1½ miles roundtrip | See a forest of American beeches on this pleasant loop hike in the northeastern corner of the preserve.

activities.name: Picnic at the Abraham Lincoln Birthplace
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: You and your family are able to enjoy the beautiful picnic area and shaded Picnic Pavilion on a first-come first-served basis. While you eat, you may even get a chance to see some of Kentucky's wildlife! Trash and recycling receptacles are provided under and near the pavilion, please remember to use them.

activities.name: Paddle through Blind Ash Bay
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: Explore the rocky shoreline and a calm bay with your canoe or kayak. From the paddle launch head west one mile between the rocky shore and small islands before turning south to explore Blind Ash Bay. Your total trip length will be about 2.5 miles.

activities.name: Picnic at Wind Cave
activities.description: Looking for a quiet place to enjoy a picnic? Whether you're looking for a good picnic spot or just a place to eat lunch while waiting for a tour, the picnic area is open year-round from sunrise to sunset.

activities.name: Hike to Johnson Lake from Snake Creek
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Hike to the backcountry and isolated Johnson Lake. 8.0 miles round trip rewards visitors with a chance for isolation and exercise. This version of the route approaches from the Snake Creek Trailhead, but Johnson Lake is also accessible from the north via Baker Creek Trailhead.

activities.name: Backpack the Craters of the Moon Wilderness
activities.description: Immerse yourself in the solitude of the Craters of the Moon Wilderness.

activities.name: Hike the Estero–Glenbrook–Muddy Hollow Road Loop
activities.basis: estimated from duration (3-4 Hours)
activities.description: This loop hike passes through young woodlands, coastal scrub, and grassland within the Phillip Burton Wilderness. It offers views of Estero de Limantour and the possibility of seeing tule elk and other wildlife that call this area home. It is also a great hike for spring wildflowers. Allow 15 minutes driving time from…

activities.name: Hike Bradley Fork Trail
activities.description: The Bradley Fork Trail offers a scenic and diverse outdoor experience, featuring picturesque creeks, seasonal wildflowers, fishing access, horseback riding opportunities, and backcountry camping.

activities.name: View A Cesar Chavez Documentary
activities.description: At the monument's visitor center, documentaries about the farmworker movement and Cesar Chavez's legacy bring life to the powerful stories of the struggle for justice and civil rights. The most commonly shown film is La Paz, which explains the choice to locate the union headquarters at the remote Keene site. Ask at…

activities.name: Become a Junior Ranger at Boston National Historical Park
activities.description: Become a Junior Ranger at Boston National Historical Park by learning about the sites along the Freedom Trail® here in Boston.

activities.name: Hike the Damascus Forest Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Enjoy the varied landscape of wetlands, uplands, and old growth forests on this easy loop trail. A large stand of old growth hemlock trees reminds us of the virgin forests that once stood here. This trail is located on land owned and managed by Damascus Township.

activities.name: Experience the Night
activities.description: Half the park is after dark! Night at Great Sand Dunes can include dunes exploration under a bright full moon, viewing thousands of stars on a clear moonless night, listening for owls along the foothills, or observing migrating amphibians on a wet night.

activities.name: Stroll to the Big Tree Wayside
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: For those short on time then this 5-minute walk will lead to some amazingly large trees.

activities.name: Read the Names on the Fort Caroline Memorial
activities.description: Read the known names of the French colonists of Fort Caroline, the failed French attempt to establish a colony in Florida. This first conflict between European powers in North America would lead to more bloodshed, for Native Americans, French, Spanish, English, and many more. The impact of colonization, the fight for…

activities.name: Hike West Side Loop
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Enjoy a moderate loop hike in the Black Rock area

activities.name: River Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (10-35 Minutes)
activities.description: Starting at the Cant Ranch parking lot, this 0.6 mi (1 km) long trail passes through historic fields and alongside a historic fruit orchard on its way to the John Day River. Fruit may be collected from the orchard when in season, but please do not climb the trees since the branches are old and brittle.

activities.name: Greenstone Section 6: Hike from Ishpeming Tower to South Desor
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1 Day)
activities.description: This rolling trail through hardwood forest offers an opportunity for self reflection. Mileage: About 3.5 miles

activities.name: Paddle Washington Creek
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-3 Hours)
activities.description: Paddle Washington Creek, located on the west end of Isle Royale National Park. Washington Creek is an excellent spot for wildlife viewing.

activities.name: El Capitan Viewpoint
activities.description: On the climb up Guadalupe Pass on U.S. Highway 62/180 just a few miles west of the Pine Springs area, this roadside pull-off provides an unparalleled view to the summit of El Capitan.

activities.name: Paddling Dillards Ferry to Rush Landing
activities.basis: estimated from duration (4-6 Hours)
activities.description: This 9-mile paddling trip offers some great fishing holes between Buffalo Point and Rush, where the pools get long and the current typically slows in the summer time. You have the option at stopping at Buffalo Point, which is 1.5 miles from Dillards Ferry to admire Painted Bluff and Ludlow Bluff further downstream…

activities.name: Explore the Cross Estate Gardens and Hike to the NJ Brigade Encampment Site
activities.description: You can go in any order once you arrive at the New Jersey Brigade Encampment Area and Cross Estate Gardens. The hike is approx. 1 mile to reach the encampment site (note: it is downhill going out, uphill coming back).

activities.name: Snowshoe with a Ranger
activities.basis: estimated from duration (2 Hours)
activities.description: Our popular ranger-guided snowshoe walks are a great way to explore snowy trails. Snowshoe programs are usually offered from December through March, as long as there is at least 8 inches of snow on the ground.

activities.name: Walk in the Last Footsteps of Meriwether Lewis
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Follow last footsteps of explorer Meriwether Lewis on a section of the Old Natchez Trace and visit his burial site. This self-guide tour will take you a little over half a mile in an easy loop along a trail with interpretive exhibits, to the historic Old Trace, to his burial place and monument, then back past the…

activities.name: Hike West Prong Trail
activities.description: Hike 5.4 miles (8.7 km) roundtrip on West Prong Trail

activities.name: Hike the Sulphur & Alamo Canyon Loop
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The Sulphur & Alamo Canyon Loop is a strenuous, 12.2-mile trail through Valles Caldera's geothermal areas. It takes approximately 6 hours to complete. Pets are not permitted.

activities.name: Glasshouse Ruins
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-45 Minutes)
activities.description: Site of the original glassworks. Site is self guiding with waysides and items to see within the building.

activities.name: Echo Canyon Grottoes
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-60 Minutes)
activities.description: Just 1/2 mile from the parking area, on the Echo Canyon Trail, visitors can be amazed by the tunnel-like rock formations. The Echo Canyon Grottoes are a great option for those who want to experience the rocks but have limited time or mobility.

activities.name: Hike Western Mountain Loop
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: This 3.8 mile loop travels through forested areas and up the summits of Bernard Mountain and Mansell Mountain, together creating Western Mountain. Although there are not many views, it is a challenging hike with hundreds of cut stone steps and other steep sections along the way.

activities.name: Earn a Hagerman Fossil Junior Ranger award
activities.duration: Depending on weather and your interests you can spend minutes or hours at the overlooks. Doing the workbook itself takes about one hour. Adding or substituting hands-on activities also takes about one hours with those activities usually in the visitor center.
activities.description: Junior Rangers at Hagerman Fossil Beds have options. There's the general work booklet, and there's a hands-on option in the summer (or when staffing and conditions permit).

activities.name: Get the B. Free Franklin Cancellation
activities.basis: estimated from duration (5-15 Minutes)
activities.description: Get the same cancellation on your stamp that Franklin used when he was postmaster. There's cool and then there's "B. Free Franklin" cool.

activities.name: Volunteer to complete the PHT in Northern Virginia
activities.description: Volunteers are essential to complete the PHT network in Northern Virginia.

activities.name: Hike the McClures Beach Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: A rugged trail descends moderately steeply down a ravine to the ocean. McClures Beach is contained within a beautiful cove backed by rocky cliffs, but watch out for tidal fluctuations and dangerous surf. Allow 35 minutes driving time from Bear Valley to the McClures Beach Trailhead, located at the end of the Pierce…

activities.name: View Sunset from Sunset Rock
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: Are you looking for the perfect spot for sunset? Head to Sunset Rock in the Giant Forest. This less trafficked trail is a great option for escaping the crowds and enjoying the colorful sunset.

activities.name: Boat on Blue Mesa Reservoir
activities.description: Blue Mesa Reservoir, the largest body of water in Colorado, has 96 miles of shoreline and provides opportunities for motorboating, paddleboarding, kayaking, canoeing, and more.

activities.name: Visit the Ethno-botanical Garden
activities.description: This one-acre garden of native plants restores a site that had been overtaken by invasive plants.

activities.name: Walk to John Oliver Cabin
activities.description: Explore the scenery of Cades Cove and the historic John Oliver Cabin and homesite with a short path—0.3 miles (0.5 km) roundtrip—suitable for wheelchairs and strollers. The trail gives way to level, packed gravel once it reaches the complex of log structures.

activities.name: Hike the Timber Creek Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (3-6 Hours)
activities.description: An extended loop through the Baker Creek area, Timber Creek offers more meadows, woodland, and creeks. This 5.1 mile loop is surely worth a visit, especially when the Scenic Drive is closed.

activities.name: Boat-in Camping at Point Reyes National Seashore
activities.description: Point Reyes National Seashore offers year-round boat-in camping on the west shore of Tomales Bay. There is a fee and permit system for overnight camping within Point Reyes National Seashore. Reservations may be made online at Recreation.gov up to three months in advance.

activities.name: Hiking along the Arkansas River
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-90 Minutes)
activities.description: Visitors can hike a 1.75 mile trail that winds its way through the cottonwood trees alongside the wetlands and the Arkansas River. Interpretive exhibit panels explain the further significance of this important river ecosystem.

activities.name: Hike Cedar Point Nature Trail - South Rim
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: This short, moderately sloped trail offers visitors a chance to brush up on local flora with guideposts describing the various plants along the way.

activities.name: Day Trip or Backpack Hike to Coyote Gulch
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-14 Days)
activities.description: Open year-round but most popular in Spring and Fall, Coyote Gulch is a tributary of the Escalante River with several entry points for day hiking or backpacking in the Escalante Canyons of Glen Canyon National Recreation Area and Grand Staircase National Monument. This is a wilderness area, prepare to pack out…

activities.name: Easy: Paddle from Buckingham to Long Eddy
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Paddle this calm stretch of river from Buckingham River Access to Long Eddy River Access. This stretch is approximately 9.5 river miles and takes on average 4.5 hours to paddle.

activities.name: Hike to Victoria Mine
activities.basis: estimated from duration (3-4 Hours)
activities.description: Experience Organ Pipe’s mining history by hiking to Victoria Mine, one of the oldest prospecting sites in southwest Arizona and the heart of gold and silver mining in the Organ Pipe area.

activities.name: Visit Pictured Rocks National Lakeshore
activities.description: Description

activities.name: Browse the Bookstore
activities.description: A selection of books and souvenirs are available for sale in the bookstore.

activities.name: Become a Scotts Bluff Junior Ranger
activities.description: Earn your Scotts Bluff National Monument Junior Ranger badge!

activities.name: Mysteries of the Ancient Architects Film
activities.description: Another popular choice for visitors is the highly-recommended park orientation film. Mysteries of the Ancient Architects gives viewers an overview of these American Indians and their incredible accomplishments from over 2,000 years ago. Whether your knowledge of this culture is novice or expert, this film will leave…

activities.name: Watch for Hawks at the Mills River Overlook
activities.duration: Once at the Mills River Overlook, visitors may stay for as little or long as they wish.
activities.description: The raptors are coming! And they’ve got the “kettle” on!

activities.name: Bike to Wildcat Campground
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Biking to Wildcat Campground is no easy feat—but a lot of work yields a lot of reward! Enjoy your lunch at sunny Wildcat Campground or spend some time at Wildcat Beach after you bike up and over one of the highest points of Inverness Ridge. This ride starts at the Five Brooks Trailhead. Allow 10 minutes drive time…

activities.name: Become a Saratoga B.A.R.K. Ranger
activities.description: Do you think your pet has what it takes to become an official Saratoga Bark Ranger? Learn about B.A.R.K. principles, complete activities, and check in with the rangers at the Visitor Center to get your four-legged friends certified!

activities.name: Spring and Fall Campfire programs
activities.description: Campfire Programs in the Greenbelt Park campground. Program begins at Sunset.

activities.name: Portage from Lake Richie to Chippewa Harbor
activities.description: The portage between Lake Richie and Chippewa Harbor is 1.2 miles and connects to the island's exterior.

activities.name: Hike Kurt Diederichs Climb
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Kurt Diederichs Climb is a memorial path at Sieur de Monts. It is a .4 mile steep ascent with many granite steps. It is one of the routes to reach Schiff Path, and eventually the summit of Dorr Mountain.

activities.name: Hike Bajada Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Enjoy this short, easy trail through the Colorado desert.

activities.name: First Manassas Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (2-4 Hours)
activities.description: A 5.4 mile circuit hike where you can explore the First Manassas battlefield in detail.

activities.name: Fort Baker Fishing
activities.description: Fishing in Fort Baker

activities.name: Trunk Bay Underwater Snorkel Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-60 Minutes)
activities.description: This unique underwater trail is a great way to learn about the diverse animals of the coral reef habitat.

activities.name: Visit The Sculptor's Studio
activities.description: Visit the Sculptor's Studio to learn more about Gutzon Borglum, his scale model and the process of carving Mount Rushmore.

activities.name: Take a Break on Cape Cod's Beaches
activities.duration: You can spend a few hours on the beach, or pack a lunch and plan an entire day in the sun.
activities.description: What better way to enjoy a day on Cape Cod than to relax on the beach? Cape Cod National Seashore features 6 beaches for visitors to enjoy. So grab you beach umbrella, your sunscreen, and get ready for a day of fun in the sun!

activities.name: Explore Wildflowers in Death Valley
activities.description: Learn about the different flowers you might be able to see in Death Valley during spring months.

activities.name: Close to Home
activities.description: Eleanor Roosevelt: Close to Home is an overview of the inspirational life of Eleanor Roosevelt and highlights her dedication as champion of social justice and racial equality. The film, which won the United Nations Association Film Festival Award in 2013, introduces viewers to Val-Kill, the home of this extraordinary…

activities.name: Explore Melrose
activities.description: Explore one of the best-preserved suburban estates in the Deep South from the pre-civil war era.

activities.name: Grant Grove Village to General Grant Tree Winter Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (2-4 Hours)
activities.description: This trail begins at the Grant Grove visitor center, following multiple trails to connect to the General Grant Tree Trail loop. For those who want to experience the sequoias of Grant Grove but are looking for a slightly longer hike, this is the perfect option.

activities.name: Hiking in the North Unit
activities.duration: Variable; each trail listing includes mileage and terrain description to assist the visitor in calculating how long it would take to complete.
activities.description: Nature Trails in the North Unit are perfect for casual hikers and nature enthusiasts, but the backcountry trails really steal the show! The Buckhorn, Caprock Coulee, and famed Achenbach Trails traverse the park's vast wilderness areas. Check out all the options and what will fit your trip best.

activities.name: Hike the Oconaluftee River Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Enjoy a riverside stroll approximately 3 miles (4.8 km) roundtrip on one of the only pet- and bike-friendly trails in the park. This popular trail is relatively flat, wide, and graveled and follows the Oconaluftee River through elk habitat and hardwood forest.

activities.name: Hike to Look Rock Tower
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Walk along a short, paved trail 0.8 miles (1.3 km) through the forest to an observation tower with panoramic views of the Smokies and Blount County, Tennessee. This trail includes some mild to moderate inclines.

activities.name: Hike the Alpine Lakes Loop
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: An easy trail at high elevation, the Alpine Lakes Loop is a 2.7 mile staple of many visits to Great Basin. Wildlife and wildflowers are often visible in the many meadows and streams in this shelter beneath some of the grandest peaks in Nevada.

activities.name: Take a Hike on the Russell Cave Nature Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Adventure up the strenuous 1.2-mile nature trail to see the plants and landscape that prehistoric people would have been interacting with while living at Russell Cave.

activities.name: Picnic at Pole Canyon
activities.description: The entrance to Pole Canyon area has day use picnic areas with picnic tables and charcoal grills. This shaded area offers a chance to be removed from the crowded visitor center to enjoy and mid day snack. Please pack out your ashes and obey all fire restrictions.

activities.name: Hike Sound of Silence Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: 3.2 miles (5.1 km) round trip loop. Moderate to difficult. The Sound of Silence Trail takes hikers through the geologic diversity of Dinosaur National Monument. Hikers encounter a variety of terrain, including an intermittent stream bed, upturned rock layers, desert badlands, and slickrock. A short rock scramble is…

activities.name: Hike the North Crater Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: This strenuous 3.5-mile trail drops into the mouth of North Crater.

activities.name: Fort Necessity Junior Ranger
activities.description: Come to the park, watch the movie, visit Fort Necessity, and complete the Junior Ranger Activity Book to earn a Fort Necessity Junior Ranger badge.

activities.name: Explore the Middle Prong Wilderness
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-8 Hours)
activities.description: Want to take a walk on the wild side? Try a hike in the Middle Prong Wilderness! Adjacent to the Blue Ridge Parkway, this wilderness area protects a beautiful forest and has ample opportunities for solitude.

activities.name: Snowshoe and Cross-country Ski on the McDade Trail
activities.description: Snowshoeing and cross-country skiing on the McDade Recreational Trail.

activities.name: Fly a kite like Wilbur and Orville!
activities.description: Fly a kite just like the Wright Brothers.

activities.name: Picnic by the Bayou
activities.description: Have a picnic next to Pine Island Bayou at Edgewater Day-Use Area. A short trail starts here and follows the bank of the bayou.

activities.name: Explore the Trails at Meadowood
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-4 Hours)
activities.description: Hike, Bike, and Horseback Ride at Meadowood Special Recreation Management Area.

activities.name: Visit Tuzigoot Pueblo
activities.basis: estimated from duration (45-60 Minutes)
activities.description: Walk the 0.3 mile trail that encircles the Tuzigoot pueblo, a 1,000 year old dwelling built by the Sinagua people.

activities.name: Northeast Area: Remote Winter Recreation
activities.description: Enjoy winter camping, snowshoeing, cross-country skiing, and snowmobiling in this less-visited area in the northeast of the park.

activities.name: Picnic at Echo Bay
activities.description: Echo Bay picnic area features 2 picnic tables and restrooms. There are no grills or drinking water at this location.

activities.name: Take a "Bell-fie"
activities.description: Come see the international symbol of freedom in all its glory. Learn about the Liberty Bell's legacy as a symbol of protest and celebration, from its humble beginnings as the State House bell to its use as a rallying cry to end slavery and an inspiration to the modern civil rights movement. And don't forget to get…

activities.name: Hike Chalone Peak Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: East Side Trails, Strenuous Hikes, Highest Peak

activities.name: Hike the Rabbit Ridge Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: The Rabbit Ridge Trail is a 2.4-mile round-trip hike that climbs to the south rim of Valles Caldera. It takes 1-2 hours to complete. Pets are not permitted.

activities.name: Silver Spur Meadow Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Beginning from the Visitor Center, Campground, or Faraway Ranch picnic area, this 1.2 mile/1.9 kilometer leisurely walk goes by the Faraway Ranch Historic District, Stafford Cabin, and Silver Spur Meadow. This is a dog-friendly trail.

activities.name: Hike Spectacle Island's Drumlins
activities.description: Hike one of the drumlins of Spectacle Island to catch beautiful views of the city and harbor.

activities.name: Hiking Dune Life Nature Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The Dune Life Nature Trail is full of life! This family-friendly, one mile (1.6 km) loop trail is a great way to explore White Sands.

activities.name: Kelly House Museum of Transportation
activities.description: Learn the story of the Transportation Revolution by exploring the museum and site. Walk along the river and the Blackstone Canal. Check out the reconstructed historic barn for more exhibits. Ride a bike or walk down the Blackstone Bikeway. There are many ways to explore the site and learn more about the history. Check…

activities.name: Become a Cape Cod Junior Ranger
activities.description: Visit Cape Cod National Seashore and become a Junior Ranger!

activities.name: Agents of Discovery at San Francisco Maritime National Historical Park
activities.description: Agents of Discovery® is an educational mobile game that enables players to become a secret “Agent” and explore the Park in a fun new way. Unlock hidden geo-located challenges, solve entertaining trivia questions, and earn a prize!

activities.name: Teutonia Peak trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (0-3 Hours)
activities.description: The Teutonia Peak Hike is a great way to examine the aftermath of the Dome Fire up close. The hike is three miles round-trip and takes between 2 and 3 hours for most people.

activities.name: Boulder Bridge Hike
activities.basis: estimated from duration (90-200 Minutes)
activities.description: Hike the 3.5-mile Boulder Bridge Loop from the Rock Creek Park Nature Center to one of the most iconic places in Rock Creek Park

activities.name: Sandstone Falls Overlook
activities.description: Wildlife Observation Nature Observation

activities.name: Hanford: Visit the Yakama Nation Cultural Center
activities.description: Located approximately 50 miles (80.5 km) from the Tri-Cities, the Yakama Nation Cultural Center preserves and interprets the living culture of the Yakama people. The Yakama homeland extends across the Columbia Plateau, including the Hanford Site and Tri-Cities.

activities.name: Take the Totem Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-90 Minutes)
activities.description: A historic trail lined with Haida and Tlingit totem poles passes through classic Southeast Alaska temperate rainforest to the site of the Battle of 1804.

activities.name: Opelofa Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (20-60 Minutes)
activities.description: A 1-mile loop trail through the wetlands of the park.

activities.name: Blue Basin Overlook Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The Blue Basin Overlook Trail is a 3.25 mi (5.2 km) trail that climbs 760 ft (230 m) in elevation to an overlook of Blue Basin. This trail provides breathtaking views down into steep canyons and grand vistas of the John Day River valley. It starts both at the Blue Basin parking lot and also connects along the Island…

activities.name: Picnicking in Dinosaur
activities.description: The Plug Hat Butte picnic area is located along Harpers Corner Road on the Colorado side of the monument.

activities.name: Maho Bay
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: The perfect experience for sea turtle lovers!

activities.name: Hike the Tusten Mountain Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: This moderately difficult three-mile trail takes you on a loop through historic remains of the Tusten Settlement as you climb to the summit for a magnificent view of the Upper Delaware Valley. Public access to Tusten Mountain Trail is made possible through an agreement with the Conservation Fund.

activities.name: Hiking Backcountry Camping Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (2-3 Hours)
activities.description: Are you looking for expansive views of snow-white gypsum dunes for miles? Hiking the Backcountry Camping Trail provides a sense of the magnitude of the world's largest gypsum dunefield.

activities.name: Boat on Crystal Reservoir
activities.description: Crystal Reservoir provides backcountry flatwater boating opportunities. Hand-carried craft only. Access is from Mesa Creek Trail located at Cimarron.

activities.name: Paddle Hoyes Run to Sang Run on the Upper Youghiogheny
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: A mostly easy paddle--kayak, canoe or raft--on upper Youghiogheny River and important to check water levels. Outfitters serve this area, offering shuttles and boats. Part of the Eastern Continental Divide Loop, see the "Do the Loop" section of the Garrett Trails Web page for details.

activities.name: Hike the 1871 Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The rugged lava shoreline of the South Kona coast beckons you to explore the backcountry trails of the park. Have you ever imagined visiting a historic abandoned Hawaiian village? Come and experience this special and unique area. Step back in time. The ocean will whisper ancient stories from the past as you pass by…

activities.name: Fort McHenry Movie
activities.description: Fort McHenry's introductory film is one of the most popular activities at the park.

activities.name: Tidepooling at Point Reyes National Seashore
activities.description: Only when waters recede at a low tide does the intertidal zone reveal its majesty to the careful explorer. This is a realm inhabited by magnificent creatures that look as if they came from another time and world. The best tidepools at Point Reyes are found at Sculptured Beach, near Coast Camp. Duxbury Reef near Agate…

activities.name: Pear Lake Winter Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The Pear Lake Trail is the most challenging of the marked ski trails in Sequoia National Park. The trail climbs steeply through dense fir forest, then ends at the Pear Lake Winter Hut.

activities.name: Hike the Geological Interpretive Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: City of Rocks is well known for its geologic wonders. The Geological Interpretive Trail will guide you through many types of unique rock features and formations and explain the forces that created them. There are 12 interpretive stations along the 0.5 mile trail. The trail rises 160 feet in elevation, makes a loop…

activities.name: Guadalupe Ridge Trail (GRT)
activities.basis: estimated from duration (5-6 Days)
activities.description: This trail covers 100 miles (161 km) through Carlsbad Caverns National Park, Lincoln National Forest, Bureau of Land Management, and Guadalupe Mountains National Park. Over 20 miles (32 km) of this trail is within Carlsbad Caverns National Park.

activities.name: Explore the Mission Grounds
activities.basis: estimated from duration (10-60 Minutes)
activities.description: The biggest draw to Tumacácori will likely be the grand, 3-story adobe church at its center. But a mission was much more than just a church. Explore the rest of the grounds, including the cemetery, orchard, and O'odham ki to get a fuller picture of what mission life entailed.

activities.name: Whittington Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The flat, gravel trail is popular with joggers and walkers. Whittington Trail loops around Whittington Park.

activities.name: Kayak Drakes Estero and Estero de Limantour
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-8 Hours)
activities.description: Kayaking or canoeing Drakes Estero and Estero de Limantour offers an intimate marine wilderness experience unlike any other. Kayaking and canoeing is permitted in Drakes Estero and Estero de Limantour from July 1 through February 28; closed March 1 through June 30.

activities.name: Hike the Trails at Chiricahua
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: 17 miles of trails will take you into a wilderness of rocks. Chiricahua offers a range of day hiking options from easy to strenuous.

activities.name: Stretch Your Legs at the Dismal Nitch Wayside
activities.basis: estimated from duration (5-30 Minutes)
activities.description: Start your Lewis & Clark journey where the Corps of Discovery did.
