activities.basis: estimated from duration (2-6 Hours)
activities.description: Discover Suzy’s Cave, a wave-washed cliff and an inland sea arch, found on Isle Royale’s eastern end.

activities.name: Join a Historic Town Meeting at Faneuil Hall
activities.description: Join National Parks of Boston Rangers as we recreate historic town meetings.

activities.name: Experience Smith Island Tour
activities.description: Journey by boat to Smith Island, Maryland’s last inhabited offshore island, and explore the villages of Tylerton, Rhodes Point, and Ewell. Guided by island residents, visitors can hear personal stories, enjoy local seafood, and learn about the crabbing industry and traditions like Smith Island cake. The experience…

activities.name: Take a Pullman Ranger-Guided Tour
activities.description: Park Ranger Tours

activities.name: Hike a Nature Trail
activities.description: A few miles of nature trails surrounding the Fort Frederica town site gives visitors the opportunity to stretch their legs. Numbered posts along the trail identify plants and other nature features. Pick up a Nature Trail brochure at the Visitor Center or trailhead to follow along.

activities.name: Hike Jordan Pond Path
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The trail follows the shore of Jordan Pond, providing iconic views of steep, glacially sculpted mountains and the glacially carved valley that is now Jordan Pond.

activities.name: Alamogordo: Visit the Trinity Site
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-6 Hours)
activities.description: Two times a year, visitors are allowed to see the place where history was made at the Trinity Site. Run by the US Army, the Trinity site was the test area for the Gadget, site of the first human-caused nuclear explosion. The Gadget was placed atop a 100-foot (30.48 m) tall steel tower that was designated Ground Zero…

activities.name: See Fort Rosalie
activities.description: Discover how the town of Natchez came to be as you explore Fort Rosalie.

activities.name: Explore the Self-guided Interpretive Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: A short, accessible interpretive trail features bronze figures of the French and Passamaquoddy, as well as displays that discuss historical events and the interaction of the two cultures.

activities.name: Hike to Dumpling Overlook
activities.description: Dumpling Overlook offers expansive panoramic views of Naknek Lake, Brooks River, and Lake Brooks. Visitors also have the option to continue beyond the maintained trail to the summit.

activities.name: Visit National Historic Landmarks in Sitka
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-4 Hours)
activities.description: The historic landmarks in Sitka are portals in time to significant events in Alaska history. Locations of battles and fort sites, churches, schools, military installations and more provide us with a glimpse into the rich and diverse past of Sitka, and its substantial role in Alaskan (and American) history. Use the…

activities.name: Full Moon Hike
activities.basis: estimated from duration (60-120 Minutes)
activities.description: Typically offered year-round at sunset as weather permits. Those planning to join a ranger-led full moon hike at Bryce Canyon National Park can make reservations online via Recreation.gov. Tickets for each month’s hike are released in two phases, 14 and 5 days in advance.

activities.name: Join a Star Party
activities.description: Gaze at the heavens with the National Park Service and the Shenandoah Astronomical Society (SAS). Telescopes are provided, or you may bring your own. SAS members can teach you how to use it. Bring camp chairs or blankets.

activities.name: Moro Rock
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-120 Minutes)
activities.description: A stone and concrete stairway leads to the top of Moro Rock, a granite dome that towers over the Generals Highway. From the top, enjoy sweeping views of the hills below and the wilderness to the east.

activities.name: Hike High Peaks to Bear Gulch Loop
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: East Side Trails, Strenuous Hikes, Loop Hike

activities.name: Drive to Williams Ranch
activities.description: If you have a high-clearance, four wheel drive vehicle, the primitive dirt road to Williams Ranch provides a unique opportunity to get off the beaten path and get close to the remote and imposing western escarpment of the Guadalupe Mountains.

activities.name: Rapids Bridge Hike
activities.description: This 2-mile loop hike takes you through the forest and then parallels scenic Rock Creek before heading back uphill.

activities.name: Visit the 56 Signers of the Declaration of Independence Memorial
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30 Minutes)
activities.description: As you walk through Constitution Gardens, walk across the footbridge to Signers Island. The stones of the Memorial to the 56 Signers of the Declaration of Independence could have been tombstones had events turned out differently. Celebrate these men of courage and vision at our nation's founding by paying homage to…

activities.name: Whiteoak Falls (Upper)
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: MILE 42.6 | This challenging hike to cascades and waterfalls has been popular since the early days of Skyland Resort. This particular hike goes to the upper falls before returning.

activities.name: Take a Self-Guided Walking Tour of Minidoka
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-120 Minutes)
activities.description: Minidoka National Historic Site offers 1.6 miles (2.5 km) of gravel walking trails. Visitors may explore the site and the exteriors of historic structures at their own pace. Educational exhibits are placed along the trail to provide information.

activities.name: Ride a Horse on the Rift Zone Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-4 Hours)

activities.description: Come together at Fort Monroe each August to commemorate the landing of the first enslaved Africans in Virginia. Their historic arrival still has a profound impact on the United States and its people.

activities.name: Fishing at Curecanti
activities.description: Fishing is allowed along the Gunnison River and all three reservoirs of Curecanti National Recreation Area. All Colorado State fishing regulations apply.

activities.name: Behold the Granite Mountains
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: A paved pullout about seven miles north of Highway 40 on Kelbaker Road allows visitors to park their cars and enjoy the view of the Granite Mountains. There is parking for five vehicles at a time. This is a great location to catch a sunset or to have a leisurely tailgate picnic.

activities.name: View the Night Sky at Split Mountain
activities.description: Dinosaur has been recognized as an International Dark Sky Park by the International Dark Skies Association. Much of the monument provides opportunities to view the night skies. The Split Mountain Campground has a designated night sky viewing area and is where the monument hosts night sky viewing programs.

activities.name: Hike the Hog Canyon Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: 1.5 miles (2.4 km) round trip, out and back trail. Easy. The Hog Canyon Trail is a pleasant hike into a box canyon near the Josie Morris Cabin. The trail is relatively flat and shaded, typically good for small children. Keep kids close, and watch for poison ivy. No pets allowed.

activities.name: Hike the Bunchgrass Prairie Nature Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (0-1 Hours)
activities.description: The Bunchgrass Prairie Trail is located at Spring Canyon Campground and Day Use Area. Hike along this trail to learn more about native plants in the channeled scabland ecosystem.

activities.name: Hike Grand Portage Trails
activities.description: Hike the Mount Rose Trail for stunning views of Grand Portage Bay and the Depot. To experience the trek the Voyageurs made as well as Indigenous people before them, hike a portion or all of Gitchi Onagamiing, the Grand Portage Trail.

activities.name: Picnic at Fort Dupont
activities.description: Enjoy a relaxing picnic at Fort Dupont Park. There are three picnic shelters that can be reserved through recreation.gov. Individual picnic tables and benches are also available without reservations. Come relax and get away from the stresses of everyday life. You may also bring a blanket and sit out in an open field…

activities.name: Hike Curecanti Creek Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (2-3 Hours)
activities.description: After descending from the high rim of the Upper Black Canyon of the Gunnison, the trail follows Curecanti Creek as it descends toward Morrow Point Reservoir.

activities.name: Hike to Abrams Falls
activities.description: Walk 5 miles (8 km) roundtrip through rhododendron, hemlock, and pine-oak forest to a 25-foot (7.6-m) waterfall and scenic pool. Swimming in the pool is not recommended due to slippery rocks and a dangerous undertow.

activities.name: Exploring The Brices Cross Roads Battlefield
activities.description: The Brices Cross Roads National Battlefield was established in February of 1929 with the intention of preserving 1 acre in commemoration of the battle. Since then the Brice’s Crossroads National Battlefield Commission has purchased 1600 acres of the hallowed ground and with the help of the Civil War Trust and local…

activities.name: Self-Guided Walking Tour of Plains, Georgia
activities.basis: estimated from duration (45-120 Minutes)
activities.description: A Self-Guided Tour of Plains, Georgia allowing the visitor to explore the town that raised a President, and where President and Mrs. Carter still call home.

activities.name: Mary McLeod Bethune Council House NHS Bookstore
activities.description: Visitors can purchase educational products and books related to Mary McLeod Bethune, the National Council of Negro Women, the Civil Rights Movement, and Women's History.

activities.name: Be a Junior Ranger at San Francisco Maritime National Historical Park
activities.description: While in the park, younger visitors can pick up a free Junior Ranger Program activity booklet at three contact stations: the Visitor Center, Maritime Museum, or the Ticket Booth on Hyde Street Pier.

activities.name: Become a Craters Junior Ranger
activities.description: Earn your Junior Ranger badge for Craters of the Moon while learning about the park by completing this fun activity book.

activities.name: Hike Porters Creek Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-3 Hours)
activities.description: Porters Creek is a peaceful trail that is filled with history and natural wonders, hike as far as you'd like to explore. If you are up for about a 4-mile roundtrip hike you can visit the beautiful Fern Branch Falls.

activities.name: Hike Kabetogama Lake Overlook Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: This short handicap accessible trail takes you through a pine forest to a viewpoint where you can sit on a bench and see Kabetogama Lake framed by the trees.

activities.name: Take a Lighthouse Cruise
activities.description: Cruise Boston’s outer harbor to learn about navigational aids in Boston and the uses of the islands over time.

activities.name: Tidepooling at Ship Harbor
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Explore tidepooling opportunities on the rocky shoreline off this easy figure-8 coastal forest trail.

activities.name: Paddle Through a Cypress Slough
activities.basis: estimated from duration (4-6 Hours)
activities.description: Paddle from one river to another through a cypress slough! Explore quiet oxbow lakes and bayous along the way on this 4.8-mile paddling trail.

activities.name: Locomotive Ranger Programs
activities.description: Golden Spike National Historical Park is home to the steam locomotives Jupiter and No. 119. These are replicas of the originals that met at Promontory Summit on May 10th, 1869 for the wedding of the rails ceremony. Locomotive Ranger Programs are given throughout the summer starting May 1st and ending in late September.

activities.name: Horseback Riding at Indiana Dunes
activities.description: Enjoy an equestrian ride through ancient dune formations on the Glenwood Dunes Trails system. These trails are the only horseback trails and you must bring your own horse. The trail is host to almost 15 miles of interconnected loops. Be sure to bring a map as there are 13 junctions interconnecting the loops.

activities.name: Check-out a Junior Ranger Discovery Pack
activities.description: Families and groups with children can borrow a free Discovery Pack from the Malaquite Visitor Center to explore Padre Island. Each pack includes an activity guide, field guides, binoculars, magnifiers, and more.

activities.name: Alley Slough Trail
activities.description: Alley Slough Trail

activities.name: Fishing at the Castle Rocks Fish Pond
activities.description: Besides fishing, the pond is also a great place to watch birds and wildlife. There is a walking path, benches to sit and enjoy the scenery, as well as a picnic table and fire ring.

activities.name: Hike to Divide Meadow
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Stroll through a forest of towering Douglas fir trees and along a shaded creek on this family-friendly hike to Divide Meadow. This hike begins at the Bear Valley Trailhead, at the south end of the Bear Valley Parking Lot.

activities.name: Become an Organ Pipe Junior Ranger
activities.description: Become a Junior Ranger at Organ Pipe Cactus National Monument.

activities.name: Bike the Nauset Bike Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Get ready to explore! The Nauset Bike Trail offers a variety of environments to explore along nearly 2 miles of paved trail. Explore wooded ponds and sandy beaches!

activities.name: Hike the Battlefields
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-8 Hours)
activities.description: Explore trails at Fredericksburg and Spotsylvania National Military Park and experience the battlefields up close.

activities.name: Become a New Bedford Junior Ranger
activities.description: Welcome to New Bedford Whaling National Historical Park’s Junior Ranger program! The park is excited to have you become a steward and help continue to preserve and protect your national parks. At this park, you have two options for how to become an official Junior Ranger as well as earn other types of badges.

activities.name: Hike Pole Canyon
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Hike the Pole Canyon trail, moseying by streams, wildflowers, and dense conifers. The 6.6 mile round trip trail also treks through the Baker Creek and Grey Cliffs campgrounds, making it easy to start from a campsite without a drive.

activities.name: Bike the Mohawk River or the Erie Canal
activities.description: The Erie Canal Trail stretches across New York State. In Rome, NY, you can tour the heart of it and see its largest feeder river, the Mohawk. This smaller section of trail offers scenic views of the land as it was before the modern era.

activities.name: Hike Pemetic Summit with Island Explorer Bus
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The hike up and over Pemetic takes hikers to the shores of both Bubble and Jordan Pond and summits Pemetic Mountain. Nearly 360-degree views look out over Cadillac, Sargent and Penobscot peaks, the Atlantic Ocean and the Cranberry Isles. Hiking this peak with use of the Island Explorer Bus offers hikers a…

activities.name: Fish the East Fork Headwaters
activities.description: Hike or bike the Rincon Trail to the East Fork headwaters, where wild rainbow trout and browns predominate.

activities.name: Camel Trail
activities.description: A 200 yard dirt and gravel trail that allows you to enjoy nature at Waco Mammoth National Monument.

activities.name: Explore the Washington's Wartime Family Exhibit
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Explore the motivations and decisions of General George Washington and learn about the people that made up Washington's military family during the Valley Forge encampment in this museum exhibit, located in the Historic Valley Forge Station near Washington's Headquarters.

activities.name: Visiting Fort Polk
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30 Minutes)
activities.description: When the U.S. army arrived in the Rio Grande delta in March 1846, General Taylor’s first stop was to establish a base that would allow him to receive reinforcements and materiel. He selected the Mexican settlement known as El Frontón de Santa Isabel.

activities.name: Hanford: Explore Howard Amon Park
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Serving as a community gathering place for over 100 years, Howard Amon Park offers something for everyone. You can relax under a shade tree, wade into the river, walk or ride a bike along the river path, and enjoy family time with your kids on the play equipment.

activities.name: Make Your First Stop at the Visitor Center
activities.description: Start at the Visitor Center, where park rangers and volunteers can help plan your visit.

activities.name: Visit the Cabrillo Tidepools
activities.description: Learn about visiting the tidepools at Cabrillo National Monument!

activities.name: Hike To Barnard Mountain
activities.basis: estimated from duration (2-4 Hours)
activities.description: Hike to the top of 1,558ft Barnard Mountain for a magnificent and expansive viewpoint of Katahdin Lake and Mt. Katahdin.

activities.name: Become a MNRR Junior Ranger
activities.description: Do you care about exploring, learning about, and protecting the Missouri River? If yes, become a Junior Ranger! There are many ways to earn a Junior Ranger badge at Missouri National Recreational River, and this fun activity book is a great place to start. This booklet includes activities like crosswords, drawings…

activities.name: Alcove House
activities.description: Learn about the hike and ladder-climb at Bandelier's Alcove House.

activities.name: Fort to Sea Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (3-6 Hours)
activities.description: The Fort To Sea Trail starts at the Fort Clatsop Visitor Center then takes you up a gentle climb to the top of Clatsop Ridge, where on a clear day you can see to the Pacific Ocean. From there, descend through deep woods and reach wooded pasture dotted with small lakes. The wooded pasture leads to gentle dunes that…

activities.name: Become an Oxon Hill Farm Junior Ranger
activities.description: Oxon Hill Farm Junior Ranger Program

activities.name: Relax in the Picnic Area!
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Relax in the shade of coconut trees as you enjoy the picturesque setting of the Puʻuhonua o Hōnaunau picnic area. Bring your whole ʻohana (family) for a beach picnic and make memories as you explore in the shallow tide pools in the lava rock. Watch for a "green flash" as the sun sinks below the horizon and a rainbow…

activities.name: Mountain Bike Fort Dupont!
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Mountain bike in metropolitan D.C.! Approximately 10 miles of easy to moderate biking trails meander through the Anacostia area of Washington D.C. The trails traverse through the Civil War defensive sites used to protect the city in the early 1860s. Some of the hills are challenging and bikes with wide tires are…

activities.name: Crater Rim Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-6 Hours)
activities.description: Catch views of Kīlauea caldera, feel the breath of the volcano at Steaming Bluff (Wahinekapu), and walk through lush rainforest.

activities.name: Pacific Historic Parks - Bookstore
activities.description: A bookstore and gift shop where visitors can purchase Pearl Harbor memorabilia.

activities.name: Muir Woods Birdwatching
activities.description: Birdwatching in Muir Woods

activities.name: West Mountain Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-60 Minutes)
activities.description: Both sections of West Mountain Trail have gradual change in elevation. Note: West Mountain Trail can be made into a loop by using Mountain Top Trail (elevation change: 400 feet in this section).

activities.name: Climb the Saratoga Monument
activities.basis: estimated from duration (15 Minutes)
activities.description: This 155-foot stone obelisk was built in the last quarter of the 19th century to commemorate the American victory in the Battles of Saratoga. Visitors may climb up its 188 steps to take in amazing views of the surrounding area, with up to 30+ mile visibility on clear days.

activities.name: Brown's Farm Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The Brown's Farm Trail is a mostly flat, half-mile loop trail that passes through several different forest ecosystems and the remains of an early 1900s farmstead.

activities.name: Dark Hollow Falls
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Dark Hollow Falls Parking Area (mile 50.7) | Pets are not allowed on this hike. This hike follows a stream to a beautiful waterfall, and is one of the Park’s most traveled trails. The trail is short, but very steep and rocky and the return hike is challenging!

activities.name: Hike the Rift Zone Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-4 Hours)
activities.description: Explore the floor of a valley that follows the San Andreas Fault, passing through meadows and woods between Bear Valley and Five Brooks. This hike can begin at either the Bear Valley Trailhead or the Five Brooks Trailhead. Allow about 10 minutes to drive from Bear Valley to Five Brooks.

activities.name: Sledding & Snowplay in the Manzanita Lake Area
activities.description: Sled a wintery slope, build a snowman, or otherwise enjoy Lassen's winter wonderland at the Manzanita Lake area. Got snow?

activities.name: Be A CHAT Junior Ranger
activities.description: by the Island Ford Visitor Center to pick up your Junior Ranger Booklet and get to work on becoming the next park's Junior Ranger.

activities.name: See the Exhibits at the Great Basin Visitor Center
activities.description: Great Basin Visitor Center exhibits

activities.name: Harbor to Hills Section 2: Hike from Three Mile to Daisy Farm
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1 Day)
activities.description: Hike along the Rock Harbor Trail from Three Mile to Daisy Farm and enjoy views of Rock Harbor Channel, Rock Harbor Lighthouse, and Edisen Fishery. Mileage: About 4.2 miles

activities.name: Hike to Mount Wittenberg from the Sky Trailhead
activities.basis: estimated from duration (2-3 Hours)
activities.description: This hike provides the easiest route to Mount Wittenberg, the highest point on the Point Reyes Peninsula at 1407 feet (426 meters) in elevation. Allow ten minutes driving time from Bear Valley to the Sky Trailhead, which is located along Limantour Road.

activities.name: Hanford: Hike the White Bluffs South Slope Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (6-8 Hours)
activities.description: This trail provides one of the best views of the old Hanford town site and location of the Hanford construction camp for the Manhattan Project. This trail will reward you with expansive views of the Hanford site and opportunities to explore the white bluffs geologic formation up-close. This is also an excellent trail…

activities.name: Boy Scout Trail Zone Backpacking
activities.basis: estimated from duration (2-15 Days)
activities.description: Experience Joshua Tree National Park's wilderness by backpacking along the Boy Scout Trail.

activities.name: Explore the Rugged Lance Rosier Unit
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The Lance Rosier Unit is the largest, wildest area of the Big Thicket. Discover its secrets on this scenic, unpaved auto tour.

activities.name: Hike Willow Hole
activities.basis: estimated from duration (3-5 Hours)
activities.description: Enjoy a scenic hike into the Wonderland of Rocks.

activities.name: Hiking at Friendship Hill
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-300 Minutes)
activities.description: Friendship Hill National Historic Site has ten miles of hiking trails to explore. You can walk to Gallatin House on the knoll and back in 15 minutes, or hike for hours through woods and meadows.

activities.name: Ride the Historic Dentzel Carousel
activities.description: The Dentzel Carousel is operated by our partner, the Glen Echo Park Partnership for Arts and Culture.

activities.name: Historic Fort Self-Guided Tour
activities.basis: estimated from duration (20-60 Minutes)
activities.description: A self-guided room tour guide can be found inside the park brochure or provided by a ranger upon entry to the park.

activities.name: Knob Mountain - Jeremys Run
activities.basis: estimated from duration (7-8 Hours)
activities.description: Elkwallow Wayside (mile 24) | This hike goes around a beautiful area of the Park featuring one of the most picturesque streams in Shenandoah. The majority of this hike is in the Shenandoah Wilderness.

activities.name: South Slough Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The South Slough Trail is a three mile loop that can be accessed from the Fort to Sea Trailhead or from near the North Netul Landing that features twist and turns and steep changes in elevation among large trees and a boardwalk over the Colewort Creek restoration area.

activities.name: Explore the park on Horseback
activities.description: Mammoth Cave National Park is an exceptional destination for anyone who loves to see the world from the back of a horse.

activities.name: Picnic at 33 Hole Overlook
activities.description: Enjoy a picnic with panoramic views of the Las Vegas Bay and the Black Mesa. 33 Hole Overlook Picnic area features 9 picnic tables, 9 grills, and restrooms. This location does not have drinking water.

activities.name: Become a Mammoth Cave Junior Ranger
activities.description: Do you want to explore, learn about, and protect Mammoth Cave? If so, become a Mammoth Cave Junior Ranger! The Junior Ranger activity book is appropriate for all ages and is a great way to get more in-depth knowledge about the world’s longest cave and to learn about the natural wonders of the park.

activities.name: Fish San Antonio Creek
activities.description: San Antonio Creek is famous throughout New Mexico for wild brown trout and beautiful scenery. Reserve your backcountry vehicle pass to fish this stream seasonally from May 15 - November 15.

activities.name: Thomas Condon Overlook Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (5-20 Minutes)
activities.description: This 0.25 mi (0.4 km) long trail starts at the far end of the Thomas Condon Visitor Center parking lot and ends at an overlook of the river valley.

activities.name: Bicycle Confluence to Big Savage Mountain
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Days)
activities.description: To reach Big Savage Mountain on the Eastern Continental Divide loop, bicycle 46 miles from Confluence (GAP Mile 61.3) to Frostburg (GAP Mile 15.5) on the Great Allegheny Passage, then 8+ miles on-road to the northern trailhead for the Big Savage Mountain Trail. While on the GAP, on your way to Frostburg, you will…

activities.name: Exploring the Meriwether Lewis Death and Burial Site
activities.description: The Meriwether Lewis monument marks the final resting place of famed American explorer Meriwether Lewis who died by suicide near by at Grinder's Stand on October 11, 1809.

activities.name: The Narrows
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The Narrows is a strenuous hike that follows the Virgin River through a narrow slot canyon. After 1 mile (0.6 km) on the easy, paved Riverside Walk, head down a set of stairs and into the river. The rest of your hike will take place in the Virgin River, where the flow rate can change day by day and the streambed is…

activities.name: See Crater Rim Drive and Chain of Craters Road
activities.description: Drive the two primary roads in the park for a scenic adventure through a dynamic geological and cultural landscape

activities.name: Chimney Rock
activities.basis: estimated from duration (2-3 Hours)
activities.description: Riprap Parking Area (mile 90) | An out-and-back hike into the Shenandoah Wilderness ending at Chimney Rock, an excellent viewpoint with some very interesting geological features.

activities.name: Hike the Cecil Cove Loop
activities.basis: estimated from duration (5-8 Hours)
activities.description: This 7-mile loop winds through the wooded valley following Cecil Creek. The trail crosses Cecil Creek 5 times in the first 2 miles, so it may not be passable during rainy season due to high water. The Cecil Cove Loop passes old home sites, historic cemeteries, and provides beautiful scenic views during leaf-off…

activities.name: Riprap - Wildcat Ridge
activities.basis: estimated from duration (8-9 Hours)
activities.description: MILE 90 or 92.1 | This loop can be hiked from Riprap Parking or Wildcat Ridge Parking. It takes you through the forests of the Shenandoah Wilderness and over several stream crossings, while offering beautiful views of the hollows and valley to the west and north.

activities.name: Hike Skyline Vista Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Skyline Vista Trail is a great accessible introduction to Theodore Roosevelt National Park.

activities.name: Fishing at Fort Pulaski
activities.description: Information about fishing in the waterways around Fort Pulaski National Monument.

activities.name: Hike the Desert Voices Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: 1.7 miles (2.7 km) round trip loop trail. Moderate difficulty. The Desert Voices Trail starts at Split Mountain. It wanders through valleys and over rocky outcrops, offering dramatic views of the surrounding landscape. No pets allowed.

activities.name: Discover Our Partnership Parks
activities.basis: estimated from duration (120-500 Minutes)
activities.description: The power of working together is on display in this park partnership area which offers more than any one unit could provide. The 7 Creeks Recreation Area is managed by state, local, non-profit organizations, and federal agencies.

activities.name: Shoot Winter Photography at Fort Falls
activities.duration: Walking to the Fort Falls from the parking lot may take about 5 minutes, but along the way you will crossover the stream that feeds the falls and see the forest canopies at all levels as you travel down to the base of the waterfall. You can take as much or as little time to photograph these phenomena of nature as you would like.
activities.description: See the Niobrara River in the light of a winter lens. Photographers can find winter scenery, natural phenomena's, wildlife, canyons, waterfalls, and the perfect angles for those golden hour photos in many places along the Niobrara River, but Fort Falls is one of our favorites.

activities.name: Explore the Civil War Defenses of Washington Hiker-Biker Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-5 Hours)
activities.description: Hike or bike the 7-mile trail from Fort Stanton to Fort Mahan and take in scenery that ranges from urban greenspaces to forest ecosystems, all while recreating through a historic landscape.

activities.name: Self-Guided Tours - Historic Sites
activities.description: The City of Richmond, California houses multiple sites that are of historical significance to the WWII Home Front. Many of the old buildings and sites can only be viewed from the street. The park can help describe any buildings or sites that are of interest.

activities.name: Hiking Interdune Boardwalk
activities.basis: estimated from duration (15-30 Minutes)
activities.description: The Interdune Boardwalk is an elevated boardwalk that leads you through the fragile interdune area to a scenic view of the dune field and the Sacramento mountains.

activities.name: Fountain Freight Road Bike Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (2-4 Hours)
activities.description: Six miles north of Old Faithful, bikes are allowed on the Fountain Freight Road, an old dirt and gravel road now closed to autos.

activities.name: Drive Park Loop Road
activities.description: Wind your way through forests, past lakes and mountains, and along the shoreline on scenic Park Loop Road. The 27-mile (43 km) road also provides access to popular areas such as Sieur de Monts, Sand Beach, Otter Point, Jordan Pond, and Cadillac Mountain.

activities.name: About Hiking Safety
activities.description: Hiking Safety

activities.name: Ranger Talks
activities.description: Ranger talks are scheduled on most days from April through September.

activities.name: Drive the Yampa Bench Road
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The 18 mile (29 km) unpaved Yampa Bench Road offers visitors a look into the quieter side of Dinosaur. Running along a "bench" of land high above the Yampa River, visitors can experience incredible views and historic sites. High-clearance, four-wheel-drive (4WD) vehicles are strongly recommended for this rugged road…

activities.name: Visit Adney Gap
activities.description: Take a scenic drive through Adney Gap around milepost 136 and experience one of the many mountain gaps that provided an important early tool in traversing the surrounding hills and mountains.

activities.name: Swamp Canyon Loop
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Swamp Canyon appears relatively small and sheltered from the overlook, allowing the viewer to develop a more intimate connection with the landscape than some of the grander viewpoints in the park. The Swamp Canyon Loop, which starts at the viewpoint, is more rugged than the Bryce Amphitheater trails, taking hikers…

activities.name: Spend the Night in the Mount Pisgah Campground
activities.description: The Mount Pisgah Campground is a cool, high elevation retreat in the summer's heat. This peaceful and relaxing spot is the perfect place to stay and explore the southern end of the Blue Ridge Parkway.

activities.name: Nicholson Hollow
activities.basis: estimated from duration (6-7 Hours)
activities.description: PARK BOUNDARY | An alternate option for visitors with pets who still wish to hike from the Old Rag parking area. This hike takes you through the Shenandoah Wilderness to Corbin Cabin, an old homesite built by a former resident, and features several stream crossings along the way.

activities.name: Teton Park Road in Winter
activities.description: The Teton Park Road is open to skiing, snowshoeing and walking during winter from Taggart Lake Trailhead to the Signal Mountain Lodge. Located along the base of the Teton Range it offering stellar views. The road is closed to vehicles November 1 to April 30.

activities.name: Salt Basin Dunes Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-3 Hours)
activities.description: The white gypsum sands of the Salt Basin Dunes rise 100 feet from the desert floor and provide a brilliant contrast to the dark, towering cliffs of the Guadalupe Mountains. From the trailhead, follow the trail to the gypsum sand dune field with excellent views of the western escarpment of the Guadalupe Mountains…

activities.name: Hike Civil War Skirmish Lines at Harpers Ferry
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Did you know the park has over 20 miles of hiking trails? The trails vary from easy, riverside strolls to four-mile hikes across Civil War battlefields to eight-mile adventures on the tops of mountains.

activities.name: Hear the Centennial Bell Ring
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-5 Minutes)
activities.description: Do you hear that? Look up! Listen to the Centennial Bell ring each hour at the clocktower of Independence Hall.

activities.name: Tent Camping
activities.description: Catoctin Mountain has multiple traditional camping options for various group sizes.

activities.name: Hike the Tobin Harbor Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (2-4 Hours)
activities.description: The Tobin Harbor Trail connects the Mount Franklin Trail to Rock Harbor. This easygoing route is preferred amongst backpackers compared to the Rock Harbor Trail. Mileage: About 3 miles

activities.name: Camp on the Boston Harbor Islands
activities.description: Experience the ultimate urban escape with an overnight camping stay on the Boston Harbor Islands!

activities.name: Old North Church: Prince's Pet Pursuit Family Activity
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Explore Old North through a scavenger hunt narrated by Prince, the friendly North End cat who used to frequent the church.

activities.name: Hike the Emigrant Trail
activities.description: The Emigrant Trail roughly parallels visible remnants of the Oregon Trail, capturing some of the experience of mid-1800s emigrants moving West.

activities.name: Hike the Sentinel Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: Located at Fort Spokane, this self-guided trail navigates to trailside markers telling the story of the people who lived and worked here in the late 1800s. For the adventurous, take the Bluff Trail 300 feet to the top of the bluff, with spectacular views of the fort grounds and the confluence of the rivers.

activities.name: Bike the Golden Gate Bridge
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-4 Hours)
activities.description: Bike the Golden Gate Bridge!

activities.name: Hike the Estero Trail to Drakes Head or Sunset Beach
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-7 Hours)
activities.description: This trail through grassland and cattle pastures offers outstanding views of Drakes Estero and Estero de Limantour, and the opportunity to see the birds, bat rays, and leopard sharks that call these ecosystems home. Allow 25 minutes driving time from Bear Valley to the Estero Trailhead.

activities.name: Visit the Holzwarth Historic Site
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Take a step back in time at the Holzwarth Historic Site, the spot where the Never Summer Ranch, Holzwarth Trout Lodge, and family homestead was operated by the Holzwarth family for multiple generations from the 1910s to the 1970's. The Holzwarth Historic Site is located on the West Side of Rocky Mountain National Park…

activities.name: Learn About the Fur Trade and the Colorful Voyageurs
activities.description: Voyageurs, North Men and Montrealers, made up the bulk of the fur trade employees at Grand Portage. These hardy souls would spend weeks to months in the wilderness transporting trade goods to remote posts either in canoes or on their backs.

activities.name: Hike To Orin Falls
activities.basis: estimated from duration (3-6 Hours)
activities.description: Hike to Orin Falls for a magnificent view of a cascading waterfall.

activities.description: Enjoy a ranger-guided tour of the birthplace and home to the nation's 27th President and 10th Chief Justice of the U.S. Supreme Court. activities.name: Find Flowers and Butterflies in Lucy's Garden
activities.description: New Philadelphia buzzes to life in Lucy’s Butterfly Garden! The wildflowers in this garden represent the types of plants that greeted the McWorters when they arrived. Today, bright flowers greet many native butterflies, moths, and bees.

activities.name: Passport Stamps at Bering Land Bridge

activities.name: Navajo Loop Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: The iconic Navajo Loop Trail begins and ends at Sunset Point. Its switchbacks wind between narrow walls of colorful limestone with views of towering Douglas-fir trees and the park's most famous hoodoo: Thor's hammer. The loop has two sides: Two Bridges and Wall Street. The Two Bridges side is open year-round, however…

activities.name: Visit the Furnace Creek Visitor Center
activities.description: Stop by the visitor center to speak with park rangers and pay park fees and purchase national park passes. View the exhibits about Death Valley's history and natural wonders. activities.name: Discover Sheep Creek Cascade
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: Visit Cedar Grove, in the heart of Kings Canyon. Once there, take a hike through a forested ravine to a shady glen and a small cascading waterfall called Sheep Creek Cascade. You’ll also see views of the Monarch Divide.

activities.name: Go Birding at New Philadelphia
activities.description: Birds provide a living link to the past in New Philadelphia. Forest and field habitats continue to shelter many species that graced – and inspired – the McWorters. Bring your binoculars and your ears to look and listen for Eastern Meadowlarks, Sandhill Cranes, Bald Eagles, and more.

activities.name: Discover the Valley's African American History
activities.description: Talks and presentations uncover emerging discoveries and stories of enslaved and free African Americans. These stories help us uncover a rich and inclusive cultural history of the Shenandoah Valley.

activities.name: Hike Deep Creek Trail to Indian Creek Falls
activities.description: Hike 1.6 miles (2.6 km) roundtrip along Deep Creek, which features views of two waterfalls, Tom Branch Falls and Indian Creek Falls.

activities.description: The most technical section of Buffalo National River, Boxley to Ponca is recommended only for highly-experienced whitewater paddlers. Water levels on this section tend to rise and fall rapidly, so paddlers must have a solid understanding of reading river gauges to properly time their float.

activities.name: Hike Beaver Pond Overlook Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (10-30 Minutes)
activities.description: A short uphill hike through an aspen and pine forest leads to a rocky outcrop high above a beaver pond. Although beavers are no longer active at this pond, this trail provides great birding opportunities, and the possibility of spotting large wildlife.

activities.name: Trail of Fossils
activities.basis: estimated from duration (10-35 Minutes)
activities.description: The Trail of Fossils is 0.25 mi (0.4 km) long and is the best trail in the monument to see real fossils. Look for leaf imprints and pieces of wood within the boulders that have fallen from the cliffs. No collecting is allowed and please stay on trail.

activities.name: Disc Golf at Castle Rocks
activities.description: With the dramatic Castle Rocks landscape in the backdrop, this small three-hole disc golf course is fun for all ages and abilities. activities.name: Riverside Walk
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The Riverside Walk is a relatively flat and paved trail in the northern end of Zion Canyon. This easy trail follows the Virgin River as the sheer sandstone walls narrow in around you. activities.name: Visit the Wayside: Home of Authors, Wed & Sun, July 5 - Sept 5, 2026
activities.description: Explore this unique home, witness to over 300 years of history! From revolutionary patriots to famous authors, the Wayside has played host to many influential thinkers in American History. Guided tours at 1:00, 2:00, 3:00 and 4:00 pm.

activities.description: Kurtzman Park is a community park that was created in the late 1950s by Black neighborhood boys in segregated East Pasco who wanted a place to play. activities.name: Visit the Small Space Gardening Exhibit

activities.description: While the Roosevelts had a plenty of space for an expansive garden, the small space garden exhibit demonstrates different systems for gardening with whatever space you have available. The designs displayed here address the common challenges faced when gardening and provide sensible solutions for the home grower. With…

activities.name: Hike the Lost Valley Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The Lost Valley Trail is an easy to moderate hike through a box canyon sculpted by Clark Creek. At 2.4 miles round-trip, this trail features caves, waterfalls, a Native American bluff shelter, and breathtaking groves of American beech trees.

activities.name: Become a Jr. Ranger at Pearl Harbor National Memorial
activities.description: This program is a wonderful way to connect and engage children with the often complex themes and issues presented at Pearl Harbor National Memorial.

activities.name: Tidepooling at Wonderland
activities.description: Explore rocky tidepools at the far end of this coastal forest trail on the west side of Mount Desert Island.

activities.name: Interpretive Exhibits
activities.description: Contains a permanent exhibit gallery addressing some of the major events in Ulysses S. Grant's life, and this history of the mausoleum.

activities.name: Blue Spring Trail
activities.description: Blue Spring Trail

activities.name: Horseback Riding at Cowpens National Battlefield
activities.description: Horse Riding Regulations at Cowpens

activities.name: Hike the Inscription Rock Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: This 0.75 mile (1.2 km) trail takes you to the pool and past hundreds of Spanish and American inscriptions, and prehistorical petroglyphs. The trail is paved and the main 1/2 mile loop is wheelchair-accessible with assistance. This is a great option if you have an hour or less to spend at the park. It must be started…

activities.name: Bike the Estero Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-3 Hours)
activities.description: This trail through grassland and cattle pastures offers outstanding views of Drakes Estero and Estero de Limantour, and the opportunity to see the birds, bat rays, and leopard sharks that call these ecosystems home. Allow 25 minutes driving time from Bear Valley to the Estero Trailhead.

activities.name: Explore the Moore Homestead
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The Moore Homestead was established 10 years before the gold rush. Today, contemplate early frontier life in the wilds of remote Alaska as you explore the first building in Skagway and the first family to live here.

activities.name: Hike Crystal Creek Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (2-3 Hours)
activities.description: Winding through abundant wildflowers, Gambel oak, aspens, conifers and a recovering burn area, Crystal Creek Trail is ideal for spring or fall hiking.

activities.name: Drive to Dog Canyon
activities.description: Dog Canyon, the park's remote north district, is only seven miles as the crow files, but a full two hour drive [one-way] from Pine Springs through a panoramic Chihuahuan Desert and mountain landscape.

activities.name: Bunker Hill: Muskets, Men, and Liberty
activities.description: Listen to a ranger dressed in period clothing discuss why three men from different backgrounds fought in the battle. The program concludes with a musket firing demonstration!

activities.name: Visit Quarai
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-120 Minutes)
activities.description: Visit Quarai

activities.name: Walk to the Monument
activities.description: Explore Big Kill Devil Hill and climb to Wright Brothers Monument.

activities.name: Strenuous Hike Across the Crater Floor
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Experienced hikers can "thru" hike the crater from Keoneheʻeheʻe (Sliding Sands) Trailhead, across the crater floor, and out to Halemauʻu Trailhead. This hike is extremely strenuous and should only be undertaken by individuals who are equipped for a wilderness environment.

activities.name: See the Pacific at Cape Disappointment
activities.basis: estimated from duration (2-4 Hours)
activities.description: It was at the base of Cape Disappointment that the Corps of Discovery achieved their principal mission of traveling across the continent to the Pacific Ocean. Eleven expedition members led by William Clark surveyed the area, fulfilling President Jefferson’s instructions to the expedition.

activities.name: Hanford: Hike Candy Mountain
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The trail up Candy Mountain is a moderate 3.6 mile (5.8 km) roundtrip hike that offers sweeping views of the Tri-Cities region and a walk through time. Signs along the trail explain the impact of the ice age floods on area geography. Hikers capture sweeping views from the summit, with Mount Adams, Rainier, and Stuart…

activities.name: Harbor to Hills Section 5: Hike from Lake Richie to West Chickenbone
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1 Day)
activities.description: Hike from one interior lake to the next on the Indian Portage Trail. Mileage: About 3.6 miles

activities.name: Glasshouse
activities.description: Visitors can see the remains of the original furnaces used by those early glassblowers and watch as modern glassblowers produce wine bottles, pitchers, candleholders and various other glass objects.

activities.name: Kīlauea Iki Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (2-4 Hours)
activities.description: Descend 400 feet (122 m) through rainforest into a volcanic crater and hike across a hardened lava lake from the 1959 eruption.

activities.name: Hike Goldmine Loop via Tunnel Bypass Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Hike 4 miles (6.4 km) on Lakeshore and Goldmine Loop trails through a hardwood forest filled with signs of old homesites and farms. This trail is moderate but includes some rocky areas and shallow stream crossings.

activities.name: Hunter Peak
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The hike to Hunter Peak is a challenging day hike done as a loop up the Bear Canyon Trail and down the Tejas Trail that provides solitude, stunning views, and opportunities for side trails into the Bowl area.

activities.name: Walk the Tawa Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Enjoy the tranquility of the grassland as the paved trail leads you to scenic Tawa Point. The 1.2-mile one way Tawa Trail is a perfect place to stretch your legs after a long road trip.

activities.name: Drive Foothills Parkway (Cosby to I-40)
activities.description: Drive 5.6 miles (9.01 km) one-way on Foothills Parkway from Cosby to I-40.

activities.name: Watch Crossroads of a Revolution
activities.description: This 22-minute orientation film tells the story of Ninety Six during the 1700s.

activities.name: Opelofa Loop Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (15-30 Minutes)
activities.description: A small loop trail off-shooting from the Opelofa Trail.

activities.name: Hike the Chimney Rock Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (40-90 Minutes)
activities.description: Enjoy spectacular views of Drakes Bay, the Pacific, and, in spring, wildflowers along this open coastal walk. From January through May, look for migratory whales from the point. Allow 45 minutes driving time from Bear Valley to the Chimney Rock Trailhead.

activities.name: Become a Bethune Council House Junior Ranger
activities.description: Come to the site to obtain a Junior Ranger book and complete it. When you complete it, you can mail or email it and a Park Ranger will sign your certificate and mail your official Junior Ranger badge

activities.name: Hike to the Taylor Farm Site
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-120 Minutes)
activities.description: The Taylor Farm site is a short hike from the Turkey Run parking area or parking lot H. While slowly being reclaimed by the forest, this site is a great example of the farms that were once scattered throughout the forest before it became a national park. Though not much evidence of the farm remains, the small meadow…

activities.name: Hiking from Devils Kitchen Picnic Area
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Many incredible hikes begin just inside the East Entrance to the Monument. Choose from short day hikes to longer, more difficult backcountry travel.

activities.name: Hike to Deasey Mountain
activities.basis: estimated from duration (5-8 Hours)
activities.description: Hike to the top of Deasey Mountain for a scenic view of the monument and surrounding region.

activities.name: Picnicking at Chamizal National Memorial
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The rolling landscape of Chamizal National Memorial is the perfect spot to enjoy a picnic with friends and family!

activities.name: Hike to Mount Le Conte on Trillium Gap Trail
activities.description: One of five routes to Mount Le Conte, Trillium Gap Trail to Mount Le Conte is 13 miles (20.9 km) roundtrip and rewards hikers with mountain views, diverse forest, and a waterfall. Near the summit, the best views are at Cliff Top and Myrtle Point, both marked with signs.

activities.name: Hike the Kelso Dunes
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-180 Minutes)
activities.description: Hike the Kelso Dunes

activities.name: Climb the Observation Tower at Round Marsh
activities.basis: estimated from duration (40-90 Minutes)
activities.description: Hike the trails at Theodore Roosevelt Area out to Round Marsh and climb the observation tower to look over the eco-system, bird watch, read the exhibit plaque, or sit and watch the world go by on the St. Johns River.

activities.name: Lehman Caves Tour
activities.description: Lehman Caves Tours

activities.name: Hike the Abbotts Lagoon Trail to the Footbridge
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Take an easy hike that will lead you to a unique coastal lagoon bordered by sand dunes that offers great opportunities for viewing birds and wildflowers. Allow 20 to 25 minutes driving time from Bear Valley to the Abbotts Lagoon Trailhead.

activities.name: Tour the Visitor Center
activities.description: Start your visit to President William Jefferson Clinton Birthplace Home NHS at the park visitor center with exhibits plus a kiosk with digital vignettes of memorable moments in President Clinton's life as well as the renovation of the Birthplace Home. Browse the Jefferson National Parks Association (JNPA) bookstore…

activities.name: Check Out Devils Golf Course
activities.description: An immense area of rock salt eroded by wind and rain into jagged spires. So incredibly serrated that "only the devil could play golf on such rough links." Listen carefully and you'll hear sounds like tiny pops and pings. The sound is literally billions of tiny salt crystals bursting apart as they expand and contract…

activities.name: Hike Arch Canyon
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: One of the most photographed sites along the Ajo Mountain Drive are the double arches carved into the mountains. Walking the easy, relatively flat Arch Canyon trail provides wonderful opportunities to see wildflowers and gaze upon the rhyolite arches.

activities.name: Hike Gorge Path
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Gorge Path follows a narrow, rocky gorge separating Dorr and Cadillac Mountains. It crosses streams, climbs steep, granite steps, and intersects other trails leading to either summit.

activities.name: Meet a Demonstrating Artist
activities.description: Artists demonstrate traditional Tlingit and Haida forms of carving, weaving, beading, and metalworking. Many of the things they create have ceremonial uses.

activities.name: Watch the Sunrise from Pounding Mill Overlook
activities.description: Sunrise on the Blue Ridge Parkway can be an amazing, once-in-a-lifetime experience. Pounding Mill Overlook at Milepost 413 is a great place to welcome the dawn of a new day and appreciate the natural beauty of this special place.

activities.name: Take a Tour of the Poe House
activities.description: Step into author Edgar Allan Poe's world on a ranger-led or self-guided tour of the home where Poe lived from 1843-44.

activities.name: Greenstone Section 2: Hike from Mount Franklin to Mount Ojibway
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1 Day)
activities.description: Travel from one scenic viewpoint to another starting at Mount Franklin, a picturesque overlook along the Greenstone Ridge. Mileage: About 2.8 miles

activities.name: George Washington’s Mount Vernon and Estates
activities.description: Explore George Washington’s iconic Mount Vernon Mansion and Estate.

activities.name: Hike the Rings Loop
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The Rings Loop Trail is a popular 1.5 mile hike that takes you past beautiful scenery and ancient petroglyphs, and up a series of metal rings. This is a moderately difficult hike, and generally flat until the rings climb.

activities.name: Ride a Train
activities.description: Steamtown's seasonal train rides offer a unique National Park experience. Rail experiences include short 30-minute trips exploring the park’s historic railroad yard.

activities.name: Explore the Ridge View Trail, Osceola Loop

activities.name: WNPA Park Store

The trailhead is adjacent to a small parking area with several accessible spaces along Newfound Gap Rd (US 441) near Sugarlands Visitor Center.

activities.name: Ranger-led Programs at Padre Island
activities.description: Discover Padre Island National Seashore with free ranger-led programs like beach walks and deck talks! Explore nature, history, and wildlife while enjoying the Gulf shoreline or chatting over coffee with a ranger. Check the NPS App or visitor center for schedules and pop-up events.

activities.name: Historic Quarry Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: This 2.5 mile (4 km) loop trail provides an overview of the geology and paleontology of the park and surrounding area.

activities.name: Hanford: Bike and Walk the Sacagawea Heritage Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-4 Hours)
activities.description: This recreational trail along the Columbia River is a perfect way to explore the Tri-Cities on foot and bike. You can also take in panoramic views of the Columbia River, which was…

activities.name: Discover Fort Monroe's African American Heritage

activities.description: Immerse yourself in over four hundred years of African American history. That story begins in 1619 with the arrival of the first enslaved Africans at Old Point Comfort. It continued through the age of slavery and abolition, and into the 2000s.

activities.name: Hike Boicourt Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: This short hike, with its elevated perspective and accessible trail, offers a unique view of the Little Missouri Badlands that the whole family can enjoy.

activities.name: Hoodoo Geology Talk

activities.name: Become a Minidoka Junior Ranger!
activities.description: Become a Minidoka Junior Ranger and earn a special badge or patch! Junior Ranger booklets offer opportunities for visitors of all ages to explore and help protect this important chapter in American history.

activities.name: Picnicking at Fort Vancouver National Historic Site
activities.description: Enjoy a picnic on the grounds of Fort Vancouver National Historic Site. There are several picnic areas in the park, which are open from dawn to dusk.

activities.name: Explore the Little Free Library
activities.description: During your visit to the park, stop by the Little Free Library to grab a book and donate your old ones.

activities.name: Grand Avenue Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (10-20 Minutes)
activities.description: Grand Avenue Trail connects Oertel Trail with Grand Avenue. A local motel lies just south of the trailhead.

activities.name: Birdwatching at Kaloko-Honokōhau
activities.description: Grab your binoculars and set out on a birdwatching adventure along the Kona coastline. See the vibrant yellow saffron finch, hear the boisterous calls of the common Myna, and watch as the ʻAukuʻu (black crowned night heron) slightly stalks its prey.

activities.name: Explore Waterfalls from Longmire to Paradise
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: This tour is a great opportunity to see four of Mount Rainier's stunning waterfalls between Longmire and Paradise without taking on any long or strenuous trails.

activities.name: Hike to Mount Le Conte on Bullhead Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: One of five routes to Mount Le Conte, the Bullhead Trail offers consistent views. The strenuous hike is 13.6 miles (21.9 km) roundtrip. Near the beginning, visitors will see rocky cliffs and climb the Bullhead, a heath-covered bald that may resemble a bull's head from a distance.

activities.name: Hike the Northwest Rim Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (9-10 Hours)
activities.description: At 18.6 miles round-trip, the Northwest Rim Trail is ideal for trail runners. At an average hiking pace, it takes 9-10 hours to complete. Pets are not permitted.

activities.name: Kwis Kwis Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-5 Hours)
activities.description: The Kwis Kwis Trail is a 3.6 miles one way trail that can be combined with the Fort to Sea to form loops. 2.7 miles - Fort to Sea west to 1st Kwis Kwis connector to Kwis Kwis to the Fort to Sea Trailhead. 5.3 miles - Fort to Sea west to 2nd Kwis Kwis connector (below Clatsop Ridge Overlook) to take Kwis Kwis to…

activities.name: Take a Self-Guided Auto Tour of Valles Caldera
activities.description: This self-guided driving tour leads visitors through Valles Caldera National Preserve while recommending various stops at photo locations, geologic features, and historic structures.

activities.name: Panther Winter Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Taking its name from Panther Gap (8,600 feet), the Panther Trail is part of a difficult loop for experienced skiers. Steep grades and dense forests guard the great views from Panther Gap.

activities.name: Whitewater Boating
activities.duration: Most river trips last for a half day, though longer trips are possible.
activities.description: Whitewater rafting and kayaking is one of the more popular activities at New River Gorge. Boaters can go with an outfitter or on your own if you have the proper experience. The New River is characterised by big, powerful rapids and a boulder strewn river gorge.

activities.name: Places of Interest Related to Carter G. Woodson
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-4 Hours)
activities.description: After you visit the Carter G. Woodson Home National Historic Site, check out these nearby places.

activities.name: Middle Emerald Pools Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Middle Emerald Pools Trail is a moderate hike along an unpaved sandstone ledge above the Lower Emerald Pool Trail. activities.name: Canyon Overlook
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: Long drop-offs, mostly fenced. Rocky and uneven trail ends at a viewpoint for Pine Creek Canyon and lower Zion Canyon. To enter or exit the parking area just east of the tunnel, you must turn right. Parking is extremely limited, be prepared to try multiple times. Pit toilets are available in the parking area.

activities.name: Watch Voices of Sitka
activities.description: Watch a 15-minute film for an overview of Tlingit, Russian, and American history in and around the park.

activities.name: Sunrise at Point Isabel
activities.basis: estimated from duration (20-60 Minutes)
activities.description: Enjoy a picturesque sunrise at Point Isabel on Fort George Island and beat the heat of midday hiking in Florida. The sea breeze and views are worth it!

activities.name: Hike Devils Orchard
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Enjoy an easy, 0.5 mile walk through an open limber pine woodland.

activities.name: Clarno Arch Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (15-45 Minutes)
activities.description: This 0.5 mi (0.8 km) trail climbs almost 200 ft (60 m) in height to the base of the Palisades to a view of an arch above. No collecting is permitted.

activities.name: Painted Hills Overlook Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (5-30 Minutes)
activities.description: The Painted Hills Overlook Trail is 0.5 mile (0.8 km) roundtrip. This fairly level trail follows an old road and offers further distinctive views of the Painted Hills. Walking on the hills is strictly prohibited.

activities.name: Bike the Katy Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (0-7 Days)
activities.description: Katy Trail State Park runs 240 miles across the state of Missouri between Clinton and Machens. Known as the country's longest continuous rail-trail, it attracts cyclists, walkers, equestrians, nature lovers, and history buffs seeking adventure along the Missouri River.

activities.name: Snowshoeing in Valles Caldera
activities.description: Winter is a spectacular time to visit Valles Caldera National Preserve. The park has miles of groomed and ungroomed trails for the adventurous snowshoer.

activities.name: Hike the Buffalo River Trail - Woolum to Tyler Bend
activities.basis: estimated from duration (12 Hours)
activities.description: The Buffalo River Trail follows along the south side of the river from Woolum to Tyler Bend for a little more than 11 miles.

activities.name: Mill Prong - Laurel Prong Loop
activities.basis: estimated from duration (7-8 Hours)
activities.description: MILE 52.8 | A circuit hike to Camp Rapidan, the rustic getaway of President Herbert Hoover and First Lady Lou Henry Hoover. Today, this restful spot features exhibits on the First Couple and their perspectives.

activities.name: Paddling Gilbert to South Maumee
activities.basis: estimated from duration (6 Hours)
activities.description: This reach is about 12 miles which makes it one of the less crowded sections of the river.

activities.name: Watch the Charlestown Navy Yard Orientation Film
activities.description: Before exploring the Charlestown Navy Yard, take a few minutes to watch an introductory film on the Charlestown Navy Yard.

activities.name: Bike the Tea Kettle Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-60 Minutes)
activities.description: Tea Kettle Trail is a great mountain biking trail that runs between Bread Loaves and Elephant Rock. activities.name: Quarry Exhibit Hall
activities.description: The Quarry Exhibit Hall allows visitors to view the wall of approximately 1,500 dinosaur bones in a refurbished, comfortable space.

activities.name: Hike the Rabbit Mountain Loop
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: The Rabbit Mountain Loop (2.9 miles, 4.7 km round-trip), formerly known as the Coyote Call Trail, contours along the southern rim of the caldera, offering great views of Valle Grande and Redondo Peak. The loop takes 1-2 hours. Leashed pets are permitted.

activities.name: Visit the Planetarium
activities.description: Learn about the night sky in the Rock Creek Park planetarium.

activities.name: Junior Ranger Program at Hopewell Culture NHP
activities.description: The park's Junior Ranger program is a free program to visitors of all ages. Simply visit or call the park and ask a ranger for your booklet so you can get started. Once you finish the required number of pages, take your booklet to a ranger and get ready to be sworn in as one of the park's newest Junior Rangers!

activities.name: Walk Down Broad Street
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Take a stroll down the historic Broad Street at Frederica and leard about who used to live in the town and what it took to survive in the 1740's on the Georgia coast.

activities.name: Be a Dinosaur Junior Ranger
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Junior Rangers help to "Explore, Learn, and Protect" our national parks. Anyone can be a Junior Ranger! Once you learn about the monument and the amazing resources found here, you will be able to share your knowledge with friends and family!

activities.name: Visit the Strentzel/Muir Home

activities.description: Take a trip back in time and visit the Armory when it was was producing firearms and learn about the site that shaped the City of Springfield and the United States. activities.name: Grandview Main Overlook
activities.description: The Grandview Main Overlook is located about two football fields in distance from the parking area near the Grandview Visitor Center. There is a kiosk that is a triangular shaped structure with maps and information and the walking path to the Overlook begins at this location.

activities.name: Explore Hidden Sequoias at Muir Grove
activities.basis: estimated from duration (2-3 Hours)
activities.description: Take a hike to a sequoia grove that is tucked away from the road. Muir Grove provides a quiet experience among these giant trees. If you find other sequoia groves to be a bit crowded, take a walk to experience Muir Grove.

activities.name: Birding In The Southern Section
activities.description: Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument provides important and diverse breeding habitat for many species of birds. Enjoy birding in the monument!

activities.name: Hike Along the Towpath Through the Paw Paw Tunnel
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Minutes)
activities.description: Walk through the 3,118-foot Paw Paw Tunnel, a significant engineering feature along Mile 155 of the C&O Canal towpath.

activities.name: Hike the Cobey Pond Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: This loop trail offers a leisurely stroll around the picturesque Cobey Pond after a moderate incline through the forest from the trailhead to the pond. The trail offers hikers ample opportunities for view wildlife and waterfowl. The trail is located on Pennsylvania Game Lands 316.

activities.name: Kayenta Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The moderate, 2.0 mi (3.2 km) Kayenta Trail follows the Virgin River before ascending to the Lower and Upper Emerald Pool Trails. Provides panoramic views of Zion Canyon along the way. Long drop-offs are present along this trail. You can either return on the same trail, or make a loop using one of the Emerald Pools…

activities.name: Short Hikes in the Monument
activities.basis: estimated from duration (20-60 Minutes)
activities.description: These out-and-back trails start from along scenic Rim Rock Drive in Colorado National Monument. All are less than two miles round-trip, perfect for short treks from the car to get better views of these outstanding canyons.

activities.name: Hike the Nightingale Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (20-30 Minutes)
activities.description: The Nightingale Trail on the south end of the island is a great place to experience the interior of the maritime forest.

activities.name: The Story of the Colts: Symbolism at the Church of the Good Shepherd and the Parish House

activities.description: The Church of the Good Shepherd and the Caldwell Hart Colt Memorial Parish House were commissioned by Elizabeth Hart Jarvis Colt in remembrance of her husband, infant children and their son. activities.description: East Side Trails, Moderate Hikes, Cave Hike

activities.name: Hiking The Blackberry Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-60 Minutes)

activities.description: Float this short stretch of river from Mongaup River Access to the New York DEC river access at Sparrowbush, NY. This stretch is approximately 3 river miles and takes on average 1.5 hours to float.

activities.name: Valles Caldera Junior Ranger Program
