10 am - 4 pm Friday and Saturday
Plan to spend at least 2 hours at the fair.
activities.description: Step back in time at the Port Oneida Fair and experience life as it was in the late 1850's through the early 1940's.

activities.name: Explore the Cannonball Concretions
activities.basis: estimated from duration (5-15 Minutes)
activities.description: The cannonball concretions are an arresting and unusual geological formation. Stop at this pullout to explore their mysteries!

activities.name: Contemplate Your Place in the Landscape At The Big Map
activities.description: The Glen Canyon and Surrounding Area Relief Map sits in a place of honor at the Powell Museum & Archives next to Glen Canyon Conservancy's Flagship office. Use it to help plan your Glen Canyon adventure, or pretend you are in space looking down at the landscape. Whoa.

activities.name: Explore the FDR Presidential Library Exhibits
activities.description: The Franklin D. Roosevelt Presidential Library and Museum is independently operated and maintained by the National Archives and Records Administration, a federal agency.

activities.name: Fort Larned Living History
activities.description: Fort Larned staff and volunteers help bring the fort to life during the summer with our living history programs.

activities.name: Birdwatch at Cottonwood Campground
activities.description: Situated near the Rio Grande, under the shade of numerous large cottonwood trees, Cottonwood Campground is a great place to look for birds and other wildlife.

activities.name: Hike Minerva Hoyt Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: Information on the Minerva Hoyt trail.

activities.name: Fife and Drum Music Demonstration
activities.description: Music played an important role in the daily lives of soldiers garrisoned at Fort McHenry. A soldier's entire day would revolve around the sounds of fifes and drums. Join living historians in the famous "Fort McHenry Guard Fife and Drum Corps" as they play period music and give a history of music's role at Fort McHenry.

activities.name: Hike the Big Savage Mountain Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The Big Savage Mountain Trail, managed by Maryland Dept. of Natural Resources, is an 18-mile footpath providing outstanding views of the high points in western Maryland. Best traversed north to south, the Trail is a challenging one-day hike or can be an overnight; a permit for backpacking is available from the Forest…

activities.name: Climbing at New River Gorge
activities.description: With over 1,400 established climbing routes, New River Gorge National Park and Preserve has become one of the most popular climbing locations in the country.

activities.name: Spend a Day at the Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad National Historical Park
activities.description: Amid bird calls, freshly plowed fields, and the hum of mosquitoes, the landscape that shaped Harriet Tubman’s life as an enslaved child, young woman, and freedom seeker thrives still in Dorchester, Talbot, and Caroline Counties, preserved within the Harriet Tubman Underground Railroad National Monument and National…

activities.name: Become a Citizen Scientist
activities.description: Help park rangers monitor erosion and shoreline changes.

activities.name: Become a Fort Smith BARK Ranger
activities.description: Complete the Fort Smith BARK Ranger booklet so your pet can become an official BARK Ranger!

activities.name: Watch An Icon Reborn
activities.description: Watch an 18-minute film for an overview of the Russian Bishop's House and the history of Saint Innocent's efforts to reconcile Tlingit and Russians.

activities.name: Backcountry Camping in the Otis Pike Wilderness
activities.description: The Otis Pike Fire Island High Dune Wilderness offers a wilderness experience like no other. Backcountry camping is one of the best ways to experience it.

activities.name: Visit the Burial Site
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: According to Franklin D. Roosevelt's own instructions, he was buried in the family garden. His wishes reflect his connection to the place of his birth and the launching point of his rise to public prominence.

activities.name: Hike Double Bubble Nubble Loop with Island Explorer
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The trek to summit both Bubbles and Conners Nubble summits three peaks and accesses iconic park locations. Hikers will be treated to views of lakes and mountains while exploring woodlands. By hiking with the use of the Island Explorer Bus, these trails are accessible in a unique way and helps hikers overcome the…

activities.name: See Mount Vernon From Piscataway Park
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: As a scenic easement meant to preserve the view from Mt. Vernon, Piscataway Park is a testament to the rich history of the Potomac River.

activities.name: Hike Schoolhouse Gap Trail
activities.description: Hike 4.4 miles (7.1 km) roundtrip on Schoolhouse Gap Trail which offers a peaceful walk with a touch of history and a chance to spot seasonal blooms and wildlife.

activities.name: Hike Bench Trail to Sycamore Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: East Side Trails, Moderate Hikes

activities.name: Biking at Ocmulgee Mounds
activities.description: Biking is a great way to experience Ocmulgee Mounds while getting in some exercise.

activities.name: Hike to Baker Lake
activities.basis: estimated from duration (5-10 Hours)
activities.description: The hike to Baker Lake is a 10 mile round trip through pine forests and along a mountain stream. Baker Lake is one of the largest mountain lakes in Great Basin National Park. Nestled in a mountain cirque the beautiful lake frequently has snow on its rocky banks.

activities.name: The Grotto and Hunter Line Shack
activities.basis: estimated from duration (3-5 Hours)
activities.description: Stretch out your day hike into McKittrick Canyon by hiking to the Grotto. Elevation gain doubles as you travel further up canyon, but is still mild at less then 600 feet gained from the trailhead. Exposed cave features and stone picnic tables near the Hunter Line Shack make for a fabulous lunch destination.

activities.name: Hike Pine Creek Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: This trail follows Pine Creek as it cascades into the depths of the upper Black Canyon to Morrow Point Reservoir. It follows the old narrow gauge railroad bed along the reservoir.

activities.name: Become a Great Basin National Park Junior Ranger
activities.description: Great Basin Junior Ranger

activities.name: Dunlap Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (5-15 Minutes)
activities.description: A short, 1/4th of a mile long trail leading to the Dunlap Mound and Civil War earthworks.

activities.name: Driving the Burr Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Drive the scenic Burr Trail from Glen Canyon's Bullfrog district, along the bottom of Capitol Reef, through Grand Staircase, to Boulder, UT. Distance: 67 miles (108 km) one-way Mix of paved and dirt roads, impassable when wet Four-wheel drive sometimes required. No RVs.

activities.name: Western National Parks Store at Bent's Old Fort
activities.description: The park store is operated by Western National Parks, an official non-profit partner of the National Park Service dedicated to supporting the educational mission of Bent's Old Fort National Historic Site. The park store has a wide range of books, maps, travel guides, media, educational games, posters, and other items…

activities.name: Visit the Statue's Pedestal
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: Visiting the pedestal is a great addition to any trip to the Statue of Liberty. Starting in 2004, the National Park Service implemented a new system that requires reservations to access the pedestal. This reservation system is much different than how the public accessed the pedestal prior to 2001.

activities.name: Hike the Fort Hill Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-60 Minutes)
activities.description: Find your trail to explore at Cape Cod National Seashore! One of eleven trails in the park is the Fort Hill loop, a one-mile loop trail that winds around the historic Fort Hill site.

activities.name: Paddling Spring Creek to Dillards Ferry
activities.basis: estimated from duration (2-4 Hours)
activities.description: This friendly, 4.6-mile paddle is great for folks that want to get a good feel for the river, but don't want to be out all day. You will paddle by Jackpot, Kimball, and Stairstep Bluffs as you make your way towards Water Creek, a great place to park the boat and get out and explore. This river trip ends at Dillards…

activities.name: Picnic at the Park
activities.description: Fort Stanwix National Monument has a nice, big, grassy lawn and plenty of picnic tables to make your travels more convenient. Feel free to play and picnic on the park lawn during your visit!

activities.name: Explore Tallgrass Visitor Center
activities.description: Park rangers attend the visitor center with a range of exhibits. Geology, ecology, history, and culture all shaped today's Tallgrass Prairie. A modest gift shop provides souvenirs and the park stamp for collecting memories. Junior Ranger books, event posts, trail maps, and brochures constantly draw visitors.

activities.name: Hike to Mount Le Conte on Rainbow Falls Trail
activities.description: Hike 13 miles (21 km) roundtrip on one of five routes to Mount Le Conte that includes a waterfall, rocky ascents, and forest views. Lush forests line the trail and hikers will intersect the Bullhead Trail, Alum Cave Trail, and Trillium Gap Trail before reaching the summit.

activities.name: Visit the Gulf Islands Park Store
activities.description: Purchase souvenirs and more pages for your passport at this bookstore located within historic Fort Pickens.

activities.name: Swim in Boston Harbor
activities.description: Cool off by taking a dip in Boston Harbor! Swim in Spectacle's designated swimming area.

activities.name: Figure-8 Combination
activities.basis: estimated from duration (4-5 Hours)
activities.description: The Figure-8 Combination combines three amphitheater hikes, Queen's Garden, Navajo Loop, and the Peekaboo Loop, into one ultimate hike! We recommend a clockwise direction descending Queen's Garden, connecting to the Peekaboo Loop (we recommend hiking it in a clockwise direction), and ascending either side of the…

activities.name: Paul Revere House: Step Back in Time at The Revere's Family Home
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Take a self-guided tour through the well-preserved rooms where Paul Revere and his family lived for about twenty years.

activities.name: Golf in DC's National Parks
activities.description: Visit one of three golf courses at National Parks in Washington, DC

activities.name: Join a Guided Tour of Fort Monroe
activities.description: National Park Service and the Fort Monroe Authority offer guided walking tours year-round. Tours may answer questions about different aspects of Fort Monroe's history. What peoples came to this area and what were their legacies? Who built the fort, why, and how?

activities.name: Blue Ridge Hills & Hollows
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-8 Hours)
activities.description: The Blue Ridge Hills & Hollows Bikepacking Route is a 300-mile cycling experience that connects eight memorials honoring displaced Blue Ridge communities. Riders explore scenic mountain roads, rural landscapes, and the headwaters of major Chesapeake Bay tributaries while discovering stories of settlement…

activities.name: Stoll Memorial Trail (Scoville Point)
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The Albert Stoll Jr. Memorial Trail is a relatively easy hiking trail that captures the majesty of Lake Superior and engages with the wilderness character of Isle Royale National Park.

activities.name: Paddling Tyler Bend to Grinder's Ferry
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Easy, flat water for 1 mile reach of the river.

activities.name: Hike Emmons Moraine Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: Enjoy a short hike from the White River Campground through the forest to a view of the Emmons Glacier and a beautiful turquoise lake colored by glacial silt.

activities.name: See Exhibits at the Casemate Museum
activities.description: Exhibits at the Casemate Museum chronicle the military history of Fort Monroe. Get your free museum ticket Fort Monroe Visitor & Education Center. The Casemate Museum is within the stone fort. Information desk staff will give direction when you get your ticket.

activities.name: Portage from Chickenbone Lake to Lake Livermore
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The portage between Chickenbone Lake and Lake Livermore is a short and steep 0.2 miles.

activities.name: Explore with Lewis and Clark
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Stroll through the paved paths of the Explorer’s Garden located in the North Gateway area of the park. In the Garden, you can find plants that were used by Native Americans and detailed by Lewis and Clark in their expedition journals as they traveled west.

activities.name: Spalding Walking Tour
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-90 Minutes)
activities.description: Historic area with cultural, state and national significance.

activities.name: Hike Ocean Path Trail with Island Explorer Bus
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: Ocean Path follows atop Acadia’s granite cliffs along the Atlantic Ocean. While exploring the Ocean Path, visitors can enjoy scenic vistas and iconic park locations including Sand beach, Thunder Hole and Otter Cliffs. Combining this hike with Acadia’s Island Explorer bus gives hikers flexibility in trail distance on…

activities.name: Webcams
activities.description: Webcam views from the Visitor Center at Park Headquarters in Copper Center, Kennecott Mill and Mt. Blackburn and Kennicott Glacier and the Chugach Range.

activities.name: Gettysburg Winter Programs
activities.description: Featuring some of the best Rangers, historians, and authors from across the country, this popular eight-week Winter Lecture Series returns to the Gettysburg National Military Park Museum and Visitor Center in 2026! Programs take place at 1:30 pm on weekends in the Gettysburg NMP Museum and Visitor Center, January 10…

activities.name: Hike the Historic Railroad Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-4 Hours)
activities.description: The Historic Railroad Trail features incredible vistas of Lake Mead and Boulder Basin and five tunnels – each approximately 25 feet wide.

activities.name: Bryce Amphitheater Traverse
activities.basis: estimated from duration (3-4 Hours)
activities.description: The Bryce Amphitheater Traverse is a one-way hike combining the Peekaboo Loop with the Queen's Garden trail. Hikers descend from Bryce Point, turning left (clockwise) on Peekaboo Loop and then connecting to the Queen's Garden trail to ascend to Sunrise Point.

activities.name: Cinnamon Bay Beach and Snorkeling
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Cinnamon Bay offers a long gently sloping snow white beach to stick your toes in, or go for a leisurely stroll. The crystal clear waters provide many delights for even a novice snorkeler. Turtles and fish of all sizes and colors can be seen here.

activities.name: Red Scar Knoll Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (15-30 Minutes)
activities.description: This mostly level trail is 0.25 mi (0.4 km) long and leads to a hill of bright yellow and red clays; called Red Hill Trail on road signs. Walking on the exposed soils is strictly prohibited. Please stay on trail.

activities.name: Astronomy Ranger Program
activities.description: Astronomy Program

activities.name: Walk the Earthquake Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Discover the geology of the San Andreas Fault on this paved loop nature trail. A fence that was constructed half way around the trail illustrates the 16 feet (3 meters) of displacement that occurred during the infamous 1906 earthquake. The Earthquake Trail begins and ends at the northeast corner of the Bear Valley…

activities.name: Birding in Theodore Roosevelt National Park
activities.description: The badlands of North Dakota are home to more than 180 species of birds. Take a moment and see which ones you can spot!

activities.name: Hike to Minong Ridge Overlook
activities.basis: estimated from duration (2-6 Hours)
activities.description: Hike to the Minong Ridge Overlook and enjoy views of Isle Royale's west end, Lake Superior, and the Canadian shoreline to the north.

activities.name: Watch the Fort Union Trading Post Orientation Film
activities.description: Learn how Fort Union Trading Post became an epicenter for trade between the Assiniboine and other Northern Plains Tribes and Euro-American fur traders.

activities.name: Juniper Flats Zone Backpacking
activities.basis: estimated from duration (2-15 Days)
activities.description: Backpack in the Juniper Flats Zone

activities.name: Tuskegee Airmen NHS Hangar 1
activities.description: Hangar 1 is the starting point for the indoor museums. It focuses on the training of the cadets and the involvement of the Tuskegee Institute.

activities.name: Walk Around the Tidal Basin
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-3 Hours)
activities.description: The Thomas Jefferson Memorial, Martin Luther King Jr. Memorial, and the Washington Monument are easily visible along the two mile long Tidal Basin Loop Trail.

activities.name: Eagle Nest Point Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: This unmaintained trail is 2 miles (3.2 km) round trip along an old dirt road. The trail goes along a ridge to an overlook amid limber pine and Douglas fir. The overlook provides a great vantage point to view the canyons and ridges in the distance. This trail can be difficult to follow. Speak to a ranger at the…

activities.name: Tour the Hospital Complex
activities.description: Visit the Hospital and Contagious Disease Ward on Ellis Island.

activities.name: Drive the Tour of Tilted Rocks
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: This 10 mile (16) km paved tour along the Cub Creek Road in Utah provides a great introduction to Dinosaur National Monument. Take the Tour of Tilted Rocks to enjoy sweeping geology, historic homesteads, petroglyphs and pictographs, hiking trails, campgrounds, and scenic vistas! The road is usually accessible for…

activities.name: Hike to Burroughs Mountain
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Hike the Burroughs Mountain Trail for outstanding mountain views and to visit the most accessible tundra in the Cascade Range.

activities.name: Picnicking at the Birthplace
activities.description: Spending the day at the park? Bring a lunch and enjoy the scenery of the Picnic Area.

activities.name: Watch "River of Change"
activities.description: This 18-minute film tells the story of Missouri National Recreational River. Learn about the park's wildlife as well as the history of the river, explorers, and people who lived along the river.

activities.name: Drive East Portal Road
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: East Portal Road is a windy, steep scenic road down to the Gunnison River. East Portal is within Curecanti National Recreation Area, but only accessible from within Black Canyon of the Gunnison National Park. Vehicles over 22 feet are prohibited on the East Portal Road.

activities.name: Hike to Rainbow Falls
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Hike 5.6 miles (9 km) roundtrip through varied forest to a popular waterfall named for the misty rainbow that often appears at its base. This trail is well-traveled and maintained, but the climb to the falls is relatively steep.

activities.name: The Union Advance Trail at Antietam
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-90 Minutes)
activities.description: Hike the Union Advance Trail to learn about the fighting around the famous Burnside Bridge.

activities.name: Fish the Middle Jaramillo Creek
activities.description: Jaramillo Creek is the middle of the three fishable streams in Valles Caldera. The middle section of the creek runs from Cerro Pinon upstream to the Cerro Abrigo Trailhead.

activities.name: Stones River NB Junior Ranger Program
activities.description: Become a Stones River National Battlefield Junior Ranger!

activities.name: Paddling Woolum to Baker Ford
activities.basis: estimated from duration (5 Hours)
activities.description: Several bluffs along this reach (Margaret White, Whisenant, Buzzard Roost and Peter Cave) are more than 200 feet high.

activities.name: Snowshoe the East Branch Loop
activities.description: Snowshoe 3.7 miles around the East Branch Loop, located at the northern section of Katahdin Woods and Waters National Monument.

activities.name: Queen's Garden Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The Queen's Garden Trail is the least difficult of the trails descending from the rim into the Bryce Canyon Amphitheater. Hike this out-and-back trail to the Queen Victoria hoodoo at the end of a short spur trail and experience the splendor of hiking amongst the hoodoos. This trail is commonly combined with the Navajo…

activities.name: Attend the Timucuan Science and History Symposium
activities.description: Learn about the latest research in the park in the fields of history, ecology, biology, archaeology and more! Students are invited to present their research in the poster hall. All are encouraged to attend. This event takes place every other January on even years.

activities.name: Hike to Chimney Rock: The Orange Blazed Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (2-4 Hours)
activities.description: Chimney Rock reaches a maximum elevation of 1419 ft and Wolf Rock has an elevation of 1401 ft. Great for a romantic hike for that offers opportunities to get back in touch with nature and time to reflect on natures peacefulness and beauty.

activities.name: Driving Down Island
activities.description: One of the most popular activities to do when visiting the national seashore is to drive on the beach and travel down island. Venturing beyond the pavement can get you to some of the most remote areas of the park, awarding you the experience of solitude in this natural landscape.

activities.name: View the Russell Cave Film
activities.description: Russell Cave Film 7 minutes

activities.name: Alley Overlook Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1.3 mile loop trail.)
activities.description: Alley Overlook Trail

activities.name: Main Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-90 Minutes)
activities.description: A 1/2 mile trail leading to three of the park's most popular points of interest.

activities.name: Hike Beech Mountain South Ridge Loop
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: This loop hike traverses a forest before ascending Beech Mountain, where there is a fire tower and views of Long Pond, Mansell Mountain, and the west side of Mount Desert Island.

activities.name: Hike the Valley Trail
activities.description: The Valley Trail stretches for five miles down the east side of Rock Creek Park from Boundary Bridge to a spot near Peirce Mill and Picnic Grove #1.

activities.name: Climb to Liberty's Crown
activities.duration: Most visitors access the pedestal and crown in less than 2 hours. Set aside 30-45 for the Statue’s museum, 20-30 minutes for the different levels of the pedestal and 20-30 minutes for the crown.
activities.description: Crown access is limited and advanced reservations are required. Starting in 2009, the National Park Service implemented a new system that requires advanced reservations for access to the crown. This reservation system is much different than how the public accessed the crown prior to 2001.

activities.name: Hike the South Mountain Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (3-4 Hours)
activities.description: The South Mountain Trail is an 8.2-mile round-trip hike that climbs to the summit of South Mountain. The hike takes 4-5 hours to complete. Pets are not permitted.

activities.name: Lost Peak Saddle
activities.basis: estimated from duration (3-6 Hours)
activities.description: Hiking the Tejas Trail from Dog Canyon out to the Lost Peak Saddle and back makes an excellent day hike in the Guadalupe Mountains.

activities.name: Visit the Denison Sawmill Exhibit
activities.description: Learn about early infrastructure of the Lake Clark region. The Denison steam powered sawmill led waves of change to the Lake Clark region.

activities.description: The Aliante Loop temporary trail offers year-round scenic views of Mojave Desert scrub habitat and the Las Vegas Range, wildflower blooms in spring and summer are a sight to see.

activities.name: Become a Junior Ranger at Wupatki
activities.description: Join Jackie Rabbit in exploring the human history, geology, and wildlife of Wupatki National Monument and earn a Jr. Ranger badge.

activities.name: Houchin Ferry to Brownsville
activities.basis: estimated from duration (90-120 Minutes)
activities.description: This short trip travels along the Green River from Houchin Ferry inside Mammoth Cave National Park to the former site of Lock and Dam #6 or the Brownsville boat ramp.

activities.name: Hike Flying Mountain Loop
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: This loop hike offers a short, relatively steep hike to the top of a small mountain with spectacular views of Somes Sound and descends to a quiet ocean cove with a rocky beach.

activities.name: Hike the Lehman Creek Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (3-6 Hours)
activities.description: Hike the Lehman Creek Trail in summer and fall for amazing colors and plenty of shade, or to access the higher elevation trails in the winter time. This 6.4 mile round trip journey travels through a varied forest showcasing a harder to see perspective of the many mountain peaks.

activities.name: Visit the Thomas Jefferson Memorial
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-120 Minutes)
activities.description: Walk around the Thomas Jefferson Memorial or go to a ranger led program to learn more about Jefferson's life and work as a philosopher, a politician and a President.

activities.name: Pinery Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The Pinery Trail offers visitors an opportunity to take a quick walk on a paved trail. The trail also features ruins of the Old Butterfield Stagecoach Route Pinery Station built in 1858.

activities.name: Become a Jr. Ranger at the Birthplace
activities.description: Become a Jr. Ranger!

activities.name: Sandboarding and Sand Sledding
activities.description: Sandboarding and sand sledding are the most popular activities on the dunes. Read the information on this page to have a positive, fun, and safe experience.

activities.name: Hike Split Rock
activities.basis: estimated from duration (90-150 Minutes)
activities.description: Split Rock is a 2.5 mile loop trail with 150 feet of elevation gain and beautiful desert views.

activities.name: Take a Tour of the Historic Core on the Plantation Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: A walk along the Plantation Trail evokes the atmosphere of an 1850s and Civil War-era tobacco plantation, reflecting Booker T. Washington’s childhood at the Burroughs plantation. The historic core includes points of interest and reconstructed mid-19th-century buildings. The Plantation Trail forms a 0.55-mile loop…

activities.name: Earn Your Junior Ranger Badge
activities.description: Complete the activity book and earn a badge. Our park offers a chance to earn two different badges, one for Timucuan Preserve and another for Fort Caroline.

activities.name: Lewis Falls Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (4-5 Hours)
activities.description: MILE 51.2 | Leaving from Big Meadows amphitheater, this hike leads to an observation point over a beautiful 81’ waterfall.

activities.name: Hike the Kehoe Beach Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Follow this relatively flat trail from Pierce Point Road along the northern edge of Kehoe Marsh and out to Kehoe Beach. This beach is at the north end of the eleven-mile long Point Reyes Beach. Pets are permitted year-round on the Kehoe Beach Trail and on the beach to the north of the trail (e.g., to the right if you…

activities.name: Story of the Forest
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: MILE 51 | Pets are not allowed on this hike. An easier stroll through the woods that passes next to the Big Meadows Air Quality Station, an important place for scientists and researchers to learn about air quality in Shenandoah.

activities.name: Lower Dogwood Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (15-40 Minutes)
activities.description: Lower Dogwood Trail climbs North Mountain. Near the top, boulders mark the westernmost tip of the trail. From there, the trail drops downhill.

activities.name: Serenity at Alley Spring
activities.description: Be present and practice deep breathing while observing the scenery at Alley Spring.

activities.name: Hiking Alkali Flat Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Imagine yourself surrounded by the spectacular views of endless dunes with few footprints. The Alkali Flat Trail takes you through the heart of the sands, up and over steep dunes to the edge of Alkali Flat.

activities.name: Visit Little American Island
activities.description: Discover the past on this self guided walk Little American Island. This island was home to one of the area gold mines during the brief gold rush of the 1890s. You will see mine shafts, tailing piles, and machinery along the side of this short trail. Signs tell the story of the gold rush.

activities.name: The Rim Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: The Rim Trail stretches from its beginning in the south at Bryce Point 5.5 miles (8.9 km) north to Fairyland Point. As it follows the edge of the Bryce Amphitheater area of the park, it connects to the park's most popular viewpoints: Inspiration Point, Sunset Point, and Sunrise Point. This relatively easy hike…

activities.name: Hike the Battle Road Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-4 Hours)
activities.description: The Battle Road Trail is a five mile trail connecting historic sites from Meriam’s Corner in Concord to the eastern boundary of the park in Lexington. Much of the trail follows the original remnants of the Battle Road: Where thousands of Colonial Militia and British Regulars fought a bloody engagement on April 19…

activities.name: Clara Barton National Historic Site
activities.description: Clara Barton dedicated her life and energies to help others in times of need - both home and abroad, in peacetime as well as during military emergencies. Glen Echo was her home the last 15 years of her life and the structure illustrates her dedication and concern for those less fortunate than herself.

activities.name: Fall Walkabouts
activities.description: Join a Park Ranger as we explore each one of our 6 park sites on Saturdays this Fall. Tours will discuss the history of each site and its importance withint the larger context of US history. Tours start at 10:00 AM and last about 90 minutes.

activities.name: Visitor Education Center
activities.description: The Visitor Education Center for the Rosie the Riveter/WWII Home Front National Historical Park provides films, interactive exhibits and more. We recommend making this your first stop when visiting our park.

activities.name: Explore the Freedom Riders Story
activities.description: Explore the indoor and outdoor exhibits that tell the stories of the Freedom Riders. Indoor exhibits are limited to open hours, but outdoor exhibits are always available.

activities.name: Hawk Watch at Harveys Knob
activities.description: Every autumn, thousands of raptors ride the thermal updrafts of the Blue Ridge Mountains on their way to wintering grounds. You can watch the graceful flights of these soaring birds from Harveys Knob Overlook.

activities.name: Fort Film: "I Am So Wore Out with Fatigue"
activities.description: What was a typical day like for a Continental Soldier on the New York frontier after the Siege of 1777? Routine, work, and fear were common. As was doubt. This 18 minute film tells the story of the garrison of Fort Schuyler from the perspective of a regular soldier.

activities.name: Tour a Family Farm Turned Field Hospital
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: See the battle of Wilson’s Creek through the eyes of a farming family caught up in combat and its aftermath. The Ray family not only lost much of their property to foraging soldiers, but they witnessed the horrifying toll of battle when their home became a makeshift field hospital. The historic Ray House and…

activities.name: Visit the 10th Mountain Division Memorial
activities.description: Take a short walk up the Skyline Trail to visit the 10th Mountain Division Memorial which honors the U.S. Army Troops who trained at Paradise during World War II.

activities.name: Hike Mastodon Peak
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: A moderate three mile loop with 375 feet of elevation gain.

activities.name: Birding
activities.description: The park's location along the Atlantic flyway affords visitors the opportunity to see wintering, migratory, and breeding birds along park roads.

activities.name: Visit Pearson Air Museum
activities.description: Visit Pearson Air Museum and discover the history of aviation in Vancouver, Washington!

activities.name: Tidepooling at Bar Island
activities.description: Access the shore from downtown Bar Harbor for a unique tidepooling experience on a natural land bridge.

activities.name: Visit National Mall and Memorial Parks
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-7 Days)
activities.description: Each year, millions of people visit the National Mall and Memorial Parks to recreate, to commemorate presidential legacies, to honor our nation's veterans, to make their voices heard, and to celebrate our nation's commitment to freedom and equality.

activities.name: Hike Ship Harbor Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-60 Minutes)
activities.description: Ship Harbor Trail is a 1.3 mile figure-8 loop near Seawall. Great for families and birders, and a variety of habitats can be seen along the shore.

activities.name: Oak Ridge: Explore the Children's Museum of Oak Ridge
activities.description: The Children's Museum of Oak Ridge provides visitors of all ages with a wealth of exhibits on a multitude of topics. In addition, the museum is home to the Manhattan Project Oak Ridge Visitor Center. Follow the link for more information on exhibits, operating hours, and admission fees.

activities.name: Hike to Lynn Camp Prong Cascades
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Go on a woodland stroll following an old railroad bed along a mountain stream, 1.4 miles (2.3 km) roundtrip, to a dramatic cascade. The trail is mostly wide and flat and gently ascends through rhododendron and some cliff-like rock outcroppings.

activities.name: Visit La Ventana Natural Arch
activities.basis: estimated from duration (20-30 Minutes)
activities.description: La Ventana Natural Arch is a beautiful natural arch formation located just off Highway 117 in El Malpais National Conservation Area.

activities.name: Hike to Silver Falls
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Enjoy a moderate, family-friendly loop hike through the forest to a beautiful waterfall along the Ohanapecosh River.

activities.name: Cross-Country Skiing
activities.description: Generally, the best skiing is along certain sections of park roads which are closed to vehicular traffic.

activities.name: Nolin River Dam to Houchin Ferry

activities.description: This trip starts at the Tailwater Recreation Area below the Nolin River Dam north of the park.

activities.name: Winter Eagle Watching at the Lackawaxen River Access
activities.description: Although many eagles call the Upper Delaware River region home during all months of the year, winter is a particularly good time to go bald eagle-watching in the park. Wintering bald eagles visit, increasing the population of eagles in the area. Furthermore, during weekends in January and February, volunteer docents…

activities.name: Visit Kahuku: Kona Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (3-5 Hours)
activities.description: Hike through scenic pasturelands with native trees, and transverse the 1887 lava flow.

activities.name: Bike to Coast Campground
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-60 Minutes)
activities.description: Ride your bike on this multi-use trail, through alder forests and grasslands, to beautiful coastal bluffs with ocean views. Allow 15 minutes driving time from Bear Valley to the Coast Trailhead.

activities.name: Visit the African American Civil War Memorial
activities.basis: estimated from duration (15-90 Minutes)
activities.description: Over 200,000 African-American soldiers and sailors served in the U.S. Army and Navy during the Civil War. Their service helped to end the war and free over four million slaves. The African American Civil War Memorial honors their service and sacrifice.

activities.name: Visit the Mascot Saloon
activities.description: Once Skagway's longest running saloon, step back in to time with this restored saloon museum. Learn about the role of vice in the community, see how the owner adapted his business in the face of change, and find out why the saloon finally closed.

activities.name: Explore How Salmon Are Sustaining Southwest Alaska Communities
activities.description: The Kvichak watershed which is fed by Lake Clark and runs into Bristol Bay, is one of the world's most productive spawning and rearing habitats for sockeye salmon. activities.name: Hike Wind Canyon Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Wind Canyon trail is a short, moderate-difficulty trail that rewards hikers with incredible views of the Little Missouri river and the surrounding badlands.

activities.name: Unfinished Railroad Loop Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (60-75 Minutes)
activities.description: Walk along a section of Jackson's line on the Unfinished Railroad where Federal soldiers momentarily breached the Confederate line on August 29, 1862.

activities.name: Rock Climbing at Hidden Valley Nature Trail
activities.description: Hidden Valley offers a wide range of popular technical rock climbing routes.

activities.name: Wildlife Viewing at Dungeness
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Cumberland Island is a great place to view wildlife. Dungeness is a great place to look for the many common animals on the island and is an easy walk from the dock.

activities.name: Be a Cedar Creek & Belle Grove Junior Ranger
activities.description: The Junior Ranger program helps kids explore, learn about, and protect Cedar Creek and Belle Grove National Historical Park. Anyone can become a Junior Ranger by completing activities during a visit to the park.

activities.name: Watch Road of Necessity in the Visitor Center

activities.name: Take a Self-Guided Tour of the Cabin District
activities.basis: estimated from duration (30-60 Minutes)
activities.description: This self-guided audio tour walks through a day in the life of a seasonal worker at the Baca Ranch in the 20th century.

activities.name: Oak Ridge: Visit the New Hope Center at Y-12
activities.description: The New Hope Center at Y-12 tells the remarkable story of Y-12 from the Manhattan Project to the present day. Follow the link for more information on exhibits and operating hours at this free museum.

activities.name: Hike the Sherman Creek Wildlife Area
activities.description: The Sherman Creek Wildlife Area is a cooperative trail system between the Washington Department of Fish and Wildlife and the National Park Service. activities.name: Hike the Sullivan Bay Trail
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: This easy hike along an old forest road leads you through both coniferous and deciduous forest. The trail ends at a viewpoint on Sullivan Bay with a picnic table and fire ring. It treats those who are interested in geology with lots of exposed rock, created by volcanic activity over 2 billion years ago.

activities.name: Hike Beachcroft Path
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-2 Hours)
activities.description: The Beachcroft Path is an historic memorial pathway, constructed in 1915. Take this trail to reach Champlain Mountain for panoramic coastal mountain views of Mount Desert Island, Frenchman Bay, and the outlying islands.

activities.name: Ebey's Reserve - Junior Ranger
activities.description: Become and Ebey's Landing National Historical Reserve Junior Ranger! Discover the people who first called this place home. Discover how glaciers shaped the land. Discover the Salish Sea. Discover how settlers came to land and build their homes here. Discover Ebey's!

activities.name: A Forgotten Civil War: The Revolution in the Mohawk Valley
activities.description: Explore this exhibit and meet the people of the Mohawk Valley. Discover how the American Revolutionary War affected their lives. Who really won or lost? What did "victory" cost them? Was it worth it? You be the judge.

activities.name: Get a Passport Stamp

activities.name: Cave Tours

activities.name: Birding on Mount Rose
activities.description: From the Heritage Center parking lot to the top of Mount Rose and down to the Historic Depot, you'll pass through different habitats. Listen for Merlins and White-throated Sparrows, watch Turkey Vultures soar, and warblers flit among the branches.

activities.name: Torpedo Wharf Fishing
activities.description: Fishing at Torpedo Wharf near Fort Point and Crissy Field.

activities.description: Ramble along the crest of an open ridge that offers spectacular views of tule elk, Tomales Bay, and the Pacific Ocean. Allow 35 minutes driving time from Bear Valley to the Tomales Point Trailhead, located at the north end of Pierce Point Road.

activities.description: Enjoy spectacular views of Glen Lake, undulating sand dunes, and breathtaking views of the grandest of all dunes, with shimmering Lake Michigan as the backdrop. activities.name: Take a walk through Kenilworth Park and Aquatic Gardens
activities.basis: estimated from duration (1-8 Hours)
activities.description: Sparkling in the sun on a breezy day, this natural area of Anacostia Park has origins in a 1926 act of Congress to preserve the forests, water quality, and recreation value of the waterways of Washington, DC. The park reflects the policies that affect rivers and wetlands.

activities.name: Backcountry Hiking South Bluff

activities.name: Walk Around City Point
activities.basis: described by the park
activities.description: Walk around City Point to explore why this area was, and still is, a popular place for living along the rivers. The Eppes family established the Appomattox plantation and their home here as early as 1635, until 1976. activities.name: Explore Gustavus
activities.description: The town of Gustavus is considered the gateway to Glacier Bay. This charming Alaskan community offers plenty for travelers to explore as they make their way to the park.

activities.description: The Indian Pueblo Cultural Center preserves Pueblo culture, their accomplishments, and evolving history of the Pueblo people. activities.name: Watch the Sunrise at Pine Tree Overlook
activities.description: There are many places to view a sunrise along the Blue Ridge Parkway, but the sun rising over the Peaks of Otter at Pine Tree Overlook is a stand out favorite on the northern end of the parkway.

activities.description: The combination of a working railroad yard and a world-class railroad museum gives visitors a chance to do more than just step back in time. activities.name: Play Kōnane

activities.description: Peahea ka hoʻonanenane? Want to test your wits? Play a game of kōnane on the shores of Hōnaunau Bay with your ʻohana (family). This game can be learned in minutes, but may take a lifetime to master.

activities.name: Fossil Butte Nature Trail
activities.basis: estimated from duration (45-90 Minutes)
activities.description: This 1.5 mile (2.4 km) loop trail winds through sagebrush steppe and aspen groves. The signs discuss the ecosystems of the park and geology's effect on the plants that grow in the park.

activities.name: Boating in Canyonlands

activities.description: The Colorado and Green rivers have played a significant role in shaping the landscape of Canyonlands. Boating is a great way to see the park from the bottom up, and affords boaters a unique perspective.

activities.name: Backcountry Camping in Indian Grove

activities.name: Peek into the Paleo Lab

activities.name: Visit the Petroglyph Panel

activities.description: From 600 to 1300 C.E., native people of the Fremont Culture made their home at Capitol Reef. Petroglyphs carved into the Wingate sandstone remind us of their time.

activities.name: Cimarron River Overlook
activities.description: A small overlook and parking area which has scenic views of the Cimarron River valley and interpretive displays about the area's history.

activities.name: Mallard Ponds Fishing Site
activities.description: Located east of Cimarron Recreation Area on FS Road 700, these man-made ponds are stocked with fish by the Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks. Please refer to Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks for further information regarding licensing, size limit and etc.

activities.name: Point of Rocks Interpretive Site
activities.description: An important landmark along the Santa Fe National Historic Trail and the third highest point in Kansas, this site offers interpretive signs, access to the Santa Fe National Historic Trail and scenic views of Cimarron River, looking into Oklahoma and Colorado.

activities.name: Wilburton Pond Fishing Site
activities.description: Located east of County Road 16 on Forest Service Road 700, this man-made pond is stocked with fish by the Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks. Please refer to Kansas Department of Wildlife and Parks for further information regarding licensing, size limit, etc.

activities.name: Iron Spring Interpretive Site
activities.description: Iron Spring was an important water stop for travelers on the Santa Fe National Historic Trail. Depending on the season or weather conditions, several different routes to the spring were used. Between 1861 and 1871 Iron Spring was also used as a stage coach station. Trail ruts are still visible just west of the parking…

activities.name: Picket Wire Corrals Interpretive Site
activities.description: This popular meeting spot, about 33 miles south of La Junta, offers wildlife interpretation and corrals for public equestrian use.

activities.name: Rourke Ranch National Historic Site
activities.description: Rourke Ranch, also known as the Wineglass Ranch, was a cattle and horse ranch founded by Eugene Rourke in 1871. Three generations of the Rourke family lived and worked on the ranch ensuring its survival over a span of a hundred years. When the ranch was sold in 1971, it was known as one of the oldest and most…

activities.name: Sierra Vista Interpretive Site
activities.description: For Santa Fe National Historic Trail travelers heading south, the changing horizon from plains to mountains was a major milestone on their journey. One of their guiding landmarks was the distant Spanish Peaks, which came into view along this section of the trail. A short walk up the side of a bluff will give you a…

activities.name: Abe Lee Fishing Site
activities.description: Abe Lee Fishing Site is located on the south shore of Turquoise Lake, 6 miles west of Leadville. Good fishing plus a many other recreational opportunities are available at this popular lake.  The standard limit of fish allowed from Turquoise Lake is 4 fish total; 2 lake trout…

activities.name: Big Mac Fishing Site
activities.description: Big Mac Fishing Site is located on the northern shore of Twin Lakes Reservoir near the Mt. Elbert Power Plant and Visitor Center off of U.S. Hwy 82. The lake is stocked with rainbow trout. Other fishing sites for Twin Lakes are as follows: Mt. Elbert Power Plant, Deception Point , Praying Angel, Dexter Point …

activities.name: Boustead Tunnel Observation Site
activities.description: Locted at the far west end of Turquoise Lake, Boustead Tunnel conveys water collected by the West Slope Collection System under the Continental Divide and into Turquoise Lake on the East Slope. The tunnel is five miles long and has a water conveyance capacity of 945 cubic feet per second (ft/s). Eight percent of the…

activities.name: Clohesy Lake Cabin
activities.description: The Clohesy Lake Cabin was struck by lightning and burned down.  It was located near Winfield, Colorado surrounded by the Collegiate Peaks Wilderness. Spectacular views of Huron, Missouri and Iowa Peak can be seen from where the cabin once stood.

activities.name: Crystal Lake Fishing Site
activities.description: The lake stocked by the Leadville National Fish Hatchery with rainbow trout, brook trout, brown trout and cutthroat. Use only artificial flies and lures.

activities.name: Crystal Lake Overlook
activities.description: Located just off U.S. Hwy 24, south of Leadville at the Arkansas River Headwaters, the overlook provides gorgeous views of the highest peak in Colorado, Mt. Elbert .

activities.name: Deception Point Fishing Site
activities.description: Located on the north shore of Twin Lakes off of Highway 82.

activities.name: Dexter Point Boating Site
activities.description: This is the boat ramp for Twin Lakes. Located on the north shore of the lake just off of highway 82. Zebra and quagga mussels are a serious threat to Colorado waters. This boating season brings with it mandatory state-certified boat inspections to help prevent the spread of zebra and quagga mussels and…

activities.name: Huron Peak (Fourteener)
activities.description: Huron Peak is 14,003 feet and is a popular climb accessed at  South Fork Clear Creek Trailhead  via the North Huron Trail #1452. The trail is 3.5 miles one way and there is 3,418ft elevation gain. Keep in mind that although trail leading to the summit is not within the Collegiate Peaks…

activities.name: La Plata Peak (Fourteener)
activities.description: La Plata Peak, Colorado's fifth highest peak at 14,336 feet, is accessed via the La Plata Gulch Trail #1474. This trail is 4.3 miles long with a 4,350 foot elevation gain and is the recommended route to the peak. La Plata Peak and La Plata Gulch Trail #1474 are located in the Collegiate…

activities.name: Matchless Boating Site
activities.description: Matchless Boating Site provides the boat ramp for Turquoise Lake. Located on the south-eastern shoreline, Recreation vehicle camping and picnicking areas share this site.

activities.name: Moache Fishing Site
activities.description: This day use site is just east of Twin Lakes with views of Twin Peaks, Hope Pass and Parry Peak and access to fishing on the upper Twin Lake. There is a short .4 mile trail to the Twin Lakes historical village and the Forest Service visitors center.

activities.name: Monitor Rock
activities.description: Monitor Rock is a popular rock climbing area located on the north side of State Highway 82, approximately 4 miles west of Twin Lakes, Colorado. For more information, visit  Monitor Rock climbing information .

activities.name: Mosquito View Observation Site
activities.description: A scenic overlook of Turquoise Lake along the north shore drive along County Road 9.

activities.name: Mountain View Fishing Site
activities.description: Mountain View Fishing Site is located on the Northeast shore of Twin Lakes. It offers access for fishing, SUP boarding and kayaks and has a great view of the lakes.

activities.name: Mount Columbia (Fourteener)
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: At 14,073 feet, Mount Columbia is the 35th highest peak in Colorado. It is located in the Collegiate Peaks Wilderness . There is currently no standard route delineated for climbing Mount Columbia and climbers should avoid the loose scree slopes directly west of the peak. This area has seen many visitors and is…

activities.name: Mount Democrat (Fourteener)
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: ***Please stay on Forest Service land and respect private property. A closure is in effect by private landowners, which includes the peaks of Mt. Democrat, Mt. Lincoln and Mt. Bross.*** The two-mile trek to the summit of Mount Democrat (14,148 feet) begins at Kite Lake, fourteen miles…

activities.name: Mount Elbert (Fourteener)
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: Mount Elbert is Colorado's highest peak and the second highest peak in the lower 48 states with an elevation of 14,433 feet. There are two main routes to the summit, which are the South Mt. Elbert Trail and the North (Main) Mt. Elbert Trail, both being well trodden class one trails. These relatively easy…

activities.name: Mount Harvard (Fourteener)
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: At 14,420 feet, Mount Harvard is the third highest peak in Colorado and one of the many peaks in the Collegiate Peaks Wilderness . A companion peak to Mount Columbia , Mount Harvard is accessible from North Cottonwood Trail ,  Pine Creek Trail , Frenchman Creek Trail , 3 Elk Creek Trail  or Harvard…

activities.name: Mount Massive (Fourteener)
activities.description: Mount Massive, at 14,421 feet, it is the second highest peak in Colorado at just 12 feet behind its southern neighbor, Mt. Elbert. Its name comes from its elongated shape: it has five summits, all above 14,000 feet, and a summit ridge over 3 miles long, resulting in more area above 14,000 feet than any other…

activities.name: Mount Sherman (Fourteener)
activities.description: Mount Sherman, is Colorado's 46th highest peak at 14,036 feet. This mountain, usually considered one of the easiest of Colorado's 54 Fourteeners, is an excellent climb for beginning mountaineers, but basic mountaineer rules still apply. It is a fast hike for a reasonably fit person since it is…

activities.name: Red Rooster Boating Site
activities.description: Located on the Northwest shore of Twin Lakes that offers allows access to the lake for SUP and kayak use and the Interlaken boat tours take off from this site. SUP and kayaks can be rented at this site, a fee is charged.

activities.name: Sayers Gulch Trailhead
activities.description: Sayers Gulch Trailhead accesses the Sayers Gulch Trail #1465, a 1.4-mile trail in the Collegiate Peaks Wilderness . The road to the trailhead is rough with a significant stream crossing at the beginning. High-clearence 4-wheel drive recomended.  The Collegiate Peaks Wilderness was established in 1980 to…

activities.name: Shimmering Point Observation Site
activities.description: This a day use pull out area that has views of Turquoise Lake.

activities.name: Valley View Observation Site
activities.description: This a day use pull out area that has views of Turquoise Lake.

activities.name: Bottomless Pit Observation Site
activities.description: The overlook provides a view of a deep cirque and interesting rock formations of the Bottomless Pit. The site is accessed from the Pikes Peak Highway. The trail to the bottom of the pit begins on Barr Trail 1 mile west of Barr Camp.

activities.name: Cascade Observation Site
activities.description: Located on Pikes Peak Highway. There are view finders available to overlook the town of Cascade.

activities.name: Dikeside Boating Site
activities.description: This boating site is located on Rampart Reservoir. Swimming, wading and all body contact with the water in the reservoir is prohibited. Coast guard approved life jackets are required for every person onboard every watercraft, including kayaks, paddleboards and canoes.

activities.name: Homestake Fishing Site
activities.description: This site has interpretive exhibits, fishing access, and affords a good view of Pikes Peak. Swimming, wading and all body contact with the water in the reservoir is prohibited. Coast guard approved life jackets are required for every person onboard every watercraft, including kayaks, paddleboards and canoes.

activities.name: Nichols Reservoir
activities.description: The trail to Nichols Reservoir begins at the Dikeside Boatramp parking lot. It is a 0.8 mile hike down to Nichols Reservoir and back up. Swimming, wading, and all body contact with the water in the reservoir is prohibited. All watercraft on Nichols Reservoir is prohibited.

activities.name: Baldwin Lake
activities.description: Baldwin Lake is a small alpine lake located to the west of Mount Antero (14,269 ft). The lake is home to native Cutthroat trout. A valid Colorado fishing license is required. Remember to check fishing regulations before fishing at any body of water. For stocking reports and more information on regulations or…

activities.name: Chalk Lake Fishing Site
activities.description: Chalk Lake Fishing Site is located next to the Chalk Lake Campground and is a great family fishing spot with rainbow, brook and brown trout. Chalk Lake is a small lake, about 12 acres in size and is regularly stocked for fishing.  Motorized boats are not allowed on the lake.

activities.name: Cottonwood Lake Boating Site
activities.description: Cottonwood Lake is an 40 acre, man-made lake that serves as one of the water sources for the town of Buena Vista, Colorado. A large picnic area with handicapped accessible fishing docks is located on the east side of the lake.A gravel boat ramp is located on the west side of the lake. Non-motorized boats and…

activities.name: Ghost House Historic Site
activities.description: The Ghost House is located near the historic mining and railroading town of St. Elmo. Built by Mr. Ghost, an early mining and real estate developer in the 1880's. The house is of wood construction using local timber and sided with metal. The most interesting feature of the house is the use of flattened food cans…

activities.name: Mount Antero (Fourteener)
activities.description: Mount Antero is one of the Colorado Fourtneers with an elevation of  14,276ft. The peak was named for Chief Antero of the Uintah band of Ute tribe.  Mount Antero boasts the highest gem field in the lower 48. Many unpatented mining claims are scattered over the peak. Rockhounding, prospecting…

activities.name: Sugar Creek Upper Trailhead
activities.description: The Noddles Trail (#677) is one of the many OHV (Off Highway Vehicle) trails in the Rampart Range Recreation Area. These trails are designated for vehicles 50" or less in width.

activities.name: Sugar Creek Lower Trailhead
activities.description: The Noddles Trail (#677) and Log Jumper Trail (#677.A) are one of the many OHV (Off Highway Vehicle) trails in the Rampart Range Recreation Area. These trails are designated for vehicles 50" or less in width.

activities.name: Buffalo Trailhead
activities.description: This trailhead provides access to the Green Mountain Trail (#722), the Colorado Trail (#1776) and other nearby trail segments.

activities.name: Burning Bear West Trailhead
activities.description: The Burning Bear West trailhead provides access to the Burning Bear Trail (#601). The trail is approximately 6 miles, going from Hall Valley (Park County Route 60) to Geneva Creek.

activities.name: Burning Bear East Trailhead
activities.description: The Burning Bear Trail (#601) has two trail heads: east and west. The east end of the trail begins approximately 0.2 mile west of the parking area for the Abyss/Burning Bear East Trailhead (9,620'). From the small gate at the beginning of the trail, the trail leads northwest in an open meadow…

activities.name: Cabin Ridge Trailhead
activities.description: Situated along the Rampart Range Road south of Highway 67, the Cabin Ridge Trailhead is located southeast of the Cabin Ridge Picnic Area. Cabin Ridge Trailhead accesses Cabin Ridge Trail (#675).

activities.name: Dutch Fred Trailhead
activities.description: The Dutch Fred Trailhead is located south of Indian Creek along the Rampart Range Road. The Dutch Fred Trail (#679) enters into a a system of 115 miles of motorcycle and ATV trails in the Rampart Range Recreation Area. In order to use any vehicle on National Forest lands, it must either have a valid state…

activities.name: Flat Rocks Overlook Observation Site
activities.description: The Flat Rocks Overlook Observation Site provides views to the east towards Perry Park and Castle Rock.

activities.name: Flat Rocks Trailhead
activities.description: The Flat Rocks Trailhead is located south of Indian Creek along the Rampart Range Road. The Flatrock Trail (#674) trail enters into a system of 115 miles of motorcycle and ATV trails in the Rampart Range area.

activities.name: Garber Creek Trailhead
activities.description: The Garber Creek Trailhead is located south of Indian Creek. The Garber Creek Trail (#686) enters into a system of 115 miles of motorcycle and ATV trails in the Rampart Range Recreation Area.

activities.name: Gashouse Trailhead
activities.description: Located approximately an hour drive southwest of Denver, Colorado, at an elevation of 7,400', Gashouse Trailhead is located within the Buffalo Creek Recreation Area and provides access to the Gashouse (#726) and Muache Trail (#759).

activities.name: Indian Creek Trailhead
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: The Indian Creek Trailhead is near the gate to the right of the parking area and accesses the Indian Creek Trail (#800) and Ringtail Trail (#699). After the trailhead, the trail splits and both directions will complete the loop. Taking the left fork, the trail goes uphill and contains the majority of…

activities.name: Kenosha Pass Railroad Station Documentary Site
activities.description: Welcome to Kenosha Pass Railroad Station Documentary Site! The written plaque to the sign:  "Denver, South Park, and Pacific Railroad Brochure   The brochure and exhibits on this site were made…

activities.name: Kenosha Wildlife Viewing Observation Site
activities.description: The Kenosha Wildlife Viewing Observation Site is accessed by a short trail and provides views of the Kenosha Pass area including a wetland area.

activities.name: Shinglemill Trailhead
activities.description: The Shinglemill Trailhead provides access to the Shinglemill Trail (#725), Morrison Creek Trail (#724) and the Colorado Trail (#1776) Segment 3. This trailhead is in an active timber sale area.

activities.name: A. Ash Creek River Access
activities.description: The entrance to Ash Creek River Access is a short dirt road to a small turn around. The ramp to the river is sand and not designed for trailers and RV's. There is limited parking. No facilities.

activities.name: B. Cayuse River Access
activities.description: Cayuse River Access consists of a large sand and gravel river bar and a gravel walking trail to the river. There is one picnic table and a public telephone in the parking area. This area is for day use only, no overnight parking or camping. Rock hounds can explore the tailings, and nature lovers can observe wood…

activities.name: C. Skeahan Bar River Access
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: Originally named Virginia Bar, this was a mining claim worked by John Skeahan and Joe Davidson in the late 1800s. They were hard rock miners who dug deep tunnels in search of gold. This popular river access features a large wooded area with picnic tables and dispersed campsites. There is a gravel road to the…

activities.name: D. Gottville River Access
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: In 1857, William Gott built a home and post office at the mouth of Lumgrey and Empire Creeks, establishing the town of Gottville to serve the growing population of miners in the area.  At one time, some 3,000 people lived in this narrow canyon. President Herbert Hoover came here to fish for steelhead in…

activities.name: E. Brown Bear River Access
activities.description: This popular fishing access has a gravel road to the water's edge. Dispersed camping is allowed and there is some shade. There is an information bulletin board but no facilities. This nice river access was built with slide materials in cooperation with CalTrans and is a launching spot for kayaks and rafts. Across…

activities.name: F. Blue Heron River Access
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: A graded gravel ramp to the water's edge provides access at this popular fishing spot. Limited shade is available for a few dispersed campers. RV's and trailers are an easy fit. There are no facilities but an information board has current info on campfire permits and fire restrictions for the area. The Sarah…

activities.name: G. Rocky Point River Access
activities.description: Rocky Point River Access has a gravel ramp to the water's edge but parking here is limited. There is an information board with current info on campfire permits and fire restrictions for the area. Interpretive signs are installed and the Forest Service provides a portable toilet here in summer months. *As of August…

activities.name: H. Sluice Box River Access
activities.description: This is a popular put-in area for the class 3 float to Seattle Creek River Access. In addition, this area of the river is known for great bird watching and the spotting of occasional river otters. There is a river map and an interpretive panel at this access along with an information board providing current info on…

activities.name: I. Portuguese Creek River Access
activities.description: Because of the unique geology of this area, early miners in the mid to late 1800's used a method called hydraulic mining. Large monitors (metal nozzles) were connected to hoses and pipes that gradually got smaller and smaller. This created great pressure that, when aimed at the hillside, washed tons of dirt, rock…

activities.name: K. Seattle Creek River Access
activities.description: A graded gravel ramp to the water's edge is provided at Seattle Creek River Access. There is limited parking at this access.

activities.name: L. China Point River Access
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: The access road to China Point is not recommended for trailers or RV's. The steep one mile access road is partially paved to a large cobble bar. There is ample parking on the bar but very limited dispersed camping here. This is a popular fishing area.

activities.name: M. Gordons Ferry River Access
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: Gordon's Ferry is a popular fishing access just a few miles east of Happy Camp. The road is mostly paved but has a section of improved gravel. The last 1/2 mile or so is steep, narrow and windy. It is not recommended for trailers or large RV's. There is limited parking and limited dispersed camping.

activities.name: N. Indian Creek River Access
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: Located in the town of Happy Camp where Indian Creek flows into the Klamath, this is the busiest, most popular launching point for floating the lower Klamath River. There is an information board, a restroom and large parking area. You can drive to the water's edge on gravel road. This area is designated Day Use…

activities.name: O. Chambers Flat River Access
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: Chambers Flat offers a graded sandy road to the water's edge. There is an information sign and parking area. This is a popular take-out for fishermen.

activities.name: P. Wingate Bar River Access
activities.description: Wingate Bar has a graded gravel road to the water's edge. There is an information sign and parking area. The Forest Service provides a portable toilet here in summer months. There is a limited area for dispersed camping.

activities.name: Q. Ferry Point River Access
activities.description: The 1/2 mile graded gravel road off Hwy 96 to the gravel bar will accommodate self-contained RV's for dispersed camping. There is a gravel road to the water's edge, permanent toilets and ample parking at Ferry Point River Access. In the 1850's this area was a thriving little town with a hotel, dance hall…

activities.name: R. Independence Rest Area /River Access
activities.description: Facilities at the Independence Rest Area are on Hwy 96 with a short, graded gravel road on the southwest side of the bridge to take you down to the river. There are tables, restrooms and an information board. While enjoying your stay, you can be entertained by the flock of at least 200 cliff swallows that claim the…

activities.name: S. Coon Creek River Access
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: Parking for Coon Creek River Access is on Hwy 96. There is a paved access road to the water's edge but no room for turn around or parking. The Forest Service provides a portable toilet here in summer months. A short hike up Ukonom Creek is the scenic Ukonom falls.

activities.name: U. Dillon Creek River Access
activities.description: Parking for Dillon Creek River Access is on Hwy 96 across the road from the Dillon Creek Campground.  Access the Klamath River by hiking down an undeveloped trail along the Dillon Creek.  The Dillon Creek Trail starts on the north side of Dillon Creek near the bridge, and continues several miles…

activities.name: W. Persido Bar River Access
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: Persido Bar (sometimes incorrectly called Persidio Bar) is a high-use, popular take-out for river floaters. There is a graded gravel road to the large cobble bar and a flat road to the water's edge. There is a permanent restroom and ample parking.

activities.name: X. Ti Bar River Access
activities.description: The road off Hwy 96 down to the cobble bar at Ti Bar will accommodate RV's. There is an information sign, permanent restroom, ample parking and shaded dispersed camping area. Large rigs should check for overhead clearance when parking under trees.

activities.name: Y. Rock Creek River Access
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: Parking for Rock Creek River Access is only on Hwy 96 and is limited. There is a 1/4 mile steep hiking trail to the river.

activities.name: Z. Stuarts Bar River Access
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: Downstream from the R. Lyle Davis bridge is a dirt road leading to a steep graded road to the river bar under the bridge. There is parking available. Due to steepness and very sharp switchback, this access is not recommended for vehicles towing jet boat trailers, etc.

activities.name: Zz. Green Riffle River Access/Mandatory Take Out
activities.description: You must exit the Klamath River here. This is the last legal take out before the Ishi Pishi Falls (class 6).  A 1/2 mile long graded road leads to the river bar with an unimproved road to the water's edge.

activities.name: Blue Hole River Access
activities.description: Approximately 1 mile east on Highway 2B01 from Somes Bar to a small turnout on the right. Hike down to the water.

activities.name: George Geary River Access
activities.description: This access to the Salmon River is designated Day Use Only, no overnight camping. It has a graded gravel ramp to a cobble bar for parking. Boats must be carried a short distance to the water. There is limited parking and some shade. There are 2 picnic tables and a vault toilet.

activities.name: Oak Bottom River Access
activities.description: Across the road from the Oak Bottom Campground this access is a graded gravel ramp to parking on a cobble bar. Boats must be carried a short distance to the water.

activities.name: Brannon Bar River Access
activities.description: There is limited parking here. Additional parking can be found across the road at Wooley Creek Trailhead. There is a graded gravel ramp to a cobble bar. Boats must be carried a short distance to the water. There is a bulletin board with information.

activities.name: Butler Creek River Access
activities.description: This access to the Salmon River is a graded gravel ramp down to bedrock. Boats must be carried a short distance across the bedrock to the water. Butler Creek has  a vault toilet, two picnic tables and bulletin boards.

activities.name: Cascade River Access
activities.description: Views overlooking the rapids on the Salmon River. Good spot to photograph rafters.  Hike 1/4 mile down to an overlook of the rapids. Hike down to the water.

activities.name: Bloomer Falls River Access
activities.description: East on county road 2B01 from Somes Bar approx 13 miles to a small turnout. Hike down to the water and an overlook of the rapids.

activities.name: Nordheimer Flat River Access
activities.description: The river access is a graded gravel road to a cobble bar. Nordheimer Campground is administered by the Six Rivers National Forest.

activities.name: Forks Rest Area
activities.description: Nice little picnic area overlooking the confluence of the North and South Forks of the Salmon River

activities.name: Saw Pit Flat River Access
activities.description: This access to the North Fork of the Salmon River is a short road to a cobble bar for parking. Boats must be carried a short distance to the water.

activities.name: Red Bank River Access
activities.description: Swimming, wading and water play off the gravel bar on the North Fork of the Salmon River.

activities.name: Jack Ass Creek River Access
activities.description: Access to the North Fork of the Salmon River, just west of Sawyers Bar.

activities.name: Methodist Creek River Access
activities.description: Access to the South Fork of the Salmon River at Methodist Bridge.

activities.name: Matthews Creek River Access
activities.description: This access on the South Fork of the Salmon River has a short road to a large parking area on the cobble bar. Boats must be carried a short distance to the water. This access is located adjacent to Matthews Creek Campground, a fee site. Do not park in campsites.

activities.name: Johnson Bar River Access
activities.description: Located on the Wild and Scenic Scott River this access is a graded road to a cobble river bar.

activities.name: Sugar Pine Gulch River Access
activities.description: Access point to the Wild and Scenic Scott River from County Rd. 7F01 (Scott River Road).

activities.name: Townsend Gulch River Access
activities.description: Entry to the Scott River here is a graded gravel ramp to the water's edge. There is limited parking. Schuler Gulch rapids is located downstream. Be sure to scout ahead!

activities.name: Gold Flat River Access
activities.description: Access to Scott River from Scott River Road.

activities.name: Thompkins Creek River Access
activities.description: Access to Wild and Scenic Scott River from Scott River Rd.

activities.name: Bridge Flat River Access
activities.description: A pullout and short trail to a large pool under a bridge over the Scott River. This is a put-in for a Class V section of the Scott River during spring run-off and a favorite swimming hole during the summer months.

activities.name: Canyon Creek River Access
activities.description: To reach Canyon Creek River Access, turn off Scott River Road on Canyon Creek Road. Cross the bridge and find the access area at .2 mile. This site consists of a small parking area with trail access to a put-in eddy at the base of a long rapids. There is a reliable gauge on the west pier of the bridge. READINGS OVER…

activities.name: Jones Beach Picnic and River Access
activities.description: Nice day use area with a small beach along the Scott River. Popular for swimming, water play and fishing. **Effective October 23 - no water or trash service is available for the winter season.**

activities.name: Peninsula Point Lighthouse
activities.description: New! Take a self-guided tour of our Lighthouses via the Hiawatha's OnCell App! Learn more here . Peninsula Point is a special place for a number of reasons. During the 1860's, the ports of Escanaba, Gladstone, Fayette and Nahma were teeming with ships hauling fish, lumber, iron ore and other products…

activities.name: Point Iroquois Lighthouse
activities.description: In 1975, The Point Iroquois Lighthouse was placed on the National Register of Historic Places. The Point Iroquois Lightstation stands high above the waters of Lake Superior at the entry to St. Mary's River. It served passing sailors by marking the narrow channel. The name Point Iroquois references a battle…

activities.name: Lake On Three
activities.description: This small lake provides fishermen and boaters with an opportunity to get away from it all and enjoy the outdoors. The Forest Service maintains a boat ramp for access to this good fishing lake.

activities.name: Tepee Lake
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: Tepee Lake is easily accessible and fairly large lake that provides boaters and fishermen the opportunity to enjoy the outdoors and relax

activities.name: Brule Lake
activities.description: Brule Lake located on the Michigan and Wisconsin border provides excellent fishing with a good variety. This has two boat ramps, one on the north end and one on the south end of the lake.  Also located next to Brule Lake is Stateline Picnic Area and Stateline/Treaty Tree Hiking Trail.

activities.name: Bass Lake
activities.description: Bass Lake is a small lake located just east of Hagerman Lake but don't let the size fool you. There is plenty of good fishing on this lake.

activities.name: Lake Andrusia Boat Site
activities.description: A concrete boat ramp provides access to the 1,500 acre Lake Andrusia. Lake Andrusia is connected by the Mississippi River to the Cass Lake chain of lakes. Walleye, northern pike, and yellow perch are found in this lake.

activities.description: Camp Rabideau National Historic Landmark represents the best preserved of the Civilian Conservation Corps camps in the nation. Part of Franklin D.
