activities.name: Shogren Dam Picnic Area
activities.description: Pack up your picnic basket and enjoy one of this favorite spaces on the Chippewa National Forest. Shogren Dam picnic area is located on the on Bowstring River in Chippewa National Forest near Wirt, MN.

activities.name: Big Lake Boating Area
activities.description: Big Lake offers great fishing for Bluegill, Bass, Northern Pike, Muskie and Walleye.

activities.name: Moose Lake Boating Area
activities.description: Moose Lake is known for producing 30-40 pound muskies. The lake also offers fishing for walleye, largemouth bass, crappies, and panfish.

activities.name: Reese Boat Landing
activities.description: A canoe trip from Reese Landing provides a vantage point for viewing bald ealges, osprey, herons, and various waterfowl.

activities.name: Richards Townsite Boating
activities.description: Head to Richards Townsite for a day on the water and enjoy a picnic!

activities.name: Norway Beach Swimming Area
activities.description: A sandy beach and a delineated swimming area makes for summer fun at the Norway Beach Recreation Area. It is surrounded by four campgrounds and a picnic area.

activities.name: Norway Beach Boat Access
activities.description: The Norway Beach Boat ramp is located in the Norway Beach Recreation Area, four miles east of Cass Lake on Highway 2. It is a double cement ramp with a dock giving visitors access to Cass Lake.

activities.name: Little Cut Foot Sioux Boat Area
activities.description: A concrete boat ramp provides access to the 660 acre Little Cut Foot Sioux Lake. The lake is east of MN Highway 46. Northern pike, walleye, cisco, perch and other panfish are found in this lake.

activities.name: Birches Boat Area
activities.description: A concrete boat ramp provides access to the 56,470 acre Lake Winnibigoshish. Lake Winnie is north of Minnesota State Highway 2. Birches boat site is on the eastern shore of the lake. Northern pike, walleye, cisco, bass and panfish are found in this lake.

activities.name: Mosomo Point Boat Area
activities.description: A concrete boat ramp provides access to the 2852 acre Cut Foot Sioux Lake. The lake is west of MN Highway 46. Northern pike, walleye, cisco, perch and other panfish are found in this lake. This is a very popular landing as it has double ramp with a dock in the middle. Parking for twenty vehicles is available. There is…

activities.name: East Seelye Bay Boat Area
activities.description: A concrete boat ramp on the north side of Cut Foot Sioux Lake provides access to the 2852 acre Cut Foot Sioux Lake and the 56,470 acre Lake Winnibigoshish. activities.name: Plughat Point Boat Area
activities.description: A concrete boat ramp provides access to the 56,470 acre Lake Winnibigoshish. Lake Winnie is north of Minnesota State Highway 2 and the boat landing is on the northeast shore of Winnie. Northern pike, walleye, cisco, perch and other panfish are found in this lake.

activities.name: Big Fork River Boat Area
activities.description: A carry-in access provides access to the Big Fork River. The site is adjacent to State Highway 6 and County Road 14. Northern pike, walleye and musky are found in the river.

activities.name: Little Jessie Lake Boat Area
activities.description: A concrete boat ramp provides access to the 637 acre Little Jessie Lake. Little Jessie Lake is south of Itasca County Highway 35, with the landing on the northwest shore. Northern pike, walleye, perch and other panfish are found in this lake.

activities.name: Big Too Much Lake Boat Area
activities.description: A concrete boat ramp provides access to the 284 acre Big Too Much Lake. Big Too Much Lake is just east of Minnesota Highway 6. Northern pike, bluegill, other panfish, and some walleye are found in this lake.

activities.name: Caribou Lake Boat Area
activities.description: A gravel boat ramp provides access to the 246 acre Caribou Lake. Caribou Lake is east of Minnesota State Highway 38. Lake trout and panfish are found in this lake.

activities.name: Clubhouse Lake Boat Area
activities.description: A concrete boat ramp provides access to the 210 acre Clubhouse Lake. Clubhouse Lake is north of Itasca County Highway 45. Northern pike, bass and panfish are found in this lake.

activities.name: North Star Lake Boat Area
activities.description: A concrete boat ramp provides access to the 1,059-acre North Star Lake.  North Star is west of Minnesota State Highway 38. Northern pike, bass and panfish are found in this lake.

activities.name: Spider Lake Boat Area
activities.description: A concrete boat ramp provides access to the 1,349 acre Spider Lake. Spider Lake is west of Itasca County Highway 49. Northern pike, perch and other panfish are found in this lake.

activities.name: Lake 13 Boat Area
activities.description: A concrete boat ramp provides access to the 470 acres of Lake 13. Lake 13 is three miles east of MN Highway 371. Bluegill, walleye, northern pike and other panfish are found in this lake.

activities.name: Moccasin Lake Boat Area
activities.description: A concrete boat ramp provides access to the 243 acre Moccasin Lake. Moccasin Lake is along the Woodtick Trail in the Chippewa NF. Northern pike, and panfish such as bluegills and crappies are found in this lake.

activities.name: South Pike Bay Boat Area
activities.description: A concrete boat ramp provides access to the 4,670 acres of Pike Bay. Pike Bay is adjacent to US Highway 2. Walleye, northern pike, crappie and other panfish are found in this lake.

activities.name: Diamond Lake Boat Area
activities.description: A concrete boat ramp provides access to the 77 acre Diamond Lake. Diamond Lake is just south of MN Highway 200. Rainbow trout (stocked by the MN DNR) and crappies are found in this lake.

activities.name: Long Lake Boat Area
activities.description: A concrete boat ramp provides access to the 926 acre Long Island Lake. Long Island Lake is just east of MN Highway 84. Northern pike, largemouth bass, and panfish such as bluegills, sunfish and perch are found in this lake.

activities.name: Pine Lake Boat Area
activities.description: A concrete ramp provides access to the 261 acres of Pine Lake. Pine Lake is two miles north of MN Highway 200. Northern pike, bass and bluegill are found in this lake.

activities.name: Three Island Lake Boat Area
activities.description: A concrete boat ramp provides access to the 288 acre Three Island Lake. Three Island Lake is just south of MN Highway 200. Northern pike, bass, and panfish such as bluegills, sunfish and perch are found in this lake.

activities.name: Hovde Lake Boat Area
activities.description: An earthen ramp, suitable for small boat trailers, provides access to the 131 acres of Hovde Lake. Hovde Lake is three miles south of MN Highway 200. Bass, walleye, and northern pike are found in this lake.

activities.name: Lower Sucker Lake Boat Area
activities.description: An earthen boat ramp access to the 585 acres of Lower Sucker Lake. Lower Sucker Lake is approximately 3.5 miles south of US Highway 2. Northern pike, walleye, crappie and other panfish are found in this lake.

activities.name: Portage Lake 13 Boat Area
activities.description: A concrete boat ramp provides access to the 1,539 acres of Portage Lake. Portage Lake is one mile south of US Highway 2. Walleye, northern pike, crappie and other panfish are found in this lake.

activities.description: Buck Park Cabin is located on Cuddy Mountain, in the Payette National Forest of central Idaho. activities.description: Boat Launch for Lost Valley Reservoir. Restroom and tables available for day use picnics.

activities.description: Overlooking Hells Canyon, this peak was once home to a fire lookout. A large wooden sign shares information about this site. Also, nearby was the old townsite of Helena with another sign describing the town, which was built near the Peacock mines to harvest copper.

activities.name: Lost Creek Riparian Area
activities.description: This site offers a wildlife viewing area, restroom and day use picnic area. Located in the trees it is a great place to stop for a short walk out on the viewing platforms to see birds and fish.

activities.description: Whisker Lake was designated as a wilderness on October 2, 1978. activities.name: Willow Creek Boating Site
activities.place: Arapaho & Roosevelt National Forests Pawnee NG
activities.description: Willow Creek Boating Site is located in the Arapaho National Recreation Area on the Willow Creek Reservoir. The boating site is open to non-trailered, non-motor boats. View a COTREX map here .

activities.name: Willow Creek Fishing Site
activities.place: Arapaho & Roosevelt National Forests Pawnee NG
activities.description: Minimally developed site on Willow Creek Reservoir with parking for about 10 vehicles. Site provides access for shoreline fishing and for launching non-motorized, non-trailered boats. Within  Arapaho National Recreation Area .

activities.name: Beaver Lake
activities.description: Beaver Lake is a 67-acre manmade lake dating from the days of railroad logging. activities.name: Greentree Reservoir
activities.description: Greentree Reservoir is a 33-acre manmade lake frequently visited by local fishermen. Both boat and limited bank fishing is possible. Facilities include a boat ramp and a small parking area. No camping or swimming is permitted. No fee is charged. Open year-round. State fishing laws and regulations apply.

activities.name: Gavin Forest Educational Tour
activities.description: The Gavin Forest Educational Tour is an 11-mile self-guided driving tour using interpretive signs to inform visitors about south Mississippi's beautiful pine forests and the practices used to maintain a healthy forest while providing for recreation, wildlife and other public benefits. activities.description: Ashe Lake Recreation Area was originally built to provide water for Ashe Nursery.  The 8-acre lake is shallow with the deepest area about 15 feet. Visitors may enjoy fishing for bass, bream and catfish. activities.name: Chewalla Lake
activities.description: Chewalla Lake Recreation Area’s name is from the Choctaw word "Chiho-la," meaning "supreme being." activities.name: Puskus Lake
activities.description: Puskus Lake Recreation Area is a fairly remote area for those who do not like big crowds and do not need modern conveniences. The visitor will discover a pleasant and quiet environment. activities.name: Lake Tillatoba
activities.description: Tillatoba Lake is a fairly remote area for those who do not like big crowds and do not need modern conveniences. activities.name: Choctaw Lake
activities.description: Choctaw Lake Recreation Area offers a range of outdoor opportunities such as camping, picnicking, swimming, boating, fishing, hiking and bicycling. Facilities include 20 campsites with utility hookups, 35 picnic sites, three picnic pavilions, a swimming area, disc golf course, two bath houses with showers…

activities.name: Big Meadows Reservoir Boating Site
activities.description: The Big Meadows Boating site is a 600 acre impoundment. It offers a small boat ramp, restroom, parking lot. Motorboats are allowed but must control excessive wakes. Ice fishing is possible in the winter which can be accessed via snowmobile or cross-country skis on Big Meadows Road.

activities.name: Columbine Interpretive
activities.description: This is a combination rest stop with no bathroom and interpretive site right on US Highway 160 about 10 miles west of South Fork, Colorado. The facility consists of a large parking area and interpretive signs about Columbines.

activities.name: Continental Reservoir Fishing Site
activities.description: This large irrigation impoundment is regularly stocked with catchable trout, but the water level fluctuates. It has a parking lot, a restroom, and a concrete boat ramp. Boats with motors are allowed as long as they travel wakeless. Camping is not allowed.

activities.name: Highway 149 Interpretive Site
activities.description: This is an Interpretive Site along the Silverthread Scenic Byway (State Hwy 149) Between Creede and Lake City Colorado. It overlooks the historical site of San Juan City and the scenic Upper Rio Grande River Valley. It is a large paved parking area with a sidewalk and interpretive signs describing the view.

activities.name: Hwy 149 Moose Interpretive Site
activities.description: This Moose Interpretive Site sits along the Silverthread Scenic Byway between Creede and Lake City Colorado. It consists of a paved pullout and parking lot overlooking good Moose habitat. There is an interpretive sign here talking about the Moose Reintroduction in the 1990's and the ecology of the animal itself.

activities.name: Love Lake Picnic Site

activities.name: Childers Creek Trailhead
activities.description: Childers Creek is a parking area for those to access the Hiwassee River and the John Muir Trail.

activities.name: Big Bend
activities.description: Big Bend offers plentiful parking for those who are looking to fish the Hiwassee River.

activities.name: Moses Turn
activities.description: Parking for fishing and trail access.

activities.name: Dudley Falls
activities.description: Swim area and fishing access.

activities.name: Little Therriault Lake
activities.description: The Little Therriault Lake campground is located 12.5 air miles from Fortine. The campground has 6 sites with tables and fire rings and able to accommodate up to a 32' rv. Amenities include potable water, vault toilets, food storage boxes and an undeveloped boat access (pack boats).

activities.name: Lowman Nature Ponds
activities.description: The Lowman Nature Ponds are a great place for the family to fish and close to State Highway 21 just north of Lowman, Idaho. Two ponds are stocked with trout by the Idaho Fish and Game. The ponds provide a restful place for fishing from shore and picnicking.  Boats are not allowed on the ponds.  A restroom is…

activities.name: Deadwood River Access Site
activities.description: The Deadwood River Access Site is across the road from Deadwood Campground, so amenities such as restrooms, parking and picnic tables are available.  The access site is a long concrete slab ideal for rafts and non-motorized boats, but may be a bit shallow for motorized boats, depending on the time of the year…

activities.name: Bender Creek Trailhead
activities.description: Bender Creek Trailhead - is a signed site with a restroom, loading/unloading ramp for ATVs, registration box and visitor information.  This is one of the trailheads in the Danskin OHV area.  The trailhead marks one of the major entrances to the #300 Trails of the Danskin Trail System.  I All trailheads…

activities.name: Longbow Boat Ramp
activities.description: Longbow Boat Ramp is located on Cave Run Lake , on the Cumberland District . Longbow Marina is located nearby. Cave Run Lake is nestled among the beautiful mountains of eastern Kentucky. Built for flood protection by the U.S. Army Corps of Engineers, this 8,270 lake provides flood protection to the lower Licking River…

activities.name: Cinder Hills Off Highway Vehicle Area
activities.description: The Cinder Hills is a scenic recreation area enjoyed by many off-highway vehicle enthusiasts. Its numerous volcanic cinder cones and craters surrounded by a ponderosa pine forest environment gives the area its unique value. Due to a growing interest in this area for off-highway vehicle recreation, additional…

activities.name: Copperas Creek Canoe Launch
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: Canoe launching area near Osborne Bend Trailhead on the Red River in the  Red River Gorge . 19.4 miles (31.22 km) of the Red River is designated a federal Wild and Scenic River. It is the only Wild and Scenic River in Kentucky. The Red River provides a great paddling experience for both beginners and…

activities.name: Scott Creek Marina
activities.description: Scott Creek Marina is a full-service facility that provides a restaurant, groceries, fuel and other provisions for Cave Run Lake boaters. Boat rentals include houseboats, fishing boats, pontoons and paddleboats.  The marina is privately operated under a special-use permit with the Forest Service…

activities.name: Longbow Marina
activities.description: Longbow Marina on Cave Run Lake  on Cumberland District is privately operated under an agreement with the Forest Service. Rental boats, camping and fishing supplies, fishing licenses, and detailed maps of the lake can be purchased at the marina. The marina is open year-round. Sidewalks to the…

activities.name: Holly Bay Marina
activities.description: Holly Bay Marina is a full-service facility located on Laurel River Lake  near Holly Bay Campground . Rental boats, camping and fishing supplies, fishing licenses, and maps of the lake are available for purchase at the marina. The marina is open year round and accessible for persons with disabilities. A…

activities.name: Panguitch Lake
activities.description: Panguitch Lake is situated at an elevation of 8,212 feet approximately 18 miles southwest of Panguitch, Utah.  The lake is the source of Panguitch Creek and is fed by three small inlet streams: Blue Springs Creek, Clear Creek, and Ipson Creek.  The lake is a popular fishing lake with rainbow, brook…

activities.name: Hiwassee River
activities.description: The Hiwassee River offers Class I-III rapids, and is a popular destination for fishing, kayaking, and tubing.  Local outfitters rent rafts and tubes, for a list of Outfitter and Guides, click HERE . Additional information or release scedules for other locations can be found here: www.tva.org/

activities.name: Mill Pond Historic Site
activities.description: The Mill Pond Historic Site is currently open. This site has a new picnic pavilion, renovated picnic site, and parking area. A new loop trail system with a footbridge over the canyon at the former dam site is available connecting the this site with the Mill Pond Flume Trail #520 and Mill Pond Campground . The new…

activities.name: Deer Creek Boat Ramp
activities.description: The Deer Creek Boat Ramp provides access to Anderson Ranch Reservoir. There is a restroom and a small dirt parking area big enough for about 15 vehicles.

activities.name: Pine Valley Reservoir
activities.description: Reservoir

activities.name: Enterprise Reservoir
activities.description: The Enterprise Reservoirs lies within a pinyon-juniper forest surrounded by large volcanic tuff rocks.  The reservoir is popular for fishing, boating, kayaking and canoeing, and wildlife viewing.  Nearby opportunities include OHV riding, hiking, biking, horseback riding, campground camping and dispersed…

activities.name: Eleven Mile Canyon Auto Tour
activities.description: Eleven Mile Canyon Auto Tour is managed by the USDA Forest Service to protect its rich natural resources and historic sites, and to provide public recreation. The focal point along this nine-mile route is the South Platte River which begins high above Fairplay and flows in a southeasternly direction across South…

activities.name: Tobacco Plains Picnic Area
activities.description: The Tobacco Plains picnic area is located approximately 9 miles northwest of Eureka on Lake Koocanusa. Amenities include a vault toilet and boat ramp that accommodates smaller boats.

activities.name: Gateway Boat Camp
activities.description: The Gateway Boat Camp is located approximately 8.5 air miles from Eureka, and 0.18 miles from the Canadian Border. The campground has 5 sites with tables and fire rings. Amenities include a pit toilet and hitching rack. The most popular way to gain access to this campground is by boat (boat must be…

activities.name: Jane's Reservoir Boating Site
activities.description: A gravel launch ramp provides access for small boats to this lovely little reservoir.  There is a campground adjacent. There is no water provided for drinking.

activities.name: Blue Lake Boating Site
activities.description: Blue Lake, located in the southern Warner Mountains, is a favorite for local anglers and is stocked by the California Department of Fish and Wildlife.  A boat dock is available in summer only. There is a campground, trails and paved parking for boat trailers.

activities.name: Big Sage Boating Site
activities.description: Big Sage Reservoir and campground are surrounded by juniper woodland and sagebrush. The reservoir is several thousand acres and the campground lies on the shore near the boat ramp.

activities.name: Duncan North Boating Site
activities.description: This is a primitive area without facilities.  The boat ramp is gravel and dirt.  There is a small parking lot and turn around.  This area is recommended for cartop boats and small power boats.

activities.name: Duncan South Boating Site
activities.description: This is a primitive area without facilities.  The boat ramp is gravel and dirt.  There is parking for boat trailers and room for turn around.  Small motor boats and car top boats can launch from Duncan South.

activities.name: Logan Slough Boating Site
activities.description: Volcanic cliffs define a portion of the shoreline at Logan Slough.  While motors are allowed, car top boats or non-motorized boats are most appropriate for this small body of water.

activities.name: Green Springs Boating Site
activities.description: Easily accessed from Davis Creek, this very large reservoir sits among tall pines and juniper.  A very nice boat ramp allows entry to the lake but no other facilities are available.

activities.name: Reservoir F Boating Site
activities.description: The boat ramp at Reservoir F is hard packed gravel and can accommodate motorized and non-motorized boats.

activities.name: Reservoir C Boating Site
activities.description: The boat ramp at Reservoir C is paved and can accommodate motorized and non-motorized boats.  There is ample parking for boat trailers.

activities.name: Cave Lake Boating Site
activities.description: There is a gravel boat ramp and parking area on the south side of the lake as well as a bathroom facility. Non-motorized boats only. The road into this area is extremely rough, 4-wheel drive is advised.

activities.name: Lily Lake Boating Site
activities.description: Lily Lake Boating Site Lily Lake is a picturesque mountain lake ideal for kayaks, canoes and stand-up paddle boards. No boat motors of any kind are allowed on Lily Lake. This is a "day use" only facility. No overnight camping is permitted. Cave Lake is just a short distance up the road for campers.

activities.name: Middle Piney Lake Boating Site
activities.description: The Middle Piney Lake Boating Site offers access to great fishing on Middle Piney Lake. Nestled under Wyoming Peak in the heart of the Wyoming Range this boat site has a gravel boat ramp, bathroom facilities, and plenty of parking for cars, trucks and trailers. There is a small non-fee campground at the site, but no…

activities.name: Togwotee Overlook Interpretive Site
activities.description: The Togwotee Overlook Interpretative Site is located one and a half miles East of Togwotee Lodge on Highway 26/287. This site offers striking views of the Teton Range to the West. An interpretative site gives information about the area’s cultural history. A restroom is also available at this site.

activities.name: Afton Rest Area Interpretive Site
activities.description: Forest Service information, including a district map and summer or winter travel opportunities is provided on a kiosk. The Town of Afton offers a trailer dump station and garbage dumpsters at this location as well.

activities.name: Bridge Boating Site
activities.description: The Bridge Day Use Area is located just 2 miles up the Greys River Road out of the town of Alpine. The area hosts 5 picnic sites and a vault toilet, but no garbage service, and is a popular take-out for kayaks and smaller inflatables along the Greys River. The take-out has a very small turning radius making this site…

activities.name: Cottonwood Boating Site
activities.description: The Cottonwood Boating Area is located next to the Cottonwood Lake Campground and rests along Cottonwood Lake.  Day use facilities at this site inclue a small hardened, native material, boat launch for non-motorized boats, a picnic area that is first-come, first-served, and a group picnic site that is by…

activities.name: Greys River Road Interpretive Site
activities.description: About a mile upriver from the parking area at the Forest boundary is a pull-through kiosk with motorized use and dispersed camping info, plus river ecology and history.

activities.name: Murphy Lake Boating Site
activities.description: Just 2 miles up Murphy Creek Road on the south side is a small day-use area with limited parking, a vault toilet, a primitive boat launch for small craft and picnic tables.

activities.name: Salt River Pass Interpretive Site
activities.description: A series of Forest Service and area history and ecology signs at a large paved pullout off Hwy 89 provides visitors with a fuller understanding of public lands as they take in the majestic views across the divide between Kemmerer and Greys River Ranger Districts.

activities.name: Smiths Fork Road Interpretive Site
activities.description: A kiosk just above the highway 89 junction on the Smiths Fork Road provides information about motorized use and dispersed camping.

activities.name: Granite Hot Springs Pool
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: The Granite Hot Springs Pool is located at the end of the Granite Creek Road, south of Jackson, Wyoming off of Highway 189. It is a developed, concrete hot spring pool situated alongside Granite Creek amongst huge spruce, fir and pine forest. A fee is charged for soaking in the springs, and it can be accessed during…

activities.name: Gros Ventre Geological Site
activities.description: The Gros Ventre Geological Site is a large paved parking area directly below the famous Gros Ventre Landslide which formed Slide Lake, and is the direct access to the Gros Ventre Geological Trail #4073. It is located directly off the Gros Ventre Road out of the town of Kelly. Several large informational panels provide…

activities.name: Elk Creek Guard Station Interpretive Site
activities.description: The Elk Creek Guard Station Interpretive Site is a historic Forest Service Guard Station from the early days of the Bridger National Forest.

activities.name: Billy Wells Dude Ranch Interpretive Site
activities.description: "Gros Ventre Lodge" This interpretive site describes one of the oldest dude ranches in Wyoming, located in the Upper Green River Valley.

activities.name: Green River Lake Boating Site
activities.description: This a undeveloped boating site, suitable for small water craft. The access road is dirt and is steep. Parking is available onsite for day use only, overnight parking is accommodated in the adjacent stock trailhead parking area. A double vault toilet is available in the parking area.

activities.name: Green River Tie Hack Interpretive Site
activities.description: "First Tie Drive on the Green River" This interpretive panel describes the flourishing Tie business on the Green River to support the first transcontinental railroad in neighboring states.

activities.name: Half Moon Lake Boating Site
activities.description: Half Moon Boat Site has a paved ramp, which has been extended with rip rap for time periods of low water. A short dock is available along the ramp at this site. A Gravel parking lot is available for overnight and day use, with two single vault toilets.

activities.name: Lower Fremont Lake Boating Site
activities.description: The Lower Fremont Boat Site is located on the southern shores of Fremont Lake. Two paved ramps are available, depending on water levels access may be limited. A Dock is provided for your convenience. The gravel parking area is available for both day and overnight use. There is a double vault toilet onsite, please pack…

activities.name: New Fork Lake Boating Site
activities.description: This boat ramp provides boating access to New Fork Lake. It is located on the western shore, between all three campgrounds on New Fork Lake. The ramp is paved, with a dock for your convenience and a vault toilet.

activities.name: Skyline Drive Overlook Interpretive Site
activities.description: With an interpretive panel helping you name the peaks of the Bridger Wilderness, this paved pull-off is a must see destination. Access to this site is via a paved road, just a short 15 miles from Pinedale.

activities.name: Upper Fremont Lake Boating Site
activities.description: This boat ramp is located within the Fremont Lake Campground. Onsite you will find a fishing pier, a dock, double vault toilet, and drinking water. Due to limited space, parking is limited to campground guests. Day users and other overnight users may park at the Lower Fremont Boat Site.

activities.name: Willow Lake Boating Site
activities.description: This is an undeveloped boat ramp, it is a combination of both pavement and rock. No dock is available and a single vault toilet is onsite. Day Use and Overnight parking is available above the boating site.

activities.name: Aspen Flat
activities.description: This oasis of lush greenery is welcome respite from the dry ponderosa pine forest surroundings. The ground below the quaking aspen foliage is blanketed with grasses and blooming wildflowers in season. Trees are similar in bole height and diameter because wildfire swept the area in 1958 and consumed most above-ground…

activities.name: Cabin Lake Viewing Blind
activities.description: Two 8' x 12' covered shelters, approximately 300' apart on a north-south line, permit silent human observers to spy upon thirsty animals. Each blind has a small concrete basin that puddles water piped nearby water collection aprons and storage tanks. Veiled wall openings allow viewing and photography from…

activities.name: Crane Prairie Reservoir
activities.description: This is one of central Oregon's premier wildlife viewing sites because it attracts so many nesting and/or migrating birds. The relatively shallow reservoir was originally dammed to store irrigation water managed by the Central Oregon Irrigation District. Most access to the shoreline is at recreation sites. Go to…

activities.name: Davis Lake
activities.description: This is one of the most productive wildlife areas in central Oregon. Add a superb view of Cascade peaks at no charge and you have a truly special place to visit. The lake's water level may fluctuate significantly from year to year with a corresponding reduction in animal habitat. Davis Lake is one of the most…

activities.name: Hosmer Lake
activities.description: The lake is a hidden jewel of green and blue surrounded by dark green forest. Thickets of bulrush wands hide the most secretive wildlife and fish. At the north end, water drains into a porous rim of lava. The best way to experience this lake is by canoe, but a shoreline hike will still produce wondrous sights and…

activities.name: Metolius River
activities.description: This roadside route begins where glass-clear water surges from the dry ground at Metolius Spring, and continues north to Bridge 99. Special places along the way include the Camp Sherman Fish Viewing Platform, Metolius Research Natural Area, and Wizard Falls Fish Hatchery (phone 541-595-6611). A coalition of government…

activities.name: Wickiup Reservoir
activities.description: This is one of central Oregon's best wildlife viewing sites because it attracts such a variety of nesting and/or migrating birds. The relatively shallow reservoir was dammed to store irrigation water that is managed by the North Unit Irrigation District. The water level often lowers dramatically by October. The…

activities.name: Walton Lake
activities.description: This lake is a blue sparkling jewel hidden within mostly old growth ponderosa pine forest. A small dam impounds spring-fed water that seeps from surrounding sloped meadows. Quaking aspen and tall willows add habitat diversity to make this place especially attractive to wildlife and humans alike. A dirt trail, not…

activities.name: Rimrock Springs Wildlife Management Area
activities.description: A small dam traps spring-fed water to create this wetland oasis in an otherwise parched land. From the parking lot, take the 0.5-mile paved level trail to an uncovered observation deck. For a different perspective and route back to the parking lot, hike the not-so-level 0.9-mile dirt trail that loops south past a…

activities.name: Sand Spring
activities.description: An unseen spring trickles water to the fenced pond. Sagebrush shrubland borders the pond, and dry forest surrounds the shrubland. It's a long way to the next drink, so this site draws wildlife like a magnet.       Caution:  Cinder-surfaced roads leading here are often washboard-rippled and…

activities.name: Russian River
activities.description: The Russian River Campground Road will undergo construction to redo a one-mile stretch of the road surface and reinforce portions of the hillside along the bank of the Kenai River. The road and campground will be closed to the public during the construction. During the closure, all vehicle and pedestrian access will…

activities.name: Portage Glacier & Portage Valley
activities.description: Welcome to the land of ice & rock... Portage Valley is a 14 mile isthmus that connects the Kenai Peninsula to mainland Alaska. Portage Glacier once extended the entire length of the valley. The glacial remnants seen today are Explorer, Middle, Byron, Burns, and Shakespeare glaciers. While still massive in size…

activities.name: Big Creek River Access Boating Site
activities.description: River access site located on the Wild and Scenic North Fork of the Flathead River.  This river access site has designated parking area, vault toilet, and a concrete ramp.

activities.name: Bear Creek River Access Boating Site
activities.description: River access site located on the Wild and Scenic Middle Fork of the Flathead River.  This river access site is located adjacent to Bear Creek Trailhead and has designated parking area, vault toilet, and a boat slide for accessing the river.

activities.name: Red Mountain Fire Lookout
activities.description: Red Mountain Lookout unfortunately burned in the Fairview Fire of September 2022.  Red Mountain (elev. 4,573ft) is located in the southern part of the San Bernardino National Forest southeast of Hemet. Besides having the best views of the southern San Jacinto Mountains. Red Mountain also overlooks parts of…

activities.name: Black Mountain Fire Lookout
activities.description: Black Mountain Fire Lookout (elev. 7,772 ft.) is located in the San Jacinto Mountains. Access is via either a 1-mile round-trip hike on a dirt road from Boulder Basin Campground, or the longer Black Mountain Trail. The tower is staffed by volunteers and is usually open between 9:00 am and 5:00 pm during fire season…

activities.name: Tahquitz Peak Fire Lookout
activities.description: The hike up to this lookout tower through the San Jacinto Wilderness offers some of the most beautiful vistas in Southern California, including the Salton Sea to the southeast. The origin of Tahquitz's name is derived from the Cahuilla god Tahquish, who believe the peak to be the god's home. At an elevation of 8,846…

activities.name: Big Bear Dam Keepers House
activities.description: In October of 1890, the historic Dam Keeper’s House was built using hand-cut granite blocks from the same quarry that provided the stones for the first dam. For nearly a century, this was home to over a dozen dam keepers and their families. The famed Bill Knickerbocker and his family were early residents between…

activities.name: Antelope Flat Reservoir
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: Antelope Flat Reservoir is located on the south side of the Maury Mountains, is encompassed by the Ochoco National Forest and is a great getaway from the more crowded campgrounds in the state. It is an irrigation impoundment that is situated near the headwaters of Bear Creek, a tributary of the Crooked River, and is…

activities.name: Crescent Lake
activities.description: Crescent Lake is a popular recreation lake in a setting of wooded shorelines, sandy beaches and brilliant blue-green water. In addition to fishing for kokanee, lake trout, rainbow and brown trout, people come to this lake for sailing, swimming, water skiing windsurfing and camping. Lake trout are caught here in the 5…

activities.name: Cultus Lake
activities.description: Cultus Lake is a popular lake in a beautiful setting and is wellknown for producing trophy size lake trout (mackinaw). Many lake trout in the 10 lb. range are taken each season. A 17.5 lb. lake trout was weighed in at Cultus Lake Resort in 1996. In addition stocked rainbow including larger holdovers and an occasional…

activities.name: East Lake
activities.description: East Lake is a popular recreation lake in a setting of wooded shorelines, sandy beaches and brilliant blue-green water. The lake is one of two exceptional trout lakes nestled in the caldera of the Newberry National Volcanic Monument, the largest ice-age volcano in Oregon. In addition to fishing for kokanee, rainbow…

activities.name: Elk Lake
activities.description: Elk Lake has a picturesque setting, with the Three Sisters toweringover the north end of the lake and Mt. Bachelor dominating the eastern horizon. It is not a rich lake but is so transparent you can see the bottom clearly from any location on the surface. The kokanee are commonly 7 to 10 inches in length, not large…

activities.name: North Twin Lake
activities.description: The lake was formed about 20,000 years ago when rising magma-encountered groundwater resulting in violent steam explosions. The resulting explosions formed a broad shallow crater, which later filled with water. North Twin has 112 surface acres, average depth of 40’, and a maximum depth of 60 feet. The pine…

activities.name: Little Lava Lake
activities.description: Little Lava's biggest claim to fame may not be it’s fishing, but that it is the source of the mighty Deschutes River. The state record brook trout, weighing at 9 pounds, 6 ounces, was taken from the river below the lake in 1980. Little Lava Lake is a small, forest lake about a half-mile south of…

activities.name: Little Cultus Lake
activities.description: Little Cultus Lake is a 175-acre lake nestled in the pines a few miles off the Cascade Lakes Highway. With good fishing for rainbow and brook trout, Little Cultus is a great place to take the family for a quiet weekend of fishing and camping. Rainbow trout angling, 11-17 inches are the primary fishery. Brook trout…

activities.name: Lava Lake
activities.description: Lava Lake was formed as a result of lava flows creating a dam along its east shoreline. Lava Lake is relatively old as evidenced by the extrusive vegetation occurring in the shallow areas. Rushes, waterlilies and other emergent plants are especially evident on the west and northern perimeter. Another indication of the…

activities.name: Ochoco Reservoir
activities.description: A dam constructed on Ochoco Creek after World War I formed the reservoir for irrigation and flood control which allowed for recreation activities. Mill Creek and Ochoco Creek input to the reservoir and the output is Ochoco Creek.  Except for the campground and dam, almost all of the reservoir's shoreline is…

activities.name: Odell Lake
activities.description: Diamond Peak stands as a sentinel over Odell Lake, one of the blue giants of the Deschutes National Forest. This large lake is 3562 acres, 6 miles long and 1 1/2 miles wide, and reaches a depth of 282 ft. The average depth is 132 ft. which makes it ideal habitat for lake trout (Mackinaw) and bull trout. Rainbow trout…

activities.name: Paulina Lake
activities.description: Paulina Lake is located within the caldera of Newberry Volcano, about 25 miles south of Bend, Oregon. The Newberry Caldera encircles the basins of Paulina and East lakes and it is nearly 5 miles (8 km) in diameter. This collapsed caldera  is the result of more than 500,000 years of volcanic activity. Neither lake…

activities.name: Prineville Reservoir
activities.description: The Arthur R. Bowman Dam is an earthen fill structure on the Crooked River that has created the Prineville Reservoir. The main input streams are the Crooked River and Bear Creek with lesser streams (Sanford Creek, Deer Creek, Alkali Creek, Antelope Creek, and Owl Creek) and the output stream is the Crooked River. The…

activities.name: South Twin Lake
activities.description: The lake was formed about 20,000 years ago when rising magma-encountered groundwater resulting in violent steam explosions. The resulting explosions formed a broad shallow crater, which later filled with water. The lake covers an area of 99 acres with average depth of 33 feet with a maximum depth of 58 feet. South…

activities.name: Three Creek Lake
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: The lake is located in a glacial cirque, below Tam McArthur Rim, which was probably last occupied by glacial ice about 13,000 years ago during the Canyon Creek advance of the Cabot Creek glaciation. The outlet stream from the lake flows northward and is joined by two other streams to form Three Creek. The lake is…

activities.name: Todd Lake
activities.description: The lake was formerly called Lost Lake due to the difficulty in finding it. Citizens of Bend asked to have the name changed because of confusion with other Lost Lakes. The lake was renamed Todd Lake in 1922 to commemorate Uncle John Y. Todd, an early settler of central Oregon. The lake is located in a glacial cirque…

activities.name: Crooked River
activities.description: The Crooked River experience is one of rugged, dramatic canyons, enthusiastic fish, Wild and Scenic tracts, bald eagles and kingfishers, and cool, spring-fed headwaters. The river maintains a wild feeling, even in the most popular sections. Well-known locally for dependable fishing and routine rattlesnake sightings…

activities.name: Fall River
activities.description: Fall River is a beautiful spring-fed stream flowing through rolling pine forest. It is open to fly fishing only . Clear and cold, it springs full-blown from the ground about 2 miles northwest of Pringle Falls and winds it’s way northeast to join the Deschutes River. Fall River is an outstanding contributor of…

activities.name: Courthouse Vista
activities.description: Courthouse Vista is the trailhead for Courthouse Butte Loop , Bell Rock, and Bell Rock Pathway trails. These trails access Llama , Templeton , HT and Big Park trails in the immediate area. In addition there are scenic vistas of Courthouse Butte, Bell Rock, Castle Rock, Lee and Munds mountains and the Red Rock Cliffs…

activities.name: Forest Road 25
activities.description: This road provides some of the best scenery on the Forest running north-south from near the Cowlitz Valley Ranger Station in Randle to Forest Road 90 at the east end of Swift Reservoir. From Forest Road 25, Forest Road 26 and Forest Road 99 lead to sites on the east side of Mount St. Helens. Found along this road…

activities.name: Big Meadow Lake
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: Big Meadow Lake is 4.1-acre shallow lake perfect for family recreating and wildlife viewing.   This Lake is found in a beautiful setting of forested mountains. Visitors come for fishing, camping, hiking, birding and canoeing. It has a primitive boat launch and fishing pier. It is a shallow lake with a…

activities.name: Bead Lake
activities.description: This is a relatively large lake in a mountainous setting of well timbered hills. The water is of extreme clarity. The west side of the lake is predominately residential. Often used for fishing, hiking, canoeing, and boating. There is a boat launch on the lake Forest Service Road #3200412 and access to a 6.8 Mile…

activities.name: Boundary Lake
activities.description: Boundary Lake is a 9.5-acre lake 10 miles north of Metaline Falls, WA. The lake is adjacent to the US/Canada boundary line. It is set in low wooded hills.

activities.name: Browns Lake
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: Browns Lake is a 88.1 acre, 23' deep, high elevation lake that is in a setting of forested mountains. This non-motorized lake is known for its fly fishing and camping. There is a primitive boat launch on the south end. While at the lake you can enjoy fishing, camping, canoeing…

activities.name: Bunchgrass Lake
activities.description: This lake was originally maintained by a log dam and it contained native Cutthroat. The dam is now gone and very little water remains. It is now mostly marsh and wetlands. This is a 640 acre nature resource area. No motorized access allowed near this area.

activities.name: Carl's Lake
activities.description: Carl's Lake is a 20.2-acre secluded, shallow lake located 5.5 miles from Ione, Washington.

activities.name: Conger Lake
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: Conger Lake is a 5.3 acre, 10' deep lake built for fish propagation and irrigation. Leisurely kayaking is great here.

activities.name: Cooks Lake
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: Cooks Lake is a small, shallow 11.1 acre lake which lies northeast of Usk, WA. It offers rainbow trout fishing opportunities. During dry summer months the lake level can significantly recede. There is easy access for launching a small boat. Several campsites and a concrete vault toilet are located at the southeast end…

activities.name: Crater Lake
activities.description: Crater Lake lies on a geological fault on the west side of Sullivan Mountain. This is one of the few alpine lakes on the Colville National Forest. activities.name: Crescent Lake

activities.description: Bolar Mountain Recreation Area at Lake Moomaw offers visitors a fun getaway on Lake Moomaw. activities.description: Coles Point at Lake Moomaw boasts picnic shelters, two fishing docks, two boat ramps and a swimming beach. activities.description: Beautiful and secluded, Fish Lake is the largest and deepest lake in the Rogue-Umpqua Divide Wilderness . Fishing is popular, with the lake containing rainbow trout and brook trout. Swimming is also a popular activity, particularly to cool off after the hike in! Fish Lake is only accessible via hike, with numerous…

activities.name: Wapiti Wayside
activities.description: If you want to learn about grizzly bears, other wildlife, and receive general visitor information, visit the Wapiti Wayside. The Wayside is located on U S Highway 14/16/20 about 30 miles west of Cody and about 20 miles from the East Entrance to Yellowstone National Park.

activities.name: Lake Owen Recreation Area
activities.description: Lake Owen Recreation Area is located on the 1,323 acre Lake Owen that has crystal clear water, excellent fishing and swimming. There is a swim beach and shelter/chalet at the northern end of the lake on Forest Road 213 (Lake Owen Drive). There is access to the North Country Trail from this recreation area as well…

activities.name: Island River Canoe Route
activities.description: This eight mile stream route provides a different experience than the standard lake-to-lake canoeing.  A narrow twisting stream brings wildlife on shore close to your canoe.  The current flows from east to west, so that is the preferred direction of travel.  Island River does briefly enter the BWCAW, so…

activities.name: Twin Lakes Canoe Route
activities.description: Six lakes linked by four portages make up the Twin Lakes Canoe Route.  There are five backcounty campsites along the way, and lots of opportunities for fishing and wildlife viewing.   For a printable pdf file with a map and additional information, click here.

activities.name: Timber-Frear Canoe Route
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: The Timber-Frear Canoe Route (named for Timber and Frear Lakes) links seven lakes with seven portages.  There are 11 backcountry campsites accessible by canoe and one rustic campground accessible by car on the route.  There are an additional 4 rustic campgrounds nearby.  See the Timber-Frear Area in the…

activities.name: Lower Lake Mary
activities.description: Sometimes it's a lake. Sometimes it's not. Lower Lake Mary, the smaller of Flagstaff's twin lakes, has a tendency to disappear during the long dry spells that periodically hit this area. When the lake has water in it, which actually is much of the time, its banks are usually lined with anglers trying to…

activities.name: Marshall Lake
activities.description: Marshall Lake is a small marshy body of water that's generally full of coots and other waterfowl splashing, flapping, and cooting around. It is such valuable wildlife habitat that it is managed in partnership by Ducks Unlimited and the Arizona Game and Fish Department. During wet cycles the lake has enough water…

activities.name: Fossil Creek
activities.description: Fossil Creek There are ten recreation sites and trails along Fossil Creek Wild and Scenic River. Each site features deep pools and beautiful scenery. activities.name: Cape Horn Overlook

activities.description: Cape Horn Overlook is accessed via Cape Horn Trail #4418 . Follow Cape Horn Trail for a scenic 2 mile hike to Cape Horn Overlook. activities.name: Astoria Boating Site
activities.description: Astoria Boat Ramp is the first boat ramp south of Hoback Junction that is available for boat launching. It is generally a quieter boat ramp and provides a great option for putting in on the…

activities.name: Po-shu-oinge' Interpretive Site (minor)
activities.description: Po-shu-oinge' interpretive site is near the turn off to Abiquiu.  A short trail takes the visitor above the valley to look over a cultural site where the outline of a Pueblo Community can be seen.  An artist conception of the original site helps the visitor to visualize the area as it might have been.

activities.name: Vista Grande Overlook Observation Site

activities.description: This fishing site provides access to the San Antonio River in San Diego Canyon. A restroom is available at this site. activities.description: The River's Bend Fishing Site offers parking and access to the Lower Jemez River. Located on NM HWY 4 approximately seven miles south of Jemez Springs. Open seasonally, typically from May to October.

activities.description: East Table boat ramp is a quiet boat ramp that receives less use than West Table. No trailers are allowed at East Table boat ramp. activities.description: Trailhead for the Knapp-Loon Creek Trail #4036 in the Cape Horn area.

activities.name: Taco Hole Kayak Access

activities.description: The Taco Hole Kayak Access is a day use only area which begins at a turnout along the highway in the north end of the Snake River Canyon. activities.name: Brasstown Falls
activities.place: Francis Marion and Sumter National Forests
activities.description: Tucked away in the southern edge of Sumter National Forest, Brasstown Falls tumbles for 120 feet in three consecutive and equally dramatic drops. activities.description: New Canyon Reservoir is a small 6 acre reservoir located in the New Canyon area.  The Department of Wildlife Resources of Utah (DWR) stocks this reservoir with Rainbow Trout and Wiper Bass (hybrid between a Striped Bass and White Bass).

activities.name: Upper Six-Mile Pond
activities.description: The Upper Six-Mile Pond is a small 3.8 acre pond located next to Upper Six-Mile Ponds Campground .  The Department of Wildlife Resources of Utah (DWR) stocks this pond with Rainbow Trout.  Access from the town of Sterling on Forest Road #50047 is rough, 4 wheel drive recommended, no trailers.  Even…

activities.name: Loggers Reservoir
activities.description: Loggers Reservoir is a small 11 acre reservoir located off Skyline Drive.  The Department of Wildlife Resources of Utah (DWR) stocks this reservoir with Rainbow Trout.

activities.name: Snow Lake
activities.description: Snow Lake is a small 7.7 acre Llke located off Skyline Drive.  The Department of Wildlife Resources of Utah (DWR) stocks this lake with Rainbow Trout.

activities.name: Fairview Lakes
activities.description: These are 103 and 20.8 acre lakes located 1.2 miles south of Beaver Dam Reservoir .  They are on private land and the Department of Wildlife Resources of Utah (DWR) stocks these lakes with Rainbow Trout.

activities.name: Miller Flat Reservoir
activities.description: Miller Flat Reservoir is a 162 acre reservoir located on Millers Flat Road #50014.  The Department of Wildlife Resources of Utah (DWR) stocks this reservoir with Rainbow Trout.

activities.name: Ferron Reservoir
activities.description: Is a 76.3 acre reservoir located by Ferron Reservoir Campground .  The Department of Wildlife Resources of Utah (DWR) stocks this reservoir with Cutthroat, Brook, and Rainbow Trout.

activities.name: Chestatee Overlook
activities.description: The Chestatee Overlook gives you a wide-angle view of the watershed that gives rise to the Chestatee River. In the foreground lies the Dockery Lake Campground and in the distance is the Blood Mountain Wilderness. This is a great photo opportunity.

activities.name: Dark Lake
activities.description: Dark Lake has a concrete boat ramp suitable for most boats, a picnic site, and an accessible fishing deck. The lake offers a wide variety of fish including walleye, northern pike and panfish. Nearby lakes include: Knuckey Lake , Clear Lake and Camp Four Lake .  Downloadable map and information.

activities.name: Knuckey Lake
activities.description: Knuckey Lake is a small lake with a gravel boat ramp with a small turnaround area. The ramp is a little steep and is suitable for small boats and canoes. This lake contains northern pike, largemouth bass and panfish. Nearby lakes include: Dark Lake , Clear Lake , and Camp Four Lake .  Downloadable map and…

activities.name: Clear Lake
activities.description: Clear Lake is a small lake with a carry-down access off the county road. It is suitable for canoes and small boats. The lake contains crappies, northern pike and bass. Nearby lakes include: Dark Lake , Knuckey Lake , and Camp Four Lake .  Downloadable map and information.

activities.name: Camp Four Lake
activities.description: Camp Four Lake is a small lake with a carry-in access that is roughly ¼ mile from the parking area. There are 2 back country campsites on this lake. Nearby lakes include: Dark Lake , Knuckey Lake and Clear Lake .

activities.name: Little Rice Lake
activities.description: Little Rice Lake is a small lake with a carry-down lake access, boardwalk and floating bog. The lake offers wild rice gathering, wildlife viewing and waterfowl hunting.   Downloadable map and information.

activities.name: Bingham Boat Launch
activities.description: Bingham Boat Launch is a small, day use only launch at the south end of the Hills Creek Reservoir.  Please note that this ramp requires higher water levels to be accessible by boats. Note that the nearby Packard boat launch is usually accessible year round.

activities.description: El Capitan Cave is the longest mapped cave in Alaska. Cavers mapped over two miles of passage from the main entrance. activities.description: A 30-minute floatplane ride from Juneau, Pack Creek is located about 40 miles south of Juneau in the northeast corner of Admiralty Island. Its important to remember that all users must operate their off-highway vehicle with a valid California Green Sticker, and helmet. All users: Please stay on designated…

activities.name: Hume Lake Fishing Pier (north)
activities.description: The Hume Lake fishing pier north, is located near the Lakeshore ranger station and Hume Lake Campground. It offers a small pier on the lake, and offers scenic views of the forest and Kings Canyon. Leave no trace principals apply here. Please pack out all fishing line, and leave the area better than you found it.

activities.name: Marble Mountain View
activities.description: This turn-out gives views of the impressive metamorphosed limestone vein, also known as marble! View the contrast between the unpolished marble and the rocky mountain slopes that surround it while the Kings River carves the canyon below.

activities.name: Hume Lake Fishing Pier (south)
activities.description: Hume Lake Fishing Pier South offers a relaxing setting to fish from. The small pier is situated along the 2.5 mile Hume Lake trail and offers view of the lake, the dam, and nearby Kings Canyon mountains.

activities.name: Junction View
activities.description: Junction View is the most popular turnout along Hwy 180.  A breathtaking view of the Western Sierra, a bird-eyes view at the junction of two forks of the Kings River and glimpse into Kings Canyon. The turnout is on the westbound lane (leaving the canyon).

activities.name: McGee Overlook
activities.description: From this overlook you can see where the McGee Fire in1955, and the Rough Fire from 2015. These fires burned though this drainage and changed the landscape.

activities.name: Millwood OHV Staging Area
activities.description: Millwood is a developed OHV staging area with a few campsites, vault toilets, steel fire ring and tables. Millwood area provides access to various out & back routes and loop routes that can challenge OHV drivers and riders. Goodmill OHV route is one of the most popular, is an intermediate route with creek crossing and…

activities.name: Woodward OHV Staging Area
activities.description: Woodward is an undeveloped staging area with in facilities and located ¼ mile south of Montecito Sequoia Resort on the General’s Highway. In the summer this trailhead provides access to Woodward (FS 14S18) ,Starlight (14S14), and many other roads.

activities.name: Sandy Flat Put-in/take-out Boating Site
activities.description: Launch area.

activities.name: Cyrus Canyon OHV Park
activities.description: Cyrus Canyon OHV Park is located northeast of Lake Isabella at an elevation of 2,600 ft. This motorcross loop trail is a great opportunity for family outings OHV riding or even an organized event. It is open for use by ATVs, Quads, and motorcycles. activities.name: Delonegha River Access Boating Site
activities.description: Delonegha Day use/River Access site is ideal for a day trip to the Kern River. Available for picnicking, and fishing. It also is a raft put-in and take-out for rafters on the Kern River.

activities.name: Democrat Raft Take-out Boating Site
activities.description: No camping; Day use between sunrise and sunset daily.

activities.name: Hanning Flat Dispersed Area
activities.description: Dispersed Camping on the shore of Lake Isabella. No trash receptacles available (Pack In-Pack Out). ALL Upper Kern Dispersed Camping sites, under restrictions - No Camping or Campfires are allowed within 25 feet of the water’s edge. Dispersed Camping Rules, Regulations, and Tips

activities.name: Johnsondale Bridge River Access Boating Site
activities.description: This site can be utilized for white water boating access, picnicking, and hiking. At about 19 miles north of Kernville via Mountain Highway 99, this site offers a great river hiking trail and boating access. The Kern River Trail (33E30) offers a great day hike with seasonal fishing access.

activities.name: Launch 19 Boating Site
activities.description: Boat and raft launch site between the Main Dam and the Auxiliary Dam on the shore of Lake Isabella. No fishing, or diving from the courtesy dock.

activities.name: Miracle Hot Springs Day Use Area
activities.description: This is a Forest Service managed day use area.  It is located 42 miles northeast of Bakersfield and 8 miles southwest of Lake Isabella along the old Kern Canyon Road and the lower Kern River. There is no potable water available. The elevation is 2,300 ft.  There is a boat launch for…

activities.name: Lake Isabella
activities.description: The Isabella reservoir offers fishing, boating, water sports, camping, and picnicking. Close proximity to Los Angeles and Bakersfield makes this lake a popular year round vacation spot for southern Californians. activities.name: Buck Rock Lookout
activities.description: Located in the Sequoia National Forest, Buck Rock Lookout sits perched atop a granite dome and offers a breathtaking view of the Great Western Divide and other spectacular high mountain peaks of the Sierra Nevada Mountains.  Access to the top is via a series of stair flights (consisting of 172 steps) suspended…

activities.name: Converse Basin Grove
activities.description: Converse Basin Grove gives us a glimpse of a time when Manifest Destiny was the slogan of the day. The axe was king, and engineering feats in the mountains included lumber mills, water flumes, steam locomotives, and unrivalled will power. This grove is the largest contiguous grove in the world and contains Boole Tree…

activities.name: Cherry Gap OHV Staging Area
activities.description: Cherry Gap is an undeveloped staging area with dispersed camping nearby. Remember when dispersed camping to pack out what you pack in and follow leave no trace methods. Also check fire restrictions for the local area.

activities.name: Hume Lake
activities.description: Hume Lake is an 87-acre lake formed by a unique multiple arch dam, constructed in 1908. Built to support a large, commercial logging operation, the lake supplied water to the longest lumber flume transporting logs to the Central Valley. Today the lake area is a destination where visitors can enjoy fishing…

activities.name: Boole Tree
activities.description: The Boole Tree is the 6th largest Giant sequoia tree in the world, and the largest known Sequoia on Forest Service lands. The tree was named around 1895 by A.H. Sweeny, a Fresno doctor, after Franklin A. Boole, a supervisor of the logging operation that is thought to have spared the tree's life due to…

activities.name: Indian Basin Grove
activities.description: Indian Basin Grove is a mid size grove of 448 acres with the popular Princess Campground and Indian Basin interpretive trail within its boundaries. Before the Forest Service acquired the grove in the 1930s the area was privately owned. Between 1901 and 1907 the Sanger Lumber Company removed all the mature trees…

activities.name: Thumb Butte (Climbing)
activities.description: Seasonal Closure: Thumb Butte is closed to climbing from February 1 to July 15 yearly to protect nesting sites for peregrine falcons.  Thank you for your cooperation in allowing the peregines to be undisturbed during the courtship and breeding season. Slight Changes to Closure Area Starts in 2015 The closed area…

activities.name: Forks River Access and Boat Ramp
activities.description: Launch your boat or enjoy the fishing, swimming, and sunbathing opportunities at this Smith River access. Restroom facilities available at boat-trailer parking lot.

activities.name: Musselshell Meadows
activities.description: Only 30 minutes southeast of the town of Pierce in north central Idaho, visitors will find Musselshell Meadows.  Home to beautiful and rare wildlife, dense forests, eye catching scenery, and interpretation explaining the significance of the area.  OHV trail riding, hiking, fishing, hunting, scenic driving…

activities.name: Dry Wash Reservoir
activities.description: Is a 6.9 arce reservoir located about 12 miles from Blanding, UT up Causeway Road #095. The Department of Wildlife Resources of Utah (DWR) stocks this reservoir with Rainbow Trout.

activities.description: Buckeye Reservoir is a 109 acre reservoir located on the east side of the La Sal Mountains in Colorado and is situated in a valley of mature Ponderosa Pines at 7,600 feet. It is a favorite fishing and camping spot. activities.name: Medicine Lake
activities.description: Medicine Lake is a small lake located 350 yards off Pack Creek-La Sal Pass Road #073 on Medicine Lake Road #238.  Occasionally during the wet seasons, there is a second small lake here.  The Department of Wildlife Resources of Utah (DWR) stocks this reservoir with Rainbow Trout.

activities.name: Oowah Lake
activities.description: Oowah Lake is a small 2.9 acre lake that sits at 8800 feet in the La Sal Mountains. There is a day use area, a reservable cabin for up to 4 people, and 19 campground sites some of which are reservable on www.Recreation.gov . activities.description: This extreme road starts off Homestake Road #703 and ends at Holy Cross City historic site. This is one of the more difficult and popular roads in the state. Consult a 4-wheel drive guidebook for a detailed description of this route and recommended vehicle specifications. Stock vehicles should not attempt this one.

activities.name: McAllister Gulch Road TH #708
activities.description: McAllister Gulch Road #708 begins at Camp Hale and ends at Shrine Pass Road #709. This is a rough 4WD road that requires a high-clearance 4WD vehicle. It does provide excellent views near the top of both Resolution Mountain and Hornsilver Mountain.

activities.name: Harralson Trailhead

activities.name: Aldrich Lakes Rim #2251
activities.description: The Aldrich Lakes Rim Trail runs east-west from FS251 to FS252. The east end of the trial is rocky and rutted, and requires technical skills to traverse safely. It is not recommended for beginners.

activities.name: Spring Creek Boat Ramp
activities.description: Boat launching dirt ramp at Spring Creek Lake.

activities.name: East Rim Viewpoint
activities.description: The East Rim Viewpoint overlooks North Canyon and the Saddle Mountain Wilderness. activities.name: Marble Viewpoint
activities.description: Marble Viewpoint offers a spectacular, panoramic view of House Rock Valley, Vermilion Cliffs, Marble Canyon, North Canyon and Saddle Mountain Wilderness. Here is cool, summer camping, with excellent opportunity to view such wildlife as deer, fox, turkey, squirrel, grouse, hawks, eagles and a number of songbird species.

activities.description: From the parking area you do a short walk on the Bill Hall Trail on the Forest Service land before entering into the National Park. activities.name: Stone Hill Climbing Area
activities.basis: described by the Forest Service
activities.description: Along the Koocanusa Reservoir is the Stone Hill Climbing Area.  Stone Hill is a unique area for climbers of all levels.  The area offers a good range of easy to moderate climbs for the intermediate…

activities.description: This scenic byway is located along the Cache la Poudre River, Colorado's only wild and scenic river! You can find more information on the Colorado Department of Transportation website .

activities.description: Stageyard Trailhead provides access to six OHV trails that are open to vehicles 62-inch in width or less. activities.name: Riley Hill Trailhead
activities.description: Riley Hill Trailhead offers extensive access to a wide variety of trails from just south of Roubaix Lake Recreation Area to north of Pactola Reservoir. activities.description: The Camp 5 Motorized Trailhead is the most popular gateway to over 10 miles of rock-crawling, 4x4, and OHV routes in the Deadwood area. activities.name: Spearfish Quarry Trailhead
activities.description: The Forest Service designed the Spearfish Quarry Trailhead for beginners to practice their motorized riding skills. The former gravel pit near the parking area is open to cross-country travel and there are four short trails accessible from the trailhead.  Access the trailhead from Spearfish via Interstate 90…

activities.name: Piedmont Trailhead
activities.description: The Piedmont Trailhead is on the east side of the most popular system of trails in the Northern Hills. The trails west of Piedmont wind through Ponderosa Pine forests, meander through large meadows, and climb to some of the most spectacular vistas in the Black Hills. activities.description: Set amid the sagebrush and pine is this small 260 acre wetland.  From spring through fall, the marsh is a stopover for many migratory species.  The marshes and bulrushes support mallards, northern pintails, American wigeons, cinnamon teal and gadwalls.  Each spring Canada geese use the…

Fossenvue Trail is a gravel path descends through forest to an open area beside the lake with a gravel beach and panoramic views. Please be aware that the last portion of the trail can be quite steep. Reimagining Caywood…
